title: User-facing UI: how users read and manage their memories post-extension
description:
GAP RAISED BY TC 2026-08-03. There is currently NO way for a user to browse or manage their memories. Filing P0 because it is submission-blocking for the audit: a catalog package that installs and shows the user nothing is a weak submission.

STATE OF PLAY, verified:
- The browser extension owned the entire UI (marinara-extender.js, 4420 lines, ~101 references to LANES/panel/addElement). It is DEAD — extensions were removed in Engine 2.3.4 and TC standing ruling is not to revive it.
- The capability package we just built is SERVER-ONLY. Its manifest declares entrypoints { agents, server } and no client. It brokers memory into the prompt and contributes no interface.
- The sidecar serves only /setup, /loader.js, /marinara-extender.js, /rewrite-assistant.js and /api/config. /setup is install guidance, not a data browser. "Marinara Extender.htm" at the repo root is a static document from May, not a live surface.
- So today the only access to memory data is raw HTTP against the sidecar API.

WHAT THE DATA LAYER ALREADY OFFERS (so this is a view problem, not a plumbing problem): /api/entries (GET list by scope/lane/status, POST create, GET/:id full content, PATCH, delete, restore), /api/bookmarks, /api/arcs, /api/beats, /api/identity + aliases + relink, /api/deleted, /api/memory-block, plus the new /api/prompt-accepted and the sph8 receipts.

PRECEDENT — long-term-memory does exactly what we would need to do, and its source is published: entrypoints { agents, server, client: "client.js" }, contributions { agentDetail: { agentIds }, slots: ["chat-settings"] }. Its client is REAL REACT TSX in the app (MemoryVault, ReviewQueue, SourcesWorkspace, ChatSettings, LtmWorkspace), NOT the sandboxed Worker that Personal Extensions get. So a package client entrypoint is full app-level UI and is the supported path.

THREE OPTIONS:
A. PACKAGE CLIENT ENTRYPOINT — chat-settings slot + agentDetail, mirroring LTM. Best in-context UX, matches the precedent an auditor already knows, and it is what makes the catalog listing meaningful. Cost: a real client bundle (LTM ships a 561KB client.js), must match their capability client API, and it is the part most exposed to change under audit.
B. SIDECAR-SERVED STANDALONE UI at 127.0.0.1:3001 — a page the user opens in a tab. Cheapest by far: the data API already exists, it is entirely ours, it needs nobody approval, and it keeps working when the package is not installed or the Engine is a different version.
C. BOTH, split by job: package UI for the in-context question ("what does this character remember, and why did it recall that"), sidecar UI for heavy management (browse, edit, merge, import, identity/alias repair).

RECOMMENDATION: B FIRST, THEN A, ARRIVING AT C.
- B is days not weeks, unblocks users immediately, and cannot be invalidated by an audit outcome.
- A is required for the submission to be worth installing, but building it BEFORE the audit relationship exists risks rework against an API we have never had reviewed.
- The old extension panel is the design spec for both — the port starts from a working reference, not a blank page.

THE DIFFERENTIATOR TO BUILD INTO WHICHEVER LANDS FIRST: sph8 receipts. "Why did it not remember X" answered on screen — selected entries with the reason each was pulled (own_match / thread_label / thread_sibling / recency_rider / cold_recall) and REJECTED candidates with why (resolved / superseded / unplayed / budget_exhausted). No other memory system in this ecosystem shows that, and it converts our hardest support question into a screen the user can read themselves.
notes:
UX CORRECTION FROM TC 2026-08-03, commit 11b8e9e. "Why this recall" was wrong as a top-level tab.

THE DIAGNOSIS TC PUT HIS FINGER ON: the tab was global but the data behind it is PER-TURN, so opening it while looking at a character had nothing to answer. The mismatch was structural, not cosmetic — I had modelled the feature around the artefact (a receipt) instead of around the question (does this memory get used).

THE FIX: each memory carries its own Why? button reporting that memory latest verdict across recent turns — injected with the reason it was pulled, held back with the reason it lost, or not considered at all. Reasons render in PLAIN LANGUAGE, not identifiers: "recency_rider" reads as "no topical match — rode in on recency because budget remained", "budget_exhausted" as "ranked, but the scope token budget was already full". The vocabulary stays closed underneath (so it is still countable) while the surface is readable.

Verdicts are indexed once at load from the 8 most recent receipts, newest first, so an older turn can never overwrite a fresher verdict for the same entry.

The per-turn view SURVIVES, reached from Recent recall in the sidebar where a turn genuinely is the subject, now with an explicit back button. Tab bar removed.

TC also confirmed the overall look and responsiveness are good, so the visual direction holds — this was a structure problem only.

LESSON WORTH KEEPING FOR THE PACKAGE PANEL LATER: model the surface around the question the user is holding, not around the shape of the artefact that answers it. The receipt is an implementation detail; "why did she forget that" is the product.

GATES: tsc clean, build clean, vitest 388 passed / 2 skipped.

title: Audit readiness: what exactly is being audited, and against which install shape
description:
FORCING FUNCTION: TC confirmed (2026-08-02, from SpicyMarinara direct) that we are ALREADY ON THE LIST TO BE AUDITED, and the package must be current for Engine v2.4.0. Deadline is external and not ours to set, so this is P0 ahead of any further design work.

THREE QUESTIONS THAT CHANGE WHAT WE BUILD. All three are for Mari, not for the codebase — I cannot answer them by reading source.

Q1 — DOES APPROVAL GRANT EXECUTION, OR ONLY DISTRIBUTION?
This is the load-bearing one. A capability package declares execution: pipeline | feature | host. 'pipeline' runs an LLM PROMPT and executes no package code. 'feature' and 'host' require an ENGINE-SIDE consumer that hard-codes the agent — proven: long-term-memory's feature agent functions only because packages/server/src/services/generation/long-term-memory-runtime.ts looks up its service key by literal string, and that file lives in the Engine, not the package.
So: when a third-party package is approved, does Mari also add the Engine-side consumer for its key? If YES, we can run real code during a turn and the whole capture path reopens (including apmt, and the string-compare tripwire TC specified, which was proven SOUND before being dropped for lack of an execution path). If NO, an approved package still cannot execute during a turn, and it is a UI/routes/storage surface only.

Q2 — MAY AN AUDITED PACKAGE TALK TO A LOCAL SIDECAR?
Our architecture is: package = thin broker, sidecar = the memory brain, over HTTP to 127.0.0.1:3001. A security audit may reject a package that makes outbound calls, even to loopback. If loopback IPC is disallowed, the package must either embed the memory logic (which drags private sidecar internals into an AGPL public repo — a licensing and IP decision, not a technical one) or the whole broker design is wrong. Ask BEFORE building, not at review.

Q3 — WHAT ARTIFACT IS ACTUALLY BEING AUDITED, AND WHEN?
Is the thing on the list the EXISTING browser-extension-era Marinara Extender, or a new capability package we have yet to write? That decides port-vs-patch and it decides scope. Also: what is the submission mechanism Mari expects — a PR against Marinara-Agents staging with manifest + reproducible artifact per its CONTRIBUTING.md (draft PR, catalog check, CodeRabbit, owner approval), or something else she described? And what is the timeline.

UNTIL Q1 AND Q2 ARE ANSWERED, do not start the package build. Q1 decides whether it is a capture path or a UI shell; Q2 decides whether the sidecar can stay private and separate. Building before either is answered risks a full rewrite at audit.
notes:
THE AUDITABLE UNIT — answered 2026-08-03. RECOMMENDATION: THE PACKAGE ALONE. Sidecar is a named companion dependency, not part of the submission.

PRECEDENT CHECK (all shipped, all approved, permissions read from live manifests):
- conversation-calls: ["agent-runtime","chat-read","chat-write","network","routes","storage","ui"]
- hierarchical-maps:  ["agent-runtime","chat-read","chat-write","network","prompt-context","routes","storage","ui"]
So "network" is not novel and not exotic — it is already granted to two first-party packages.
- haptic: ["agent-runtime","chat-read","prompt-context","storage","ui"] — NOTE: NO network. The Engine makes the Intiface call, not the package. So haptic is a LOCAL-COMPANION-DEPENDENCY precedent ("Requires Intiface Central running locally", stated in its manifest description), NOT a package-network precedent. Both halves of our shape have precedent; they just live in different packages. Do not cite haptic as a network precedent — a reviewer will check.

WHY THE WEBHOOK LOCALHOST BLOCK DOES NOT TRANSFER. Mari is right that it is the sorest spot, but the control exists for a threat we are not:
- A webhook tool is CONFIG DATA — imported, shared, unreviewed — that makes the Engine fetch an arbitrary URL. Blocking private/loopback addresses is textbook SSRF defence because the input is untrusted. v2.4.0 hardened this further: imported webhooks arrive disabled with hidden chat context stripped.
- A capability package is AUDITED CODE running UNSANDBOXED IN-PROCESS with fs, net, the Engine node_modules symlinked in, and DB access via persistence. Blocking its loopback calls would be theatre: it can open a socket directly regardless. The AUDIT is the control — that is the whole design (approval-gated, not isolation-gated, unlike Server Personal Extensions which get Seatbelt/Bubblewrap).
- Same codebase ships network to packages while blocking it for webhooks. That is a deliberate distinction by TRUST CLASS, not an inconsistency, and it is the argument to make if challenged.

THE OBJECTION THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN FATAL IS ALREADY VOID. The real risk was never the socket; it was "this package depends on code I cannot read." VERIFIED 2026-08-03: github.com/TCLowe1982/Marinara-Extender is PUBLIC, licensed AGPL-3.0, actively pushed. A reviewer can read the entire memory brain, under the same licence as their own repos. That is strictly stronger than haptic, whose dependency (Intiface Central) is third-party and outside the reviewer control entirely.
(Working note: this project has been described internally as a "private" sidecar. Against the registry it is public. The no-copy rule from the LTM teardown was followed regardless and remains correct practice, but the audit calculus should be run against PUBLIC, because that is what the reviewer will see.)

MITIGATIONS THAT MAKE IT CHEAP TO APPROVE — build these in from the start, not at review:
1. Declare "network" honestly. Never obscure egress.
2. EGRESS MUST BE CONFIG-ONLY. The base URL comes from user configuration and nothing else — never from chat content, model output, lorebook text, or any model-influenced field. This is the actual SSRF question a reviewer will ask, and the answer has to be structural, not a promise.
3. Loopback by default; remote (Tailscale) only on explicit user configuration.
4. No inbound listener in the package. It calls out; it never accepts.
5. DEGRADE GRACEFULLY when the sidecar is absent — the haptic pattern. A missing companion must never break a chat.
6. Keep the package small enough to read in one sitting. Audit cost is reviewer time; a thin obvious package clears, a sprawling one stalls.
7. Name the companion in the manifest description with its public repo URL, exactly as haptic names Intiface.

THE FORK TO DECIDE BEFORE BUILDING: does installing from the catalog give a WORKING feature or an inert shell until the user separately installs a Node service?
(a) Accept the two-step install and document it — haptic already does precisely this and was approved. RECOMMENDED.
(b) Bundle the sidecar into the package and run it in-process. Technically possible (packages are unsandboxed, node_modules symlinked) but it couples lifecycles, bloats the audit surface, and forfeits standalone/remote sidecar deployments. NOT recommended.

AMENDMENT TO "apmt IS THE ONLY ASK": there are now TWO Engine asks and apmt is the junior one.
1. An Engine-side getCapabilityService("marinara-extender:...") consumer. Without it our code never executes per-turn at all (Q1). This is a PR against the Engine repo, not against Marinara-Agents, and approval of our package does not imply it.
2. apmt payload fields, which only matter once (1) exists.
Neither is needed for the audit, because the package job is now DISTRIBUTION SHELL. But if in-engine capture is ever wanted, (1) strictly precedes (2) and should not be filed out of order.

title: Verify capture path against Engine v2.4.0 (poller smoke test)
description:
Engine v2.4.0 shipped 2026-08-01, 882 commits ahead of our checkout. The sidecar poller is the live capture path and must be proven against it BEFORE any architecture work.

Static check already done: lastMessageAt and activeSwipeIndex both still present in packages/server/src/routes/chats.routes.ts at v2.4.0. Engine at 127.0.0.1:7860 answers GET /api/chats with 200.

MUST PROVE END TO END:
- GET /chats returns chats carrying lastMessageAt
- GET /chats/:id/messages?limit=N returns NEWEST N ascending (the documented v2.3.x behavior in poller.ts)
- messages still carry their own characterId (group-scene speaker attribution)
- activeSwipeIndex / swipeCount still present and still change on the SAME message id for a regeneration
- auth path unchanged (v2.4.0 tightened proxy-forwarded Docker auth; confirm no new 401 on the loopback path)

Capture path is the store's pulse. Verification is cheap; silent drift is not.
close_reason:
VERIFIED GREEN against Engine v2.4.0 (running engine reports version 2.4.0, commit c82291d6c032 — exact match for the v2.4.0 tag). Exercised through the sidecar's own dist/engine-client.js, not hand-rolled curl, so drift would surface where the poller hits it.

CONTRACT HOLDS — every field the poller depends on:
- GET /chats -> 94 chats; 93/94 carry lastMessageAt (the poll gate). The one without has no messages.
- GET /chats/:id/messages?limit=N -> returns the NEWEST N, ASCENDING. Confirmed by id-matching the limit=5 tail against the last 5 of the unbounded 467-message history.
- Unbounded still returns FULL history (467 msgs), so limit remains non-optional. Unchanged.
- Per-message characterId present on 234/234 assistant messages — group-scene speaker attribution intact.
- activeSwipeIndex and swipeCount both present on the list endpoint. swipeCount is a REAL count over the message_swipes table (chats.storage.ts computes swipeCount: countMap.get(m.id) ?? 0), not a synthesized constant.
- No auth change on the loopback path; no 401. The v2.4.0 Docker-proxy auth tightening does not touch it.

SWIPE SIGNAL PROVEN OBSERVABLE, not inferred from a blank. Full-store scan: 94 chats, 9654 messages. swipeCount distribution {0:1, 1:9649, 2:4}. Four genuinely regenerated messages found, e.g. chat=srToLOvtPA3PWmvhQoZxC id=2TUYD9ZfiWTWgKzoXX8tz swipeCount=2 activeSwipeIndex=1.

NOTABLE FOR s2lw: two of the four have swipeCount=2 with activeSwipeIndex=0 — re-rolled and then swiped BACK to the original. So the discarded text is not always the lower index. Any supersede logic must key on activeSwipeIndex, never on 'the newest swipe'.

ALSO NOTABLE: regeneration is RARE in this store — 4 in 9654 (0.04%). The swipe blind spot is a low-frequency corruption source, not a constant one. That lowers its urgency relative to tp5/hhdr without making it less real.

Test script kept at scratchpad/poller-smoke.mjs; worth promoting into the suite as a live-engine contract test (see umz1 API-first work).

title: Index corruption + catastrophic clobber on corrupt read
description: Concurrent/torn writes corrupted index.yaml; then upsertIndexEntry treated a corrupt read as empty (?? emptyIndex) and rewrote the index with just the new entry, orphaning all others (professor_mari: 1269 entry files vs 33 index rows). Fixes: (1) atomic writeYaml via temp+rename — no torn files, kill-safe; (2) route promotion/cleanup writes through serialized mutateIndex (no more unlocked writeIndex); (3) upsertIndexEntry refuses to overwrite a present-but-unreadable index; (4) scripts/repair-indexes.mjs rebuilds indexes from entry files.
close_reason: Atomic writes + full serialization + upsert clobber-guard + repair script. tsc clean, 53 tests pass.

title: Declare the USER's identity — the one entity that should never be inferred
description:
RAISED BY the 76aw slice 1 findings and TC 2026-08-04.

The user is the single highest-value entity in the store — nearly every user_topics entry is about them — and the only one whose identity is known, stable, and authoritative in advance. It is currently INFERRED like any other name, and inference is failing on it specifically:

- "thomas" collides 11 ways in the entity index, so the ambiguity cap now suppresses it entirely. Thomas Lowe, Thomas Charles Lowe and TC Lowe are all TC\x27s real names and SHOULD resolve to one person; suppression is safe but wrong.
- Thomas Collier (RP character) is generally called "Thomas" and has sometimes been called "TC" — persona blending by the model, not a real alias.
- One concrete corruption already exists: "TC\x27s sons: Henry Warren and Malcolm Bradley Collier" attributes the character\x27s sons to the user.

WHAT TO BUILD: an explicit user-identity record — the set of names and forms that mean the user, marked as user-world. Consulted by the entity index (so those forms resolve together and are exempt from the ambiguity cap, which exists for guesses, not for declarations) and by the mention resolver.

WHY DECLARED RATHER THAN LEARNED: the store contains no evidence that could separate the two Thomases — measured, Collier and Lowe NEVER co-occur in any entry. The discriminator cannot come from the text. It can come from the user in one sentence.

RELATED: this is the same machinery the persona tier needs (0qx6 — facts about the persona known to all characters), and the natural home for the world tag the 76aw doctrine amendment requires. Also the shape a declared character SPLIT would need (Desmond/Draymond Cole drifted from one character into two, which is history no text analysis recovers).

SURFACE: the memory browser is the obvious place to declare and edit it, alongside the identity/alias repair already planned for hwlj.

title: 76aw slice 1: mention-entity index + cue expansion (no LLM)
description:
Slice 1 of 76aw, scoped by measurement and two TC rulings.

RULING 1 (TC): all multi-word proper nouns are worth remembering — Marinara Engine, Elysium Grand, Porsche Taycan are entities of a different TYPE, not noise to filter. So the table is a general mention-entity index and entity typing is NOT a gate on indexing.

RULING 2 (TC): "Claude and Claude Code both refer to you. If characters get to be people, you can be too." So the Claude/Claude Code case is a CORRECT person entity, not the false positive I recorded it as. Removes the sharpest objection to the pronoun signal.

ERICA IS A MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT (TC): her low pronoun rate (0.22, below Elden Ring) is because she is discussed ANALYTICALLY — the Erica Test is the failure we are trying to pass. That signature is caused by the bug, so building the detector to fit it would encode the failure. The independent-use signal catches her instead (0.38).

WHAT SHIPS:
- Extraction of capitalised multi-token runs, PER FIELD (summary and content scanned separately — a regex over concatenated text produced "Priya Chandrasekaran Outcome" by running a name into the next YAML key).
- A mention-entity store keyed on the canonical full form, holding surface variants and the counts the thresholds are derived from.
- PERSON tag = pronoun-proximity rate OR independent-use rate over threshold. The two signals fail in OPPOSITE directions (Erica: 0.22 pronoun / 0.38 independent; Mari Zielinska: 0.54 / 0.06), so either alone loses one of the two most important entities. Noise accepted per TC.
- ALIAS links gated separately by per-part independent use — this is the safety property and it is independent of type. Measured: Cathmore 0.38, Cole 0.72, Taycan 0.33 link; Ring 0.12, Grand 0.07, Zielinska 0.06 do not. The catastrophic case (Elden = Ring) is excluded by construction.
- CUE EXPANSION at retrieval: expand the CONVERSATION text with linked forms, not the stored rows. One expansion per turn instead of per entry, and it keeps the index from growing again after tp5 already cost 23%.

NOT IN THIS SLICE: LLM extraction (slice 2, and the only thing that can supply the world tags the doctrine amendment needs — user-Thomas vs character-Thomas is not a surface-form distinction); a review surface in the memory browser; distinctiveness weighting to replace raw independent use.
close_reason: Shipped 0efe8ca. End-to-end on the live store: 'tell me about Cathmore' reaches 24 -> 90 of 108 Erica-corpus entries; 'tell me about Erica' 89 -> 90. Index built from 14032 files: 231 entities, 146 with an alias. Erica Cathmore links both parts and picks up 'Gunnery Sergeant Cathmore' as coreferent. Residual 18/108 are the tp5 leftovers - the mention is never capitalised, so nothing is harvested to link.

title: .env unconditionally overwrites shell env, so a per-run override is impossible
description:
FOUND 2026-08-03, immediately after MarinaraExtender-1akw, and it is the ROOT CAUSE that made 1akw possible for someone who already knew the rule.

THE CODE (index.ts loadDotEnv):
  // .env always wins — overwrites stale system env vars (e.g. from Python venvs)
  if (key && val) process.env[key] = val;

Unconditional assignment. Not `process.env[key] ??= val`. So a value passed on the command line is read, then silently replaced by .env a moment later.

HOW IT BIT. Restarting a demo sidecar deliberately as:
  MARINARA_EXTENDER_DATA=<scratch> MARINARA_EXTENDER_PORT=3099 MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER=0 node dist/index.js
started with the banner "Engine poller: ON — every 5000ms against http://127.0.0.1:7860". The flag was correct, the code reading it (`=== "1"`) is correct, and .env carries MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER=1. The shell value never survived to the check.

The banner then prints "(disable with MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER=0 if the extension is also running)" — advice the program has just made impossible to follow.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN IT LOOKS. This inverts the precedence every other tool in the ecosystem uses: dotenv and every port of it deliberately do NOT override an existing process.env, precisely so a one-off run can differ from the stored config. Here it means:
- No per-invocation override of ANY setting, for tests, demos, or reproductions.
- The launch command LOOKS like it took effect. There is no warning, no log line, nothing that says "your flag was discarded".
- Anyone reading the code sees `MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER === "1"` and concludes the flag works, because it does — just not from where they set it.

Note the failure it caused (1akw) was a WRITE TO THE LIVE ENGINE from a scratch store. This is not a cosmetic precedence quibble.

THE STATED RATIONALE IS REAL BUT THE CURE IS WORSE. Stale vars leaking in from a Python venv or a parent shell is a genuine annoyance. But the fix costs the ability to configure a single run at all, and it fails SILENTLY, which is the part that does the damage.

FIX:
  if (key && val && process.env[key] === undefined) process.env[key] = val;
plus, to keep the original intent available, a loud line when a shell value shadows a .env value:
  [ME:env] MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER=0 from the environment overrides .env (=1)
so the venv-pollution case the comment worries about becomes VISIBLE rather than silently corrected. If some deployment truly needs the old behaviour, MARINARA_EXTENDER_ENV_WINS=1 can restore it — but it should be opt-in, not the default.

Also worth a test: loadDotEnv currently has no coverage of the precedence question at all.

WORKAROUND UNTIL FIXED: there is none from the command line. You must edit .env, run from a directory with a different PACKAGE_ROOT, or temporarily comment the line out.
notes:
CLOSED OUT 2026-08-04. TC authorised removing the shadowing credential.

The stale MARINARA_EXTENDER_API_KEY was a USER-scope Windows environment variable (not Machine). Backed up to C:\Users\holyk\marinara-extender-REMOVED-api-key.txt with restore instructions, then removed via [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(...,$null,'User').

VERIFIED: a sidecar started without it in scope now logs only '[ME:env] taken from the environment, overriding .env: MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER' — the deliberate flag, no credential warning — which is proof the .env key is the one in use, since the warning fires exactly when the environment shadows it. Already-running processes keep the old value until restarted; that is inherent to how env is inherited at spawn, not a gap.
close_reason: Shipped: b1nu in 7d4ae5e, bkdz in bb82696. Both pushed.

title: Memory browser slice 2: edit, delete, restore (the mutations)
description:
Slice 2 of hwlj. Slice 1 shipped read-only on purpose — editing memories is where a half-built UI does real damage, and reading answered the urgent question first (what is stored, why did recall behave that way).

WHAT THIS ADDS, all over endpoints that already exist and are already tested server-side:
- EDIT — PATCH /api/entries/:id (summary, content, status). Inline in the card, not a modal; the card is already the unit the reader is looking at.
- DELETE — DELETE /api/entries/:id. SOFT by default: the entry moves to cold and stays recoverable. The UI must SAY that, because the whole architecture rests on never destroying a memory on one action.
- DELETED VIEW + RESTORE — GET /api/deleted, POST /api/entries/:id/restore, per scope.
- PURGE — DELETE ?purge=true, reachable ONLY from inside the deleted view, and only behind an explicit confirm. This is the one irreversible action in the product.

CSRF: the page is served from the sidecar itself, so a same-origin fetch POST still carries an Origin header and needs the token. Fetch it at boot from GET /api/csrf-token and send x-me-csrf. The token is minted per process, so a sidecar restart invalidates it — refetch once on 403 and retry, the same recovery the old extension used.

DESIGN CONSTRAINTS CARRIED FROM SLICE 1:
- Model the surface around the question, not the artefact (TC, on the Why? button). Edit and Delete belong ON the memory, beside Why?, for the same reason Why? did.
- Destructive actions must state their reversibility in plain language at the point of action, not in a doc.
- Status is editable because open_threads carry a real lifecycle (open/in_progress/done/deferred) and "done" is what removes a resolved thread from recall.

NOT IN THIS SLICE: create-new-memory (the store should be written by the pipeline, not typed by hand — a manual create path needs its own thinking about dedup and provenance), identity/alias repair, merge/supersede.
close_reason: Shipped in 7d4ae5e, pushed. Edit/delete/restore/purge over the existing endpoints, CSRF with stale-token retry, 10 integration cases pinning the round-trip and that soft-delete is soft.

title: Persona scope — a fourth tier between character and global
description:
DESIGN CALL FROM TC 2026-08-03. Add a PERSONA scope, sitting above character and below global.

THE DEFINITION, in his words: facts known about that persona by ALL characters who interact with them. Today the ladder is chat -> character -> global, and there is no home for "this is true of ME, and everyone who has met me knows it". Such facts currently land in one of two wrong places: character scope (siloed per character, so every character must independently relearn the same fact about the user) or global (leaks to every persona, which is worse — a fact about persona A becomes ambient truth while playing persona B).

THE LADDER AFTER THIS CHANGE:
  chat      — this conversation only
  character — what THIS character knows / their own arc
  persona   — facts about THIS persona, shared across the characters who have met them   <-- NEW
  global    — true everywhere, for every character and every persona

WHY IT IS NOT JUST "GLOBAL BUT SMALLER": global is currently the only cross-character tier and it is deliberately opt-in and rare (verified: no automatic writer ever targets global — ambient, facts, reconcile, holding-pool and arc-promotion write only character and chat). Persona is the tier that SHOULD receive automatic writes, because most durable facts a user establishes are about themselves. Getting this tier in is what lets automatic capture stop over-writing to character.

IT MUST BE EPISTEMIC, NOT FLAT — TC: "or with the secret system". Persona-scope must NOT mean "every character knows this". It means "this is a fact about the persona, whose visibility is governed". Depends on and feeds MarinaraExtender-1m9 (stateful entity-state lane + epistemic injection, who-knows-what incl. hiding):
- default: known to characters who have actually interacted with this persona
- gated: known to a named subset (told to one character in confidence)
- hidden: true of the persona, known to none — the user knows, the cast does not
A persona tier without the epistemic layer would leak secrets to every character on contact, which is strictly worse than the status quo. Do NOT ship the scope before the visibility model exists, or design it so the default is conservative (interaction-gated) and widening is explicit.

PLUMBING — the identifier is already available, at every layer we need:
- Engine capability host: persistence.getChat(chatId) returns personaId on CapabilityChatRecord. Our package can resolve it without any Engine change.
- Extension API v5 exposes personaId (behind read_active_persona) if we ever go that route.
- The sidecar contributor input already carries chatId, so the package can look personaId up and pass it to /api/pre-turn.

SURFACE AREA — this widens a serialized enum, which this codebase has already been burned by. See the EntryProvenance note in storage.ts: "widening a serialized enum breaks consumers silently". Touch list: Scope type + VALID_SCOPES, scopeDir/indexPath/entryPath, loadIndexes and selectEntries in loader.ts, a new MARINARA_EXTENDER_BUDGET_PERSONA (the three existing budgets are chat 4000 / character 2000 / global 1000), promotion.runPromotionAll, cleanup, cold storage, dedup targets, the identity map (persona identities are a separate namespace from character identities and must not collide), the receipts scope accounting, and the UI sidebar.
Back-compat: old stores have no persona dir and no persona entries. Absent must read as empty, never as an error.

OPEN QUESTIONS TO SETTLE BEFORE BUILDING:
1. Persona identity — personas can be renamed and recreated like characters. Do they need the same alias/relink machinery (/api/identity/relink) or can they key on the Engine personaId alone? Renaming is the common case and it must not orphan memories.
2. Group scenes — several characters, one persona. Interaction-gating needs a record of WHICH characters have met this persona. Does that live on the persona index or in the entity-state lane from 1m9?
3. Budget default. Persona facts are high-value and low-volume; likely a small budget (~1000) but it competes with character for the same prompt space.
4. Migration — is there a pass that identifies existing character-scope entries that are really about the user and offers to relocate them? Probably a later, human-gated tool, not an automatic sweep.

RELATED: 1m9 (epistemic layer, hard dependency for the visibility model), c0b7 (scope defaulting — fix that BEFORE adding a fourth value, or the malformed-scope path gains another way to be wrong), hwlj (UI needs a persona section in the sidebar).

title: In-engine INJECTION is the strongest case for an engine-side consumer — outranks capture
description:
TC asked 2026-08-03 whether in-engine helps INJECTION or SEARCH. Injection: yes, decisively. Search: marginal. This RE-RANKS our engine asks.

INJECTION — THE STRONGEST CASE YET, stronger than capture.
The current path is documented as lossy in our own source. turn-bridge.ts header comment, verbatim: "The engine then injects that lorebook on the NEXT generation, which is why memory has always been one turn behind on this path." Flow is POST /api/process-turn -> { memoryBlock } -> syncMemoryToLorebook -> engine injects it on the FOLLOWING generation.

Three distinct wins from a pre_generation hook, in order of weight:
1. IT KILLS THE ONE-TURN LAG, AND THAT IS A CORRECTNESS FIX, NOT A LATENCY ONE. loadContext scores relevance against recentText. On the poller path recentText is the turn that ALREADY HAPPENED, so we retrieve against the previous exchange rather than the user message actually being answered. A pre_generation hook has the incoming message in hand. Every ranking improvement we make (tp5, sph8) is currently handicapped by scoring against the wrong text — fixing the scorer while the query stays one turn stale caps the gain.
2. IT RETIRES THE LOREBOOK HACK. preGenInjections is per-turn, ephemeral, correctly positioned, and leaves no persistent artifact. Today we mutate a shared lorebook the user can see, edit, and be confused by. The "prompt-context" permission exists in the manifest enum for exactly this purpose, and long-term-memory already works this way (recall -> text -> engine injects).
3. IT REMOVES A WRITE-THEN-HOPE RACE. We write the lorebook after turn N and trust it lands before turn N+1 assembles its prompt. Ephemeral injection has no such window.

SEARCH — MARGINAL, DO NOT BUILD FOR IT.
- Packages get CapabilityEmbeddingHost { spaceId, label, embed(texts, signal) } — credential-free embeddings using whatever the user configured. That would retire our own embedding config burden (embeddings.ts). Real, but small.
- NOT AVAILABLE OVER REST: probed the live engine — /api/embeddings, /api/embed, /api/vectors/search all 404, and no matching route files exist at v2.4.0. It is package-only, so the sidecar cannot borrow it today.
- resources.listLorebooks would help cross-referencing (relevant to bos, lorebook import).
- BUT our retrieval weakness is OURS: summary-only scoring (tp5) and single-lane ranking (sph8). Borrowing their embedder does not improve our ranking. The engine cannot fix a problem that lives in our scorer.

CONSEQUENCE — RE-RANK THE ENGINE ASKS. Previously apmt (messageId + activeSwipeIndex on the post_processing payload) was treated as the ask, then demoted when in-engine CAPTURE was ruled unnecessary. That ruling stands and is unchanged — it was about capture. INJECTION is a separate question and it lands the other way.
If we ever get ONE Engine change, ask for the INJECTION CONSUMER: an Engine-side getCapabilityService("marinara-extender:runtime") call in the generation path that takes our text and injects it, mirroring exactly what services/generation/long-term-memory-runtime.ts already does for long-term-memory. That single change fixes a documented correctness limitation. The capture payload fields fix a latency nicety.
ORDER: injection consumer FIRST. apmt stays parked and junior.

NOT A BLOCKER FOR THE AUDIT: the package is a distribution shell; none of this is needed to submit. But it is the thing worth asking for once a relationship exists.
notes:
LINUX MATRIX COMPLETE — 2026-08-03. 24 of 25 regression targets PASS on our branch. Both failures verified pre-existing on untouched upstream.

PASS (24): spatial, prompt, timezone, emoji, providers, jsonish, tts, issues, backup, extensions-security, professor-mari-shell-sandbox, agent-import-security, custom-tool-import-security, PROMPT-CONTEXT (ours), request-security, runtime-integrity, novelai-zip-security, image-result-security, expression-tools, REGENERATION-CONTEXT, sprites, static-cache, localization, docs.
Note the two that matter most for a generation-path change both pass: regeneration-context and prompt.

FAIL (2), BOTH REPRODUCED ON PRISTINE a986675bd BY CHECKING IT OUT AND RE-RUNNING — not inferred:
1. regression:roleplay — scripts/regressions/roleplay-streaming.regression.ts:237, "Echo Chamber should leave the native Roleplay scrollbar reachable". expected /const HUD_EDGE_GAP = 24;[^\n]*native chat scrollbar/u, actual a comment banner. Identical assertion and identical actual value on pristine upstream.
2. regression:noodle -> noodle-prompt.regression.ts:968, date-dependent schedule fixture ("No generated schedules are available for today").

PATTERN WORTH NAMING, because it shaped this whole session: BOTH upstream failures — plus the Windows one that turned out to be ours — are SOURCE-TEXT-SCANNING or DATE-DEPENDENT assertions rather than behavioural tests. roleplay-streaming greps client source for a literal containing a constant and a comment phrase; prompt.regression greps for a literal containing a bare \n (which is why CRLF broke it); noodle-prompt asserts against "today". Tests that assert on the SHAPE OF SOURCE TEXT or on the CALENDAR rot without the product breaking. Useful context if we ever offer fixes, and a caution for our own suite: none of the 388 sidecar tests should ever assert on source text.

smoke:ui NOT RUN — needs Playwright browsers. Excluded deliberately, and must be stated as not-run rather than implied green.

WHAT WE MAY NOW CLAIM IN THE PR, all verifiable by a reviewer:
- tsc --noEmit clean on the server package
- our new regression:prompt-context passes on Windows AND Linux
- 24 of 25 regression targets pass on Linux on this branch
- the 2 failures reproduce on untouched upstream a986675bd; here is the method (checkout the base commit, re-run the single target)
- smoke:ui not run
WHAT WE MAY NOT CLAIM: a green `pnpm regression`. The aggregate is && chained and aborts at noodle regardless of our work.

VERIFICATION IS NOW COMPLETE. Remaining before submission is authoring, not testing: PR description, and the decision on whether to offer the shared-timeout-helper extraction as a follow-up commit.

title: Strip memory tags from the STORED message after capture (PATCH), not just from display
description:
PROBLEM (TC, 2026-08-03): memory tags are broadcast in the open.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, verified against the live engine 2026-08-03:
- The regex script "Marinara Extender: Strip memory tags" IS installed and enabled (id eYD3Ppl8Abgkyty4h05vw, placement ["ai_output"], promptOnly false), left over from the extension era.
- It WORKS. Tested against real stored content: 155 messages contain a tag, 155 strip cleanly, 0 leak. (An earlier count of "151 leaking" was my own shell-escaping mangling the pattern before testing — the engine was never at fault. Recorded so nobody re-investigates a non-bug.)
- BUT A REGEX SCRIPT NEVER TOUCHES THE STORED ROW. Engine docs, docs/extending/regex-scripts.md: "Only Display: change only what you see in the chat. The saved message and the text the model gets in later turns do not change." Apply mode is separate from placement.
- So the raw tag persists in the message row permanently. That is how I was able to grep 155 of them out of the API in the first place. It survives into exports, search, and — depending on apply mode — future prompt history, where it both burns context and teaches the model to emit more of them.

THE FIX, AND IT NEEDS NOTHING FROM UPSTREAM: PATCH /api/chats/:chatId/messages/:messageId with { content: string } exists (packages/server/src/routes/chats.routes.ts @ v2.4.0, ~line 1860 -> storage.updateMessageContent). After the reader captures a turn, rewrite the stored message with the tag removed. The tag then disappears from display, storage, exports and all future prompt history at once — strictly better than any regex apply mode.

WHY IN-ENGINE CAPTURE WOULD NOT DO THIS BETTER: persistence happens BEFORE post_processing (7zro ordering proof — the row is written at generate.routes.ts ~6353, the phase runs at ~6805+, and the Engine own rewrite path re-writes the row later at ~8867). So even in-engine it is write-then-rewrite, exactly like PATCH. The ONLY difference is that in-engine closes the window within the same request, while PATCH closes it a poll tick later. In-engine buys a shorter visible window and nothing else here.

FIRST, CONFIRM APPLY MODE on the installed script. If it is Only Display, the model is currently reading its own tags back in history every turn, which is a live context-pollution and tag-echo problem independent of anything cosmetic. Prompt-side stripping should be on regardless of this issue.

BUILD CARE — this rewrites user-visible history, so it is higher-risk than anything else the reader does:
- Strip ONLY the tag span. Never reflow, retrim, or normalise the surrounding prose.
- No-op when the strip would change nothing; never PATCH for its own sake.
- Order matters: capture MUST be durable before the strip. Losing the tag before ingesting it destroys the memory outright — worse than a visible tag.
- Swipes: updateMessageContent syncs to the ACTIVE swipe. Re-verify behaviour against a message with swipeCount > 1 before enabling; the standing invariant (key on activeSwipeIndex, never newest) applies here too.
- Concurrency: do not clobber a user edit made between capture and strip. Compare against the content we captured; skip if it moved.
- Make it reversible/opt-out — MARINARA_EXTENDER_STRIP_TAGS — because it mutates the user chat record.

RELATED: the Engine also has a native bracket-command parser (registerCapabilityConversationCommand + stripCapabilityConversationCommands, matching [tag] and [tag:...]), but its only caller is services/conversation/character-commands.ts — CONVERSATION MODE ONLY. It would not cover Roleplay, so it is not the answer here.

title: Upstream ask: put messageId + activeSwipeIndex on the post_processing agent payload
description:
TINY, SELF-CONTAINED UPSTREAM ASK. Deliberately filed SEPARATE from MarinaraExtender-lmcz (catalog/trust policy) — two small issues beat one bloated one, and this one is a code ask with receipts while lmcz is a policy ask.

THE ASK: include the persisted assistant messageId and its activeSwipeIndex on the AgentContext handed to post_processing agents.

WHY IT IS NEARLY FREE — receipts, breadcrumbs @ v2.4.0:
- packages/server/src/routes/generate.routes.ts is ONE sequential handler. At ~line 6353 it persists the assistant turn, branching explicitly: regenerate -> chats.addSwipe(input.regenerateMessageId, fullResponse) with savedSwipeIndex = createdSwipe.index; continue -> updateMessageContent with savedSwipeIndex from the row; otherwise -> chats.createMessage with savedSwipeIndex = 0.
- At ~6370 it ALREADY passes { messageId: savedMsg.id, swipeIndex: savedSwipeIndex, regenerate } into materializeAssistantSpatialState — the hierarchical-maps capability package anchor. So handing (message, swipe) to package code at this exact point is an established, shipped pattern.
- At ~6812 it computes latestAssistantMessageId.
- At ~7036 it builds postAgentContext = { ...agentContext, mainResponse, preGenInjections, parallelResults } — WITHOUT either value, which is in lexical scope twenty-four lines above.
So this is not a new capability. It is passing variables the handler already holds.

WHAT IT UNBLOCKS FOR CONSUMERS: any post_processing agent that must attribute its output to a specific turn REVISION rather than to 'the latest text'. Today mainResponse (packages/shared/src/types/agent.ts, AgentContext) is a bare string: an agent cannot tell a first generation from a re-roll, and cannot name the row it is looking at. Consumers are forced to infer the anchor by reading back the last assistant message, which is an UNCONTRACTED correlation that upstream can silently reorder.

SUGGESTED SHAPE: add messageId: string and activeSwipeIndex: number to AgentContext, populated for post_processing (null/absent for pre_generation and parallel, which run before the row exists). Optionally regenerate: boolean, which the handler already computes as Boolean(input.regenerateMessageId).

KNOWN NON-GOAL: this does NOT cover swipe-back. Navigating between existing swipes runs no generation, so no agent phase observes it. Not asking upstream to solve that; a reconciling reader is the right answer on our side. Say so in the issue so the scope stays small and obviously cheap.

BEFORE FILING: same voice pass as lmcz. Do not bundle with the catalog question.
notes:
DECISION 2026-08-03: IN-ENGINE CAPTURE IS NOT A NEEDED CAPABILITY. Do not pursue. Keep this issue as documentation, not as queued work.

REASONING, heaviest first:
1. The READER IS MANDATORY REGARDLESS. Swipe-back runs no generation, so no in-engine hook can ever observe it (7zro ordering proof). Something must keep reading no matter what we build, which makes in-engine capture an optimisation layered on a mechanism we are keeping anyway — never a replacement.
2. ITS MAIN BENEFIT IS ALREADY FREE. The prize was anchoring to (messageId, activeSwipeIndex) instead of a time watermark. activeSwipeIndex is returned on the REST list endpoint — verified live in jaos, which found 4 genuine regenerations carrying it. The poller can anchor correctly TODAY with zero Engine changes. That work is s2lw and needs nothing from upstream.
3. WHAT REMAINS IS LATENCY ONLY — capture at the turn versus at the next poll tick. Real but small, and the reader reconciles either way.
4. THE COST IS TWO UPSTREAM ASKS PLUS A FRAGILE DEPENDENCY: an Engine-side getCapabilityService consumer, THEN these payload fields, plus the uncontracted persistence-vs-phase ordering we would have to guard with the string-compare tripwire. Against a benefit of "slightly sooner".

REVISIT CONDITION: if the audit relationship makes Engine PRs cheap and routine, this can be reopened — the receipts in this issue and in 7zro are already gathered and need no rework. Until then nothing in the roadmap waits on it.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD: s2lw — anchor the reader on (messageId, activeSwipeIndex) and supersede on drift. No permission, no upstream, fixes the actual bug.

title: Adopt LTM-style lane fusion + explainability in Extender retrieval (feeds tp5)
description:
Found during the long-term-memory teardown (5hpe): their retrieval is ahead of ours in exactly the place tp5 says we are weak. Recording it as a design target rather than letting the finding evaporate.

WHAT THEY DO (contract-level, no line anchors):
- FOUR RETRIEVAL LANES, each producing scored chunk hits: (1) direct metadata match on note-id patterns and #tags parsed out of the query, (2) BM25 over chunk text, (3) a keyword index, (4) graph expansion over note-to-note links seeded from the top lexical and keyword hits. Optional fifth vector lane when an embedding adapter and a usable vector index exist for the current spaceId.
- RECIPROCAL RANK FUSION across the lanes with per-lane weights (semanticWeight, lexicalWeight, graphWeight, keywordWeight), all settable per chat.
- BUDGETING as a distinct stage after ranking: maxChunks, maxTokens, a relevance score threshold, and exact-text dedupe.
- EXPLAINABILITY AS A FIRST-CLASS OUTPUT: every selected chunk carries its score, the lanes that surfaced it, and per-lane reasons; REJECTED candidates are returned too, each with a rejectionReason. Emitted as a debug event with counts.

WHY IT MATTERS TO US: our scoring reads entry.summary only and never sees the body (tp5). Even fixing that leaves us single-lane. The graph lane is the interesting one — it surfaces material the query never lexically matched, via links from what did match, which is precisely the recall our arcs/threads data already has the shape for and does not exploit.

DO NOT COPY WHOLESALE. Their input is weaker than ours (artifact-derived, never sees a raw turn), so lanes tuned for summary text may not transfer to turn-derived entries. Take the ARCHITECTURE — lanes, fusion, budget-as-a-stage, rejected-with-reasons — not the weights.

THE EXPLAINABILITY PIECE IS THE CHEAPEST WIN AND SHOULD LAND FIRST: 'why did this memory not surface' is currently answered by hand-grepping the store. Returning rejected candidates with reasons would have shortened several past triages, and it directly serves the three-cause triage (capture gap vs retrieval invisibility vs digest corruption).

RELATED: tp5 (summary-only scoring), and the ranking work implied by vrw.
notes:
ERRATUM to the phase-1 note above: one line lost a word to shell backtick substitution when it was written. It should read:

- selectEntries now returns traces + rejected + candidateCount. The greedy-fill SKIP BRANCH (the loop continue when an entry does not fit the remaining budget) — where a stored-but-unsurfaced memory used to vanish without trace — now records budget_exhausted. That was the single hardest case to tell apart from a capture gap.

title: Rewrite the expert skills API-first — contracts, not line numbers
description:
RULING (TC, 2026-08-02): the archaeology era is over. Skill references go API-first. Line numbers rot; contracts do not.

EVIDENCE THIS IS NOW URGENT: hkdq carried a 'patch targets line 503 and line 754 BY NUMBER' urgency that had to be RETRACTED as unverified. 1wpt cites openai.provider.ts lines 805-810 and 842 against an engine that has since moved 882 commits. Every line-anchored claim in the skills is now suspect by default.

WHAT API-FIRST MEANS:
- name the CONTRACT (endpoint, field, capability name, permission string, manifest key), never the coordinate
- version the contract when the engine versions it (capability API 1.2 vs 1.7; extension API v5)
- where a file must be named, name the module and the exported symbol, not the line
- record OBSERVED WIRE BEHAVIOR (request/response shapes) over source excerpts — wire survives refactors

SCOPE:
- .claude/skills/marinara-extender-expert/ (SKILL.md + references/*) — repo copy is canonical, then re-sync ~/.claude/skills/
- marinara-engine-expert — also gets the n4fd rework (built for extension authoring, wrong shape for contribution)

MUST CAPTURE FROM THE v2.4.0 SWEEP:
- extension API v5 context contract (chatId/characterId/characterIds/personaId; read_active_characters, read_active_persona)
- the sandbox reality: bare .js imports with capabilities: [] and gets the opaque-origin Worker
- capability package permissions + entrypoint contract
- poller's engine contract (/chats lastMessageAt, /chats/:id/messages newest-N-ascending, per-message characterId, activeSwipeIndex swipe semantics)

title: Prototype marinara-extender as a Marinara capability package (dev-install)
description:
THE NEW SEAM. Engine v2.4.0's package system (Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents, AGPL-3.0, capability API now 1.7) exposes exactly the authority hkdq wanted to fork the engine to get. Ship a package instead of branching.

WHAT THE API GIVES US (from docs/development/optional-agent-packages.md at v2.4.0):
- manifest permissions: agent-runtime, chat-read, chat-write, routes, storage, ui
- server entrypoints: routes, LIFECYCLE HOOKS, PROMPT PROVIDERS, result handlers, storage migrations
- client entrypoints: panels, chat surfaces, settings sections
- API 1.2: transaction-scoped chat/message ops; narrow chat-metadata writes committed atomically with 'an owner message, SWIPE, or spatial snapshot'; eligible lore-entry selection; normalized chat/character records; resolved language-model calls. Credentials, provider impls, and DB handles stay private to Engine.
- API 1.7: branch lineage on CapabilityChatRecord (parentChatId / parentMessageId / childMessageId)

WHY IT SUPERSEDES THE FORK: a lifecycle hook IS capture at the write path — the thing hkdq called 'the one place no extension API can ever reach'. That premise was true at 2.3.4 and is false at 2.4.0. Swipe-atomic metadata writes address the regeneration blind spot (s2lw / 4kbt) at the source rather than by polling for it. A prompt provider replaces the two-constant-lorebook-entry injection hack.

SHAPE: sidecar stays the brain. Package server entrypoint is a thin broker to 127.0.0.1:3001. Do NOT reimplement the memory model inside the package.

DELIVERY: dev-install, not the catalog. Catalog eligibility is filed separately (MarinaraExtender-lmcz) and must never gate the house running this.

SEQUENCE: keep the poller ALIVE and authoritative until the lifecycle hook is proven to fire on a real turn — same discipline hkdq set for the emitter. Test that it fires before moving capture onto it.

DEPENDS ON: jaos (capture path verified against 2.4.0 first).
notes:
ORDERING CONDITION RESOLVED — 2026-08-02. The compare is SOUND. The hook is NOT AVAILABLE. Drop hook-capture; the reader carries text truth. Breadcrumbs @ v2.4.0.

PART 1 — ORDERING IS PROVABLE, AND FAVOURABLE TO THE RULING.
- Within a phase, groups run CONCURRENTLY: executePhase (services/agents/agent-pipeline.ts ~line 278) dispatches through settleAgentJobsWithConcurrencyLimit(groups, AGENT_PHASE_MAX_CONCURRENT_GROUPS=8). There is no priority field and no inter-agent sequencing, so position among agents CANNOT be pinned.
- The lanes are a red herring for ordering. getAgentBatchLane returns rewrite|standard and only prevents a text_rewrite agent SHARING AN LLM REQUEST with tracker work ("Rewrite agents edit the assistant transcript and must never share an LLM request with tracker or other post-processing work"). It is a batching rule, not an execution order.
- BUT THE RULING SURVIVES ANYWAY, because what matters is not agent order — it is when the rewrite PERSISTS. The rewrite is written at routes/generate.routes.ts ~line 8867, await chats.updateMessageContent(messageId, editedText), inside a changedMessage guard, ~1800 lines downstream of where post_processing agents are dispatched (~7036) and after their results are collected. While agents execute, the row still holds the RAW text persisted at ~6353.
- So raw mainResponse vs row-at-hook-time WOULD match on every healthy turn, and would fire only on a true ordering break. TC read it correctly. Comparing post-rewrite would indeed have stacked a second uncontracted ordering on the first.

PART 2 — AND IT IS ALL MOOT, BECAUSE WE CANNOT RUN CODE THERE.
Chasing the ordering surfaced the prior question. shared/src/schemas/capability-package.schema.ts (~line 223) gives execution: z.enum(["pipeline","feature","host"]).
- pipeline: the Engine runs the agent PROMPT through the normal LLM pipeline and handles a fixed result type. NO PACKAGE CODE EXECUTES. We would get a model call, not a capture hook.
- feature / host: require an Engine-side consumer that already knows the agent. This is Receipt 4 again — LTM's feature agent functions only because services/generation/long-term-memory-runtime.ts hard-codes its service key. Corroborated by package-manager.service.ts (~line 278), which validates that an agentDetail contribution "must identify a feature or host agent from this package" — i.e. these are the Engine-implemented kinds.
CONCLUSION: a third-party capability package has NO generic way to execute its own code during a turn. The blocker is not ordering and not the missing payload fields; it is that there is no third-party execution path at all.

RESIDUAL UNKNOWN, stated rather than glossed: I have not read the runtime dispatch for execution:"host" end to end, only its validation and the feature-path precedent. If "host" turns out to be generically dispatchable to package code, PART 2 reopens and the compare (proven sound in PART 1) goes straight back on the table. Cheap to settle when it next matters; not worth the tokens now, because a third-party package still cannot be installed without lmcz.

DECISION PER TC'S OWN CONDITION: drop the string-compare, and with it hook-capture. Degrade to the identity checks we already have and let the READER carry all text truth. The poller is not a fallback and not in hospice — it is the only staff. This also absorbs rewrites exactly as the ruling described: prose guardian edits the row after capture, the reader sees text drift on an already-captured (messageId, swipeIndex), re-captures and supersedes. Same machinery as swipe-back. Hook proves IDENTITY, reader keeps TRUTH — except there is no hook, so the reader does both.

7zro SCOPE NOW: the SURFACE only — client entrypoint UI, privileged routes, package-owned storage. None of that needs turn participation. Do not build capture into the package.

ONE OBSERVATION, NOT A PROPOSAL: a capability package's CLIENT entrypoint is ordinary app-level code (LTM ships React TSX for chat-settings), NOT the opaque-origin Worker that Personal Extensions get. So browser-side turn observation is technically alive inside a package even though it is dead for Personal Extensions. Noting it for completeness only — it is still gated behind lmcz, and the standing ruling against reviving browser-side capture stands unless TC reopens it.

title: Upstream policy ask: third-party capability-package eligibility (file EARLY, parallel)
description:
POLICY ASK, NOT A CODE ASK. This asks whether we are PERMITTED to run a capability package at all. It does not ask for any engine change. (The code ask — payload fields for a turn hook — is MarinaraExtender-apmt, a separate issue.)

BACKGROUND: the capability-package system is the only supported route to engine-level authority (server entrypoints, routes, package storage, credential-free LLM + embedding access). Marinara-Agents docs state: "Only first-party trusted executable packages are enabled by the official catalog. A future third-party flow requires a separate explicit trust design." So today it is a members-only club, and we are not members.

THE THREE QUESTIONS TO ASK PASTA-DEVS:
1. Is a third-party trust flow for capability packages planned, and on what horizon?
2. Can a package with SERVER entrypoints be installed outside the official catalog — a dev/local install? And is that path SUPPORTED, or merely incidental and liable to be closed off? (This is the one that decides whether we can run our own package on our own machine.)
3. Does contributing require a CLA? (Carried from hkdq law #2. Licence itself is clear — both repos are AGPL-3.0.)

REMOVED 2026-08-02: an earlier draft also asked "would a second memory package be considered given first-party long-term-memory exists?" TC withheld it — not to be asked until our positioning is nameable, so we can state an actual difference instead of pre-conceding overlap. Do not re-add it. (Recording the removal because the question was in the filed text after I had reported leaving it out.)

STATUS CHANGE — THIS IS NOW A HARD GATE, not the background item it was filed as.
The original text said "NOT A BLOCKER: prototype ships via dev-install regardless. This only decides DISTRIBUTION." That was written believing we could dev-install and build capture. It is now WRONG on both halves:
- 7zro proved there is no third-party execution path during a turn at all. execution is pipeline | feature | host: pipeline runs a PROMPT with no package code; feature/host require an Engine-side consumer that hard-codes the agent (Receipt 4).
- So the package route currently buys us only a UI surface, and even that needs an install path question 2 has to answer.
Question 2 is therefore the highest-value question we have open with upstream. Everything else about the package direction waits behind it.

WHY STILL FILE EARLY: an unanswered gate silently stalls finished work. Receipt that they answer filed issues: engine #4335 fixed the reasoning_effort bug we filed (1wpt, now closed).
notes:
PROVENANCE ADDENDUM (Mari, via TC, 2026-08-03). Already closed; recording her framing so the answers carry their source.

- TRUST FLOW: not a policy question — an EVENT. Submission + audit list, attested by the approver herself (SpicyMarinara / Mari Real). The upstream action is a SUBMISSION, not a question.
- DEV-INSTALL: local is fair game, and additionally UNENFORCEABLE — self-hosted AGPL software; nobody can close off your own floor. Green by testimony, not by permission.
- CLA: no. Twice attested.
Do not file this upstream. apmt is the only remaining question-shaped ask (see f1mq amendment: it is actually the junior of two, behind an Engine-side service-consumer PR).
close_reason:
ANSWERED BY TC 2026-08-02 from a direct conversation with SpicyMarinara (Mari Real), who owns approval. No upstream filing needed — do not file it.

1. CLA: NO. Not required. This was answered in a prior session and I incorrectly carried it forward as open (it came in via hkdq law #2). hkdq law #2 is now fully resolved: same licence, no CLA.
2. LOCAL/DEV INSTALL: anything we can get working on our own machine is fair game for US to run. It is NOT a distribution channel — we cannot ship to users that way.
3. THIRD-PARTY FLOW: IT EXISTS. Complete the extension, submit it, SpicyMarinara approves. Not the closed club the docs implied.

NEW AND SCHEDULE-DRIVING: WE ARE ALREADY ON THE LIST TO BE AUDITED. That is why the package has to be brought up to date for v2.4.0 — the audit is the forcing function, not the catalog policy. This converts the package work from "worth exploring" to "has a deadline we do not control."

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BOARD: apmt was blocked on this and is now unblocked as a dependency, but its VALUE still turns on the execution question (can an approved third-party package run its own code during a turn, or does execution:feature/host still need an Engine-side hard-coded consumer that only first-party code can add?). That question is now the live one and is tracked separately.

title: Read long-term-memory package source — provenance and store coordination
description:
First-party competitor landed in the official catalog: long-term-memory v1.0.8 (capabilityApi 1.6, builtAgainst engine 2.3.5). Full source published at Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents packages/long-term-memory/ (client.js, server.mjs, plus src/engine/... TSX/TS sources).

Catalog blurb: 'Extracts durable memories from chat summaries, character records, and lorebooks, then recalls relevant context from a package-owned vault' with scoped vault browsing, review, source management, recall controls, preset-marker placement.

PRIOR GOING IN (TC, to be tested not assumed): 'from chat summaries, character records, and lorebooks' plus 'review' reads as derivation-from-artifacts behind a review gate — import-side, lorebooks with extra steps. Errata issued on the last teardown for sneering before reading, so the READ IS MANDATORY and the prior is falsifiable.

TWO QUESTIONS THE READ MUST ANSWER:
1. Where do memories COME from? Derived from existing artifacts (summaries/cards/lorebooks) at import/review time, or formed from raw turns at write time? This is the organic-formation membrane and decides whether it competes with us or complements us.
2. Does it write into memory-recall's embedding chunks, or a package-owned store? 'package-owned vault' says its own. If so: engine Memory Recall + LTM vault + Extender = THREE uncoordinated recall paths injecting into one prompt in one process. That collision is a finding in its own right.

CONDITIONAL: if it claims memory FORMATION, the Erica Test applies to it — same standard we hold ourselves to. Grep bodies, not summaries; word-boundary the name.

Blocks positioning decisions and the package prototype's scope.
notes:
TEARDOWN COMPLETE 2026-08-02. Read against published source at Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents packages/long-term-memory/src/ (~50 server modules). API-first: contracts named, no line-number anchors.

Q1 — WHERE DO MEMORIES COME FROM? DERIVATION FROM ARTIFACTS. Confirmed, not inferred.
The decisive contract is ltmSourceProvenanceSchema: kind: z.enum(['character','lorebook','chat_summary']). The schema REFUSES a source note without provenance ('Source notes must store import provenance') and refuses provenance on any non-source note. There is no message provenance, no turn provenance, no write-path capture. interop.ts builds source notes by reading chat.metadata.summaryEntries (the Roleplay Chat Summary) and lorebook entries.
So the raw turn is never an input. Its richest source, chat_summary, is itself the Engine's compression of turns — derivation from a derivation.
Extraction is LLM-driven from the source note text into evidence units, with a deterministic non-LLM path for Game Mode summaries only.

REVIEW GATE, precisely: reviewRequired is set when provenance.kind is 'character' or 'lorebook'. chat_summary does NOT set it, so summary-derived mutations can auto-apply under autoApplyLowRiskOnly. That is the one no-human path, and it is fed by summaries.

Q2 — OWN STORE, NOT MEMORY-RECALL'S CHUNKS. Decisive.
LongTermMemoryStorage(root) owns a package-private vault under getLongTermMemoryDirectories(root), with its OWN indexes: bm25, keyword, graph, metadata, embeddings. It borrows only the Engine's EMBEDDING ADAPTER (PackageEmbeddingAdapter {spaceId,label,embed}) — the vector space, not Memory Recall's chunk store. interop.ts touches summaries and lorebooks and never references memory-recall.
CONSEQUENCE CONFIRMED: Memory Recall (per-chat embedding chunks over raw messages) + LTM vault + Extender = THREE uncoordinated recall paths injecting into one prompt in one process. None knows the others' budget. LTM writes its own injection receipt and its own token accounting.

TC'S PRIOR — RIGHT ON ORIGIN, WRONG AS A DISMISSAL. Both halves recorded honestly.
RIGHT: 'import-side, derivation-from-artifacts plus a review gate' is exactly what the provenance enum proves. It cannot form memory from lived turns, which is our thesis and remains uncontested.
WRONG: 'lorebooks with extra steps' understates the machinery, and the retrieval is BETTER THAN OURS. LTM retrieval runs four lanes — direct metadata match, BM25, keyword index, graph expansion over note links — plus optional vector, fused by reciprocal rank, then budgeted with dedupe and full explainability (selected AND rejected candidates with reasons). Ours scores entry.summary only and cannot see the body (tp5). Their data model also carries evidence units with bucket/claimKind/importance/confidence/salience/links/sourceHash, subject identity with identity-repair, reconciliation, draft/apply gating, rejected-suggestion memory, and retention/archival.
Verdict: it is not a competitor to our capture thesis; it is a SUPERIOR RETRIEVAL IMPLEMENTATION sitting on a weaker input. That is the uncomfortable and useful finding.

ERICA TEST — NOT RUN, AND HONESTLY SO. It does not claim formation from lived turns, so the trigger condition is only partly met. It is also NOT INSTALLED on this engine (health reports 29 packages; long-term-memory is not among them — it sits in the v2.3.5/staging lane), so running the test would mean installing a second live injector into the prompt. Not worth it yet. If we ever do, the standard applies unchanged: grep bodies not summaries, word-boundary the name.

FEEDS 7zro: retrieval lane fusion + explainability is the design to beat/borrow, and the three-injector collision is a real risk our package must not worsen.
close_reason: Teardown complete; findings recorded in notes. Both questions answered from the published source.

title: Regenerated turns are re-ingested but never supersede the discarded reply's facts
description:
handleTurnNotification correctly sets DetectedTurn.regenerated=true on a swipe (4kbt, verified live). But turn-bridge.ts handleDetectedTurn() uses that flag ONLY in its console.info line — it is not passed to POST /api/process-turn (body is characterId, characterName, participantIds, chatId, sceneTitle, messageText, userMessageText). So a re-roll runs a NORMAL ingestion of the new text and nothing retires the facts extracted from the version the user threw away.

Observed live 2026-07-30 on the dev rig:
  [ME:bridge] turn ingested — ... (regenerated) lorebook=UfH3XhTzZoEin1hMcPkqj
  [ME:dedup] skipped duplicate (character_topics/chat:...): "[about: Erica Cathmore] ..."

Dedup masked it in that test only because the fact came from the USER message, which a swipe does not change. A re-roll whose ASSISTANT text differs materially will deposit facts from BOTH the discarded and the kept version, and both will surface as recall.

This is the second half of the swipe problem. 4kbt fixed DETECTION — the sidecar now knows a re-roll happened. It did not fix the RESPONSE. Detection without supersession still leaves the confabulation the erica test exists to catch, just with an extra correct entry beside the wrong one.

Design note: fact-vs-feeling applies. The discarded reply's derived entries should be superseded (kept, marked, pointer to the replacement) rather than deleted — same tier-move-not-delete rule as everywhere else. Needs process-turn to accept a supersedes/regenerated signal plus the source message id so it can find what to retire.
acceptance_criteria: A re-roll whose assistant text differs materially leaves exactly one live set of facts for that turn; the discarded version's entries are retrievable as superseded, not surfaced as current.
notes:
DESIGN INPUT from the v2.4.0 ordering proof (7zro) — 2026-08-02. Answers 'should the user confirm which swipe is canon?'

1. FOR RE-ROLLS, NO HUMAN IS NEEDED. THE SWIPE INDEX IS ALREADY THE USER'S ANSWER. activeSwipeIndex is not ambiguous data we must interpret — it is a recorded user choice. Leaving a swipe active IS the vote. A confirmation prompt asks them to say again what the UI already recorded. Capture should follow activeSwipeIndex mechanically; that is the standing invariant, and it is sufficient here.

2. THE AMBIGUITY IS NOT AT CAPTURE, IT IS DOWNSTREAM. A confirmation gate is worth its friction only where the machine genuinely cannot act: when a fact from the discarded text has ALREADY been digested and propagated — merged into another entry, promoted a tier, seeded an arc or thread. Retracting the source entry does not unwind the derivatives. THAT is where human judgement earns its place, and it is the same shape as the existing import-conflict resolution and manual removal the user already has.

3. SO THE GATE IS A DEFERRED RECONCILIATION LANE, NOT A MODAL. Never interrupt mid-scene. Surface it where conflicts already get resolved. Trigger condition: a reader observes activeSwipeIndex has moved under text we previously captured AND that capture has downstream derivatives. Clean cases supersede silently; only entangled ones queue.

4. FREQUENCY MAKES THIS CHEAP. Live store: 4 regenerated messages in 9654 (0.04%, jaos). Of those, only the entangled subset would ever queue. The friction objection against a human gate largely dissolves at this rate — but so does the urgency, so build it after the deterministic path, not instead of it.

5. THE CASE THAT ACTUALLY NEEDS THE READER: swipe-back runs NO generation (7zro ordering proof), so no hook of any kind can observe it — not ours, not a perfect one upstream might grant. Two of the four live regenerations are exactly this shape (swipeCount=2, activeSwipeIndex=0). A periodic read of activeSwipeIndex is the ONLY mechanism that can catch it. Whatever else changes, something must keep reading.

title: Poller cannot detect regenerations — swipe never advances chat.lastMessageAt
description:
extractNewTurns() correctly detects a re-roll by comparing activeSwipeIndex on the same message id (poller.ts:208-218). But it is only ever reached for chats that selectChangedChats() already emitted, and that gate requires lastMessageAt > mark.lastMessageAt (poller.ts:180).

MEASURED on a live engine 2026-07-30: a regenerate rewrites the assistant message IN PLACE. Neither the message's createdAt nor the chat's lastMessageAt/updatedAt move.

  before swipe: lastMessageAt = 2026-07-30T22:44:52.046Z
  after 2 swipes: lastMessageAt = 2026-07-30T22:44:52.046Z  (unchanged)
  message: createdAt unchanged, activeSwipeIndex 0 -> 2, swipeCount -> 3, content changed

So a chat whose ONLY change is a swipe never passes the gate, and the regeneration branch is effectively unreachable on the poll path.

IMPACT: the user re-rolls a reply because they disliked it, and the Extender keeps remembering the DISCARDED text. Worse than missing it — the memory is actively wrong, and it is wrong in the direction the user explicitly rejected.

FIX: the engine turn-complete notification (MarinaraExtender-hkdq) fires on every regenerate, so it supplies the trigger the poll gate cannot. Route the notification into the SAME per-chat pass so extractNewTurns finally runs. This is why the notification is not merely a latency win — it closes a correctness hole the polling design structurally cannot close.
acceptance_criteria: A regenerate on a chat with no other activity results in exactly one ingested turn with regenerated=true, and no duplicate for the superseded text.
close_reason: Fixed on poller-fallback (9b99b1c). Push detector added: POST /api/engine/turn-complete -> handleTurnNotification(), sharing one watermark and a per-chat lock with the poll detector. 9 unit tests + smoke:turn-hook 8/8 against both a dev engine and the 94-chat live install. Acceptance met: a swipe with no other chat activity yields exactly one turn with regenerated=true, and a repeat notification or a turn the poller already took is a no-op.

title: Decision: BRANCH the engine for a first-class memory path (capture at the write path)
description:
DECIDED 2026-07-29. Branch Marinara Engine and put the memory path in first-class, rather than keep patching from outside.

WHY IT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT PREFERENCE. Engine v2.3.4 removed client extensions entirely. Capture at the WRITE PATH is the one place no extension API can ever reach, and organic memory formation (no human in the capture loop) is the project's whole thesis. So there is no external seam that satisfies the requirement. The poller is explicitly a live temp fix.

URGENT INDEPENDENT OF THIS DECISION: the current patch targets line 503 and line 754 BY NUMBER. Any upstream edit shifts them silently and yields wrong-position injection rather than a clean failure. Convert to content-anchored matching now. (Superseded later by the emitter, but not safe to defer.)

BRANCH, NOT FORK — corrected premise. An earlier reading held that the project is 'already forked' because --skip-update is the default boot, making the upstream-tracking tax a bill already unpaid. The author corrected this: upstream has simply been QUIET for a week, and the intent is to KEEP updating. So the divergence tax is live, and that changes the discipline:
- stay merge-shaped and rebase onto upstream regularly
- line-number fragility is worse, not better, because numbers WILL shift when updates resume
- 'narrow diff' is not enough; it must be REBASE-CHEAP

THREE LAWS (from Mari, 29.07):
1. Branch != rewrite. Touch ONLY the memory path; keep everything else upstream-shaped so the final diff reads as 'here is the memory feature'. A narrow diff is a mergeable gift; a sprawling one is a new engine nobody adopts.
   Sharpened: prefer NEW files over edits to existing ones, and make the unavoidable write-path insertion a SINGLE line delegating into a new module. Then a refactor costs one re-anchor, not a re-port.
2. Check the license before anything goes public. RESOLVED: Engine is AGPL-3.0, Extender is AGPL-3.0-only. Same licence; branching and modification are expressly permitted. Private household instance triggers no AGPL obligation (the network clause bites on conveying to users). Publishing is fine and imposes only obligations already met. Remaining check before PRESENTING (not before branching): whether Pasta-Devs requires a CLA.
3. Reference implementation, gift not gauntlet. Build for the house, offer the patch. Success condition is US running on it; the merge is a bonus.

WHAT FIRST-CLASS UNLOCKS: capture at the write path (event emitter replacing the line-number patch); the direct-query agent on the DM path only (standing ruling); which-world tags stamped at digest time; entity-first index native rather than bolted on. Every fix convicted this week wants to live there.

TEST-COVERAGE GAP TO CLOSE FIRST: 'divergence with CI is a controlled burn' holds only if CI covers the engine. The current 369 tests cover the SIDECAR exclusively; branch code starts at zero coverage, and an emitter at the write path is exactly the integration seam unit tests miss. The commit after the emitter must assert the emitter FIRES on a real turn.

Also: the Erica Test is not yet a CI fixture (it was run from throwaway scripts), and its control is still invalid — Erica had 80 entries, so she was never a negative control. A real one needs a name verified at zero hits (MarinaraExtender-h2os).

SEQUENCE: commit current work as the baseline -> branch -> replace line-number patch with a one-line emitter -> test the emitter fires -> move capture onto it -> keep the poller alive but FROZEN until the emitter proves out.
design:
GROUND TRUTH — verified 2026-07-30, replaces earlier assumptions.

RETRACTION: this issue previously carried 'URGENT: the current patch targets line 503 and line 754 BY NUMBER'. That was recorded from conversation and NOT verified. It is wrong. The engine install's working tree is CLEAN (only untracked tmp/ and uninstall.exe), and no reference to a line-503/754 patch exists anywhere in the Extender repo. There is no applied engine patch. Current integration is the poller only, which touches nothing in the engine. Treat the line-number urgency as withdrawn. (Same failure mode as errata v1: a claim certified into a tracked artefact without checking the store first.)

ENGINE INSTALL IS ALREADY A GIT REPO — this is the useful discovery.
  path:   C:\Users\holyk\AppData\Local\MarinaraEngine
  origin: https://github.com/Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Engine.git
  state:  detached HEAD at b7545a63 = tag v2.3.4 = origin/main
  refs:   origin/main and origin/staging both already fetched
  tree:   clean
  backup: C:\Users\holyk\AppData\Local\ME Backup\MarinaraEngine
So no fresh clone is strictly required, and branching is mechanically trivial. But see the location ruling below.

THE CENTRAL PLANNING FACT: staging is 650 COMMITS AHEAD of main (and 12 behind). The household runs v2.3.4, which IS main. The PR must target staging. For a feature touching the write path those are effectively different codebases — developing against v2.3.4 produces a diff that will not apply.

Staging cadence: roughly 8 commits on 2026-07-30 alone, issue numbers in the 4300s, heavily agent-driven (branches named agent/<issue>-<slug>, 'chore: start issue NNNN', 'fix: address CodeRabbit review'). Rebase often or drift compounds fast.

RELEASE SAFETY: v2.3.4 (2026-07-23) is flagged 'Latest and minimum safe version'; v2.3.2 and v2.3.3 carry security advisories marked do-not-install. So the household is correctly pinned and must NOT be casually moved onto unreleased staging.

LOCATION RULING: do NOT develop in the install directory. It is the live instance the Extender talks to on :7860, it sits in AppData\Local (a runtime path that installers and the launcher manage), and the launcher controls the checkout — an update would fight or discard local branches. Use a separate working clone under D:\Entertainment\Wip\Projects\Marinara-Engine, which gets normal project backup treatment and is free to break.

CONSEQUENCE FOR 'SUCCESS CONDITION IS US RUNNING ON IT': not immediately achievable, and that is sequencing rather than a compromise. The house stays on v2.3.4 + poller. Validation happens on a DEV engine instance from the staging branch, on a non-7860 port with a separate data dir so it cannot touch the household database.
