Migrate the household only when the feature is stable or merged.

FIRST REAL GATE: does staging build and run cleanly on this machine (pnpm install, pnpm check, .nvmrc node version)? If not, everything downstream is moot. Do this before any design work.

Layout for the write-path hunt: packages/{client,server,shared}. The turn-persistence point in packages/server is where the emitter goes.
notes:
SUPERSEDED IN APPROACH, NOT IN GOAL — 2026-08-02, Engine v2.4.0 sweep.

The load-bearing premise was: 'Engine v2.3.4 removed client extensions entirely. Capture at the WRITE PATH is the one place no extension API can ever reach, so there is no external seam.' That was TRUE at 2.3.4. It is FALSE at 2.4.0.

v2.4.0 ships a versioned capability-package API (Marinara-Agents, AGPL-3.0, API 1.7) whose server entrypoints include lifecycle hooks, prompt providers, and result handlers, with permissions agent-runtime/chat-read/chat-write/routes/storage/ui. API 1.2 commits chat-metadata writes atomically with an owner message, SWIPE, or spatial snapshot. That is a supported external seam at the write path — exactly what this issue said could not exist.

RULING: do not branch. Ship a package. Tracked as MarinaraExtender-7zro.

WHAT CARRIES OVER UNCHANGED:
- Three Laws still apply, re-aimed at the package: narrow surface, licence checked (both AGPL-3.0; CLA question now folded into lmcz), reference implementation as gift not gauntlet.
- 'Keep the poller alive but FROZEN until the new path proves out' — same discipline, now applied to the lifecycle hook instead of the emitter.
- 'The commit after the hook must assert it FIRES on a real turn.' Non-negotiable; a lifecycle hook is the same integration seam unit tests miss.
- Test-coverage gap: 369 tests still cover the sidecar exclusively. Package code starts at zero.
- Erica Test is still not a CI fixture and its control is still invalid (h2os).

Keep this issue OPEN until 7zro proves the hook fires; it holds the discipline the prototype inherits.

title: Unplayed-outline provenance stratum — outline stored at fidelity, excluded from every recall path
description:
Third stratum alongside played memory and the meta/desk lane. Outline is canon the author establishes out of character for an arc that has NOT been played. It must be storable at full fidelity so it can be built on, and it must never reach recall: a character able to 'remember' an unplayed scene is the exact confabulation machine the Erica Test exists to detect.

IMPLEMENTED 29.07:
- storage.ts: new EntryProvenance = 'played' | 'unplayed'. Optional field on both Entry and IndexEntry, mirrored onto the index row because the loader filters rows and never opens files during selection. Deliberately NOT a widened EntryStatus — same reasoning as supersededBy in the EntryStatus audit.
- loader.ts selectEntries: candidates filter adds provenance !== 'unplayed'.
- loader.ts coldRecall: unplayed entries skipped, so archival cannot launder outline back into hot via the rehydrate path.
- api.ts: POST accepts and validates provenance, rejecting anything outside the enum; value mirrored to entry file and index row.
- src/__tests__/unplayed-provenance.test.ts: 4 cases — excluded from Current even as sole perfect match; not resurrected by cold recall on a miss; absent provenance still recalls; explicit 'played' behaves as absent.

Verified: tsc clean, 369 tests pass, live server probed (accepts provenance:'unplayed', rejects 'bogus').

STILL OPEN:
- PATCH does not yet accept provenance, so an existing played entry cannot be reclassified as outline (or promoted from outline to played when its arc finally plays). Promotion outline -> played is the real workflow gap and needs a deliberate endpoint, not a field edit.
- no UI affordance; outline is invisible in the entries view and indistinguishable from played there.
- the digest/ingest path cannot yet stamp provenance, so anything captured from a live turn is implicitly played. Author-supplied outline must currently be POSTed explicitly.

title: Chronology lint at ingest — validate stored dates against participants' birth years
description:
Cheap mechanical guard against referent bleed (MarinaraExtender-hhdr). Pure arithmetic, no model in the resolution path, so it is legal under the deterministic-guard rule.

Rule: when an ingested entry carries an explicit date AND names participants with known birth years, compute each participant's age at that date. Flag when an event class requires adult agency and a participant would have been a minor.

Motivating case (ctopic-4mke2qmh): 'financial responsibility and death planning handled since 2013' with character Thomas (b.~2000) and a roster of characters who would have been 13 and 15. A birth-year check catches this instantly; the LLM digest did not, and produced fluent coherent prose around the impossibility.

Needs:
- birth years / current ages as first-class structured character data, not prose. Currently ages exist only as free text (utopic-4a2yq7cw: 'TC is a veteran in a 26-year-old body (was 15 in 1997, making him around 42 chronologically)') and must be parsed out or re-elicited.
- a date extractor over entry content (explicit years first; relative dates are out of scope for v1).
- an event-class heuristic for what implies adult agency — keep it conservative and deterministic; a flag should mean review, never auto-edit.
- flag surfaces to the author for adjudication. Never silently rewrite: the correct fix for the motivating case was striking the date entirely with NO replacement, which no automated repair would have chosen.

Depends on the which-world tagging in MarinaraExtender-76aw for the case where one name spans two worlds with different birth years.
notes:
CRITICAL CORRECTION 29.07 — the motivating example in this issue was WRONG, and the lint as specified would have produced a FALSE POSITIVE on a true fact.

Original framing: 'death-planning since 2013' with participants who would have been 13 and 15 is an impossible adult event, so a birth-year check catches it. That reasoning is withdrawn.

Actual canon: Erica is the same age as character Thomas (b.~2000). Her father was killed when she was 13 — that is 2013, arithmetic-clean. 'Death-planning since 2013' is TRUE of her: it dates from the Corps handing her a folded flag. The date was never invented and was never bleed.

So a chronology lint firing on '2013 + a 13-year-old' would have flagged a TRUE statement. The flag itself is not useless — a 13-year-old in a death-planning claim IS worth a human look — but the correct resolution was to REATTACH the date to its real referent, not strike it. An auto-repairer would have deleted true canon.

Hardens two requirements:
1. flag-for-review only, never auto-edit. Already specified; now empirically justified rather than merely prudent.
2. the flag text must not assert the date is wrong. It must say 'date implies age N for participant P — verify referent', because the likeliest fault is a MIS-ATTACHED true date, not a fabricated one.

See MarinaraExtender-hhdr for the failure species this actually belongs to (chimera fusion).

title: Failure taxonomy head #3: content corruption at digest — referent bleed and witness-to-participant promotion
description:
Third distinct failure class, alongside capture gap (lara) and retrieval invisibility (the scorer). The digest writes content that is internally coherent but factually wrong, so nothing downstream can detect it — unlike a gap or a miss, a corrupt entry retrieves perfectly and asserts a falsehood.

Two mechanisms observed in ctopic-4mke2qmh:

1. REFERENT BLEED across the user/character membrane. The digest resolved a date against the wrong world: 2013 belongs to TC-the-user (b.1982, ~31 then), not to character Thomas (b.~2000, 13 then). TC and Thomas are distinct entities sharing a name; the digest treated them as one and produced an adult pact dated to a character's childhood.

2. WITNESS -> PARTICIPANT PROMOTION. First-person lane summaries flatten roles. Mari witnessed the sister/Erica pact; the digest rewrote her as a party to it. The relational framing ('the women who love him have been managing his future') survived intact and made the wrong roster read as coherent.

Detection is the hard part — both errors produced fluent, plausible text. The only signal was an implausibility joke in-scene. House rule coined: AN IMPLAUSIBILITY JOKE IS AN UNFILED BUG REPORT (Mari mocked the 2013 date and filed it as flavor rather than as an error).

Mitigations tracked separately: which-world tags (MarinaraExtender-76aw extension) and chronology lint at ingest.
design:
SPECIES NAMED 29.07: CHIMERA FUSION. This is the precise mechanism, and it is narrower and nastier than 'referent bleed'.

The digest welds several individually TRUE fragments into one FALSE composite. Every part has a real referent; only the JOINS are invented. That is why it reads as fluent, survives review, and defeats fragment-level fact-checking — there is no false atom to find.

Worked example, ctopic-4mke2qmh. The corrupt entry read 'financial responsibility and death planning handled by her [Mari] and Erica since 2013'. Decomposed:
  TRUE  — Erica has practised death-planning since 2013 (her father was killed when she was 13).
  TRUE  — a continuity-of-life pact exists between Thomas's sister Becky and Erica.
  TRUE  — it was kept from Thomas.
  TRUE  — Mari was present when it surfaced.
  FALSE — the joins: Mari as PARTICIPANT rather than witness, and 2013 as the start date of a MARI+ERICA arrangement rather than of Erica's own practice.

Diagnostic consequence: chimera fusion cannot be caught by verifying claims individually, which is exactly what a naive fact-check does. Detection has to test the RELATIONS — who did what, to whom, starting when — not the facts. A composite of true parts scores 100% on atom-level verification.

Also invalidates the first repair attempt: errata v1 read the impossible date as fabrication and STRUCK it, destroying true canon. Errata v2 reattached it. The repair instinct for corruption must be REATTACH BEFORE DELETE — a wrong-looking detail in a chimera is usually a true detail wired to the wrong node.

Sub-mechanisms retained: witness->participant promotion in first-person lane summaries; referent bleed across the user/character membrane (TC b.1982 vs character Thomas b.~2000).

title: No coreference between an entity's names — first-name and surname cues reach disjoint entry sets
description:
relevanceScore does bag-of-words token overlap, so 'Erica' and 'Cathmore' are unrelated tokens. An entry whose summary says only 'Erica' is unreachable by a 'Cathmore' cue and vice versa — no weighting scheme can match a token that is not present.

Measured over live index summaries:
  Mari  — 5 name both, 7 name Erica only, 1 names Cathmore only. A bare 'Cathmore' cue reaches 6 of 13.
  Priya — 8 name both, 9 name Erica only, 1 names Cathmore only. A bare 'Cathmore' cue reaches 9 of 18.

So roughly half the retrievable material is invisible to a surname-only cue, and the same in reverse for a first-name-only cue.

src/aliases.ts already implements exactly the needed matching (normalizeLabel, jaroWinkler, tokenContainment — 'Chandrasekaran' subset of 'Dr. Chandrasekaran'), but it is a SPEAKER-routing table consulted by api/facts/identity/threads/holding-pool/arc-promotion. loader.ts imports it zero times, so retrieval gets none of it. data/aliases.yaml holds only characters who speak (aurora, Priya, Mari, Lara); Erica is mentioned but never speaks, so she has no record and would never acquire one under the current learner.

Fix direction: extract entities at INGEST, while original capitalization still survives (relevanceScore lowercases at loader.ts:89, destroying the proper-noun signal before scoring). Store an explicit entities/aliases field per entry holding every surface form, link them, and score against it. That solves surname/first-name coreference and the body-invisibility in MarinaraExtender-tp5 in one pass, and needs a mention-entity table distinct from the speaker-alias table.
notes:
WORLD RULE, stated by TC 2026-08-04. The first concrete disambiguation rule for the doctrine amendment, and it is mechanizable — just not from the name.

TC: "Thomas Collier is the different character, and generally referred to as Thomas. Has on occasion been referred to as TC. Which is the model having some confusion, because you aren't supposed to blend personas like this. Unless TC is in an RP, it would go with the Thomas Lowe USER box. Most things in the RP section should be under Thomas Collier."

THE RULE:
  Thomas Collier  = RP CHARACTER. Default referent for bare "Thomas" inside RP.
  Thomas Lowe / Thomas Charles Lowe / TC Lowe / TC = THE USER. Default referent outside RP.
  Resolution is by CONTEXT (is this an RP?), not by surface form. The name alone cannot decide, which is exactly why no lexical method has worked.
  "TC" applied to the character is a DEFECT — persona blending by the model, not a legitimate alias.

MEASURED BLAST RADIUS (2026-08-04): far smaller than the alias-collision degree suggested. Of the whole store, 828 entries mention "TC" as a word, 47 mention Collier, 25 mention Lowe. Only 2 entries contain BOTH TC and Collier; 5 contain TC and Lowe; Collier and Lowe NEVER co-occur.

That last fact matters twice over. It means the blend has not spread — but it also means the store holds NO evidence that would let any process distinguish the two Thomases. The discriminator has to come from outside the text.

ONE CONCRETE CORRUPTION FOUND, worth a human check:
  characters/professor_mari — "TC's sons: Henry Warren and Malcolm Bradley Collier"
attributes the CHARACTER's sons to the USER. This is the ctopic-4mke2qmh failure class caught in a second instance.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DESIGN: slice 1's ambiguity cap currently SUPPRESSES the thomas cluster (degree 11), which is safe but wrong — Thomas Lowe / Thomas Charles Lowe / TC Lowe are one real person and should resolve together. Suppression is the right default only until the world tag exists. Two things follow:
  - The user's own identity should be DECLARED, not inferred. It is knowable, stable, and the single highest-value entity in the store.
  - RP-vs-not is the world discriminator to implement first, because TC has now stated it as a rule rather than a preference.

title: relevanceScore normalizes by summary length — specific memories lose to short generic ones
description:
loader.ts:87 returns hit / words.size — the fraction of the SUMMARY's words present in the cue. Dividing by summary length means an information-dense summary is penalized: matching one proper noun out of 15 meaningful words scores 0.067, while a 4-word throwaway sharing a common verb scores 0.250.

Simulated against the real scorer over the live indexes (Mari 6832 live entries, Priya 2722; character budget 2000 tokens = roughly 10-20 slots):

cue 'Hey, do you remember Erica?' — Mari: best Erica entry scores 0.111; only 1 of her 7 summary-reachable Erica entries clears the 0.1 credit threshold. It is beaten by 'wants to remember past crimes' (0.250) and 'will soon remember past actions' (0.250) — the cue's VERB outranks the entity name. The single Erica entry that does surface is the meta entry about naming the project 'THE ERICA TEST', not any in-fiction memory of her. Character answers from the test scaffolding, which reads as confabulated recognition.

Longer cues degrade further: 'What do you remember about Erica Cathmore, the Marine?' puts 95 Mari entries over threshold and the top 5 are all noise ('He is meticulous about cleanliness', 'One fact about the user'). More cue words = more spurious matches = entity signal drowns.

Priya scores better (0.167-0.286, 12/14 clearing on the rich cue) purely because her summaries happen to name Erica more often — matching the observed 'neither remembered her very much', Priya partial, Mari near-zero.

Fix direction: stop normalizing by summary length, or use IDF-style weighting so rare proper nouns dominate common verbs. Consider a rarity floor that lets a single high-specificity token carry a match. Depends on MarinaraExtender-tp5.
design:
PRIORITISE THIS ABOVE THE ENTITY LAYER. Evidence from 29.07: two freshly written entries (utopic-n9gjyuap Becky canon, utopic-i7p5bja8 Jessica resolution) were authored with deliberately entity-dense summaries to be maximally retrievable, and STILL lose.

Simulated against Mari's live index:
  cue 'what's your sister's name again?' -> neither new entry reaches the top 40.
     #1 'name is Mari' (0.500)
     #2 'The user does not remember the name of their sister' (0.400)
     A memory recording that the author FORGOT the name outranks the entry containing the name.
  cue 'remind me who Becky is' -> Becky canon ranks #6 (0.083), beaten by the Jessica entry (0.111)
     which only mentions Becky inside a NEGATION ('not Becky'). Negative mentions outrank positive records.
  cue 'tell me about the pact between Becky and Erica' -> top 3 are 'He is meticulous about cleanliness'
     (0.333), 'One fact about the user' (0.250), 'Statement about established knowledge' (0.250).

Conclusion: summaries cannot be written well enough to escape this bug. Density is precisely what hit/words.size punishes, so the better-documented a memory is, the less retrievable. This is structural, not an authoring problem.

SEQUENCING: the entity layer (tp5/76aw) does NOT fix the motivating cue. 'what's your sister's name again?' contains no proper noun, so an entity channel never fires — only de-normalised ranking surfaces the answer. Fix ranking first; the entity layer is additive, not a substitute.
notes:
FIXED 29.07. Two-part change in loader.ts, both in relevanceScore.

1. Dropped length normalisation. hit/words.size became saturating evidence accumulation, 1-exp(-0.357*evidence). Detail is no longer punished.

2. Added PROPER_NOUN_WEIGHT=2.5 on capitalised mid-summary tokens. This is the part that mattered. A first attempt with evidence-accumulation ALONE regressed 3 of 5 measured cues: removing the length divisor collapsed discrimination, since thousands of entries tie at exactly one match and recency then decides. Length was only ever a crude proxy for term specificity — terse summaries look focused because they carry little but their subject. Weighting the subject directly is what was actually meant, and capitalisation already marks it; the scorer was lowercasing that signal away before matching.

RELEVANCE_CREDIT_THRESHOLD moved 0.1 -> 0.29 to sit just under the one-ordinary-match score (0.2999), preserving the original summoned-vs-present semantics on the new scale. It is a threshold ON the score; the two must move together.

A/B against Mari's live 6841-entry index, greedy fill into the real 2000-token budget:
  'what's your sister's name again?'          corrected pact  #65  -> #1   now loads
  'remind me who Becky is'                    Becky canon     #6   -> #3   loads
  'tell me about the pact between Becky/Erica' corrected pact #208 -> #2   now loads
                                              Becky canon     #368 -> #21
  'Hey, do you remember Erica?'               corrected pact  #46  -> #2   now loads

Verification: tsc clean, 365 tests pass (2 new files' worth added in relevance-ranking.test.ts), no existing test perturbed.

RESIDUAL GAP (not fixed here, belongs to MarinaraExtender-76aw): the cue 'what's your sister's name again?' still does not surface utopic-n9gjyuap, which holds the answer. That cue contains no name, so no amount of ranking helps — resolving 'sister' to Rebecca needs a relation link. Ranking got the pact entry to #1 on that cue, but the pact entry does not contain the name.

KNOWN HEURISTIC WART: an all-caps word collects name weight (the errata summary's 'THOMAS'S SISTER' is why it wins that cue). Emphasis is not a proper noun. Harmless today and arguably correlates with importance, but it should be revisited when the real entity field lands.

title: Retrieval scores entry.summary only — content/body is never searchable
description:
loader.ts relevanceScore(e.summary, recentText) is called at loader.ts:173 (hot ranking) and loader.ts:241 (cold recall). entry.content is never scored in either path, so any entity named only in the body is unreachable by topic — it can ride in on recency but can never be summoned by its own name.

Measured on the Erica Test corpus: of 80 entries across Mari + Priya whose bodies mention Erica/Cathmore, only 21 name her in the summary. 59/80 (74%) are retrieval-invisible. Mari is worst: 37 of 44 unreachable, and only 2 of her 29 June entries are reachable.

This is the primary cause of the 2026-07-28 Erica blank. It was recorded as a true negative (see utopic-aewhfnv1) but Mari had held Erica material since 2026-06-16.

Fix direction: score summary + content (weight summary higher), or extract an entity/alias index at ingest so proper nouns in the body are matchable. Cold recall needs the same fix or a rehydrate still cannot find it.
notes:
SHIPPED + BACKFILLED 2026-08-04, commit adacc07. Backup taken first (22972 files, marinara-extender-backups/backup-2026-08-04T05-10-54-576Z-63nc).

BACKFILL RESULT, live store: 67 scopes, 14679 rows examined, 9387 updated. Re-run immediately after changed 0 rows, confirming idempotence. professor_mari now carries bodyTerms on 6279 of 7444 rows (84%).

CORRECTION TO MY OWN ESTIMATE: I predicted ~9% index growth from a names-only harvest that excluded everything already in the summary. The sentence-case fix deliberately KEEPS names the summary holds as ordinary words, which is more terms, so the real cost is 23% -- professor_mari's index went 2529K to 3108K. Still worth it for 43% to 84% reachability, but the 9% figure in the design note is wrong and should not be quoted.

NO LOST UPDATES: row count went 7441 to 7444 across the run, i.e. three entries the sidecar ingested concurrently survived. Nothing was clobbered.

657 rows still report 'entry file unreadable' -- the __professor_mari__ ghost scope, filed as pe1c. The backfill skips and counts them rather than recording 'could not look' as 'has no names'.

ACTIVATION: the running sidecar (pid 32188, started 23:49) predates the build (00:07), so it is executing OLD code and is not yet consulting bodyTerms. The DATA is in place and old code preserves the field on rewrite (rows are spread, not rebuilt), so nothing is lost meanwhile -- but the retrieval improvement does not take effect until the sidecar restarts.

RESIDUAL: 15 of the 99 Erica-corpus entries stay unreachable because the mention is never capitalised anywhere in the body. Needs 76aw (entity/alias coreference), not a larger term list.
close_reason: Shipped adacc07, backfilled across the live store (9387 rows, 67 scopes). Reachability on the Erica corpus 43% to 84%. Residual 15/99 need name coreference (76aw), which this unblocks.

title: Poller slice C: write the memory block back via the engine lorebook API
description:
Replaces the extension writeMemoryToLorebook. Ports the extension logic server-side; the mechanism itself is unchanged, so this is a port not a redesign.

MUST PRESERVE (these were hard-won in the extension, see references/extension.md):
- Force the lorebook tokenBudget to 16384 on create AND heal it on every lookup. Engine default is 2048 and it SILENTLY DROPS entries over it (e87) - this is the single most recurring silent-failure source in the whole integration.
- Nuke-and-recreate exactly two constant entries per character: Memory System - Instructions (order 0) and Memory System - Active Context (order 1); constant true, keys [], role system, noVector true.
- Serialize writes (the _lorebookWriteChain mutex equivalent). Concurrent refreshes each seeing an empty lorebook is what leaves it empty/partial exactly when generation runs.

CARRIES OVER (not fixed by this migration, unlike the dropped proxy plan): e87 (over-budget silent drop), axu (duplicate Extender lorebooks), s19 (stale lorebookIdCache). Re-verify all three against the server-side port - the causes may differ now that a browser is not involved.

INJECTION IS ONE TURN BEHIND, by design: written after turn N, injected by the engine at turn N+1. Same as the extension always behaved, so no regression - but do not promise pre-generation injection on this path (only the proxy path can do that).

VERIFICATION TOOL: POST /api/generate/dryRun (routes/generate/dry-run-route.ts, still present) runs the full pipeline with no side effects and returns the ASSEMBLED PROMPT with returnPrompt:true. Use it to prove the memory block actually reaches the prompt instead of trusting the lorebook write returned 200.
notes:
CODE COMPLETE + LIVE VERIFIED 2026-07-23 on branch poller-fallback. 12/12 live checks passed against TC running engine; 21 unit tests; suite 296 -> 317.

BUILT: memory-extender/src/lorebook-writer.ts — splitMemoryBlock, lorebookNameFor, ensureLorebook, writeMemoryToLorebook, syncMemoryToLorebook (the entry point the poller should call).

PORTED FAITHFULLY from the extension: forced tokenBudget 16384 set on create AND healed on lookup (e87 — engine default is 2048 and it silently drops entries above it); nuke-and-recreate exactly two constant/system/noVector entries (Instructions order 0, Active Context order 1, Active disabled when content is empty); unlock-before-delete (a locked entry refuses deletion and silently survives).

FIX vs the extension (axu — duplicate Extender lorebooks): the extension serialized only the entry WRITE, so two concurrent refreshes could each look up, each find nothing, and each create a lorebook. syncMemoryToLorebook now serializes the WHOLE ensure+write cycle, keyed PER CHARACTER so unrelated characters still run in parallel. The chain also swallows rejections so one failed write does not poison every later write for that character (unit-tested).

LIVE RESULTS: guard | create | tokenBudget=16384 forced | exactly 2 entries | both by name | entries persisted as constant | content round-tripped | second pass reuses same lorebook | still exactly 2 after rewrite | content REPLACED not appended | 3 concurrent syncs -> exactly 1 lorebook | still 2 entries after concurrent syncs | cleanup.

SAFETY NOTE FOR ANYONE RUNNING THIS: this code is DESTRUCTIVE — it deletes every entry in the target lorebook. TC install has THREE REAL Extender lorebooks with live memory (Professor Mari, Dr. Mari Zielinska, Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran). scripts/lorebook-smoke.ts therefore only ever uses a SYNTHETIC characterId (me-smoketest-synthetic-character), verifies no real character collides BEFORE writing, and deletes every lorebook belonging to that synthetic id on the way out. Never point it at a real character.

TOOLING: npm run smoke:lorebook.

STILL NOT WIRED: nothing calls syncMemoryToLorebook yet — that is slice 23i, which must resolve identity + loadContext to produce the memory block.

title: Poller slice B: detect a finished turn and trigger ingestion
description:
Replaces the extension POST /api/process-turn call. Feeds the EXISTING ingestion pipeline; no new memory logic.

NO PUSH SIGNAL EXISTS (investigated 2026-07-23, negative result): the engine has no event surface for message-saved. Its SSE endpoints are generate/sse.ts (bound to the callers own request), sidecar.routes.ts (the engines OWN llama.cpp/MLX local-model runtime, a NAME COLLISION with us, unrelated), and import/backup progress. The Discord webhook mirror cannot be pointed at us: chats.routes.ts rejects any URL not starting with https://discord.com/api/webhooks/.

PREFERRED TRIGGER: fs.watch on the engine file store (DATA_DIR/storage, file-native JSON since v2.3.0) as a near-instant local signal, then read the authoritative data over REST. Push-like latency, no HTTP poll load. RISK: on-disk layout is engine-internal and can change, and atomic-write/rename patterns make events chatty. Use it as a TRIGGER ONLY, never as a data source, with an interval poll as the always-correct fallback.
FALLBACK: interval poll (fast while a chat is open, backing off when idle).

BIG SIMPLIFICATION vs the proxy path: scope resolution is FREE here. The engine hands us chatId and characterId directly, so proxy slice w8g (prompt-tail matching + fingerprint cache) is NOT needed on this path.

EDGE CASES: regenerated turns must supersede not duplicate; partial/cancelled generations must not ingest; group scenes ingest per participant; do not re-ingest history on sidecar restart (persist a per-chat high-water mark).
notes:
CODE COMPLETE + LIVE VERIFIED 2026-07-23 on branch poller-fallback. 7/7 live checks; 29 unit tests; suite 317 -> 346.

DESIGN CHANGE vs the original plan (fs.watch): rejected in favour of polling GET /api/chats. Every chat carries lastMessageAt, so ONE cheap call says which chats moved and only those get a message fetch. fs.watch would be lower latency but binds us to the engine internal on-disk layout and its atomic write-and-rename pattern makes events noisy. lastMessageAt is a stable public field that answers the question directly. fs.watch stays available later as a pure TRIGGER that reads through this same path — a latency optimisation, not a different design.
MEASURED: a quiet tick over TC real 91-chat library costs 10-13ms. Baselining all 91 cost 258ms with ZERO per-chat message fetches.

LIVE ENGINE FACTS VERIFIED (these drove the design):
- GET /chats/:id/messages?limit=N returns the NEWEST N, ascending. UNBOUNDED IT RETURNS EVERYTHING (195 messages on a real chat) — the limit is not optional.
- Messages carry their OWN characterId, so group scenes name the actual speaker per message; we never guess from the chat.
- Regeneration is a SWIPE: activeSwipeIndex/swipeCount change on the SAME message id. The engine re-rolls in place rather than appending. That is the supersede signal.
- Conversation-mode chats use a characterIds ARRAY, not a scalar characterId.

BUILT: memory-extender/src/poller.ts. Pure, directly-tested core (selectChangedChats, extractNewTurns, watermarkFrom, isAssistantTurn, getChatCharacterId) plus pollOnce/startPoller/stopPoller. Watermarks persist to poller-state.yaml through mutateYamlFile (serialized + atomic per project rule — never a raw YAML write).

EDGE CASES HANDLED: first sighting BASELINES without ingesting (otherwise a fresh install replays all 91 chats history at once — verified live: 0 ingested, 91 tracked); watermark advances even when the new message is a user turn, so the same tail is not re-read forever; overlapping ticks are skipped so a slow engine cannot double-ingest; a failed message fetch skips that chat only; a throwing onTurn never aborts the pass.

BUG FOUND BY UNIT TEST: defaulting a missing activeSwipeIndex to -1 made every unchanged message compare unequal to a recorded index of 0, so the same turn would be re-flagged as regenerated on EVERY tick — duplicating memory indefinitely. Fixed to require the field on both sides before claiming a regeneration; two regression tests pin it.

LIVE PROOF OF DETECTION: rolling one chat watermark back behind its own last message made the poller detect a REAL assistant turn from real data — chat "Dr Z", characterId Po_H0vIbkPUMbZmt7aUoQ, which matches the existing "Marinara Extender — Dr. Mari Zielinska" lorebook exactly. So detection and write-back resolve to the same character. Not re-detected on the following pass.

TOOLING: npm run smoke:poller (read-only; uses a throwaway data dir, attaches no onTurn, writes nothing back to the engine).

STILL NOT WIRED: nothing calls startPoller yet, and onTurn is not connected to ingestion + syncMemoryToLorebook. That integration is the next step.

title: Poller slice A: engine API client (read chats/messages, write lorebooks) from the sidecar
description:
Foundation for the poller path (epic hq7). The sidecar talks to Marinara Engine server-to-server over localhost.

VERIFIED ENABLER: engine CSRF is a STATIC header, not a per-session token. CSRF_HEADER = x-marinara-csrf, CSRF_HEADER_VALUE = 1 (packages/shared/src/constants/security.ts), and loopback origins are auto-trusted. So a non-browser client can mutate the engine API by sending that header from 127.0.0.1.

BUILD:
- Engine base URL config (default http://127.0.0.1:7860), separate from the proxy upstream vars.
- Client that sends x-marinara-csrf on mutations; handles the CSRF_* error codes (CSRF_ORIGIN_NOT_TRUSTED / CSRF_REFERER_NOT_TRUSTED / CSRF_CROSS_SITE / CSRF_MISSING_HEADER) with actionable messages rather than a bare 403.
- Reads: GET /api/chats, GET /api/chats/:id/messages. NOTE (existing bd memory, already verified against source): that endpoint returns ALL messages by default; pagination is opt-in via ?limit=N&before=cursor. Do not fetch full history every poll.
- Writes: /api/lorebooks CRUD for the memory block.
- Handle engine-not-running and engine-behind-Basic-Auth gracefully (docs/REMOTE_ACCESS.md documents BASIC_AUTH_USER/PASS + IP_ALLOWLIST).

Also the read channel bos (lorebook import) and chat digest/import have been waiting for.
notes:
LIVE VERIFIED END-TO-END 2026-07-23 — 10 passed, 0 failed against TC running engine (read + write round-trip).

REAL BUG FOUND BY THE LIVE TEST (this is why it exists): engineFetch set content-type: application/json on EVERY request, including bodyless ones. Fastify rejects that with "Body cannot be empty when content-type is set to application/json", so EVERY DELETE was a 400. GET tolerates it, which is exactly why the stubbed unit tests sailed past it - they asserted the body was absent but never checked the header.

IMPACT IF IT HAD SHIPPED: slice lxp nuke-and-recreate cycle depends on deleting entries. Every delete would have failed, so stale memory entries would accumulate forever while the create half kept working - memory would look like it was updating while silently growing garbage. Found before a single line of lxp was written.

FIX: only set content-type when init.body !== undefined. Two regression tests pin it (no content-type without a body, content-type present with one). The CSRF header stays unconditional.

FINAL LIVE RESULT: engine reachable | listChats 91 | listCharacters 9 | listLorebooks 6 | listMessages limit honoured | createLorebook | patchLorebook tokenBudget read back as 16384 (the e87 assertion - engine default is 2048 and it silently drops entries above it) | createLorebookEntry | listLorebookEntries | unlock+delete entry | lorebook cleaned up.

Also cleaned up the orphaned lorebook lIUvrw8Pdi2eWvO0tqbu9 left by the first failed run (DELETE returned 204; listLorebooks back to 6).

Suite 296 passing (30 in engine-client.test.ts).

title: Proxy slice 1: faithful streaming passthrough at /v1/chat/completions
description:
FOUNDATION SLICE. Marinara must be able to chat through the sidecar with ZERO behaviour change before any memory logic is added (validate before scaling).

The existing handleChatCompletions is the nqy Rewrite Assistant relay and is unsuitable: hardcodes stream:false, rewrites body.model to the sidecar default, drops most sampling params, uses the sidecar API key.

REQUIREMENTS:
- SSE streaming passthrough (Marinara streams; non-negotiable). Pipe upstream bytes through unmodified.
- Faithful param forwarding: model, top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, stop, seed, tools, tool_choice, response_format, max_tokens/max_completion_tokens, n, logit_bias.
- Forward the CALLER Authorization header upstream so API keys stay in engine config and never land in the sidecar.
- Upstream base URL configurable, separate from the Extender analysis-model config (that stays for memory analysis + Rewrite Assistant).
- Route the Rewrite Assistant relay to its own path so the two uses stop sharing a handler.
- Errors and non-200s pass through with status + body intact.

DONE WHEN: Marinara Custom connection -> sidecar, a normal roleplay turn streams identically to a direct connection. No memory involved yet.
notes:
ANTHROPIC COVERAGE ADDED 2026-07-23 (commit e20fb47). Slice 1 originally only handled OpenAI-shaped providers; Anthropic speaks POST /v1/messages with x-api-key and its own SSE shape, so the OpenAI route would have 404d against api.anthropic.com.

KEY FINDING (verified against engine source, not assumed): Marinara native Anthropic connection has a USER-EDITABLE baseUrl. packages/shared/src/constants/providers.ts LOCAL_AUTH_PROVIDERS = [openai_chatgpt, claude_subscription, grok_subscription] are the only ones that hide it; baseUrl is a generic per-connection field in connection.schema.ts. anthropic.defaultBaseUrl = https://api.anthropic.com/v1, modelsEndpoint /models, apiKeyHeader x-api-key, usesAuthHeader false.

=> NO OpenAI->Anthropic translation layer needed. Proxy speaks Anthropic on both sides, pure passthrough. Avoids owning message-shape conversion, SSE event translation, tool-call and stop-reason mapping permanently.

ROUTES: POST /anthropic/v1/messages (+ /anthropic/messages alias), GET /anthropic/v1/models. Engine appends /messages to baseUrl, so the connection is set to http://127.0.0.1:3001/anthropic/v1.
CONFIG: MARINARA_EXTENDER_ANTHROPIC_UPSTREAM (default https://api.anthropic.com).

DESIGN NOTE FOR SLICE 3 (rid): Anthropic takes `system` as a TOP-LEVEL request parameter, not a role:system message. Injecting memory there is CLEANER than the OpenAI shape (append to / create body.system, which accepts a bare string or an array of text blocks) - no messages-array splicing. Slice 3 must implement injection per format; the seams are marked in proxy.ts.

SUPPORT GOTCHA TO EXPECT (upstream constraint, NOT a proxy bug - the proxy passes 400s through verbatim so the real message is visible): on Opus 4.7/4.8 and Fable 5 the Anthropic API REJECTS temperature/top_p/top_k with 400, and rejects last-assistant-turn prefill with 400. Roleplay frontends commonly send both. If TC hits this, it is the engine sending unsupported params for the chosen model, not the sidecar.

Tests now 26 in proxy.integration.test.ts; suite 266 passing. Live smoke test still outstanding for BOTH routes.

title: Stateful entity-state lane + epistemic injection (who-knows-what, incl. 'hiding')
description:
This bead builds a substrate, then proves it with epistemic. The deliverable is two things welded together: (a) a new stateful entity-state lane, and (b) epistemic knowledge as its first rider — with INJECTION as the load-bearing piece.

THE LANE (the reusable substrate). Today ambient.ts produces append-only flat facts. This lane is different in kind: per-entity entries, KEYED (epistemic keys on character->fact), that evolve over time by SUPERSEDING their own prior entries rather than appending a contradictory flat fact, and that feed the existing promotion path (dedup -> apply-gate -> judge-consensus -> tiers). It sits alongside ambient/facts, not inside them. Distinct from reconcile-queue: reconcile resolves contradictions between facts that shouldn't conflict; this lane models state that is SUPPOSED to change. Open question: does update.ts already give a supersession primitive to build on, or is that net-new? Check before designing.

FIRST RIDER — epistemic stance, keyed character->fact: knows / suspects / believes_false / unaware / hiding. Extracted at scene breaks.

THE ACTUAL CAPABILITY IS INJECTION, NOT STORAGE. Anyone can store a hiding tag. The feature is that the responding character's knows + hiding entries are injected into the memory block so the model sustains the deception and maintains dramatic irony across turns — it keeps guarding the secret turn over turn instead of forgetting it next reply. This injection path is the bead that must be airtight; the tracking is the easy half.

WHY CONSENSUS-GATING IS LOAD-BEARING HERE SPECIFICALLY. A falsely-extracted hiding fact is not clutter — it makes the model lie about the wrong thing, or guard a secret that was never real. That is a categorically worse failure than a dropped fact. Routing epistemic extraction through judge-consensus + apply-gate is therefore not a nice-to-have; it is the entire reason this foundation beats Smart-Memory's ungated epistemic.js. Gate hard, default to NOT asserting a hiding fact under doubt.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Lane substrate exists, keyed, with supersede-prior semantics, feeding the promotion path.
- Epistemic entries extracted at scene breaks and consensus-gated before they can land.
- Injection wired into the memory block under its own small token budget.
- Demonstrable across >=N turns: the model maintains a hiding secret and does not leak it; a single-pass false hiding extraction is gated out, not injected.

Blocks MarinaraExtender-d06 (Smart-Memory import) for the epistemic category. Evidence: Smart-Memory epistemic.js (5 stances, injects hiding); our gap at storage.ts:12, loader.ts:106, ambient.ts (flat append-only).
notes: Design enrichment (Doc_3_NextGen Slice 4): represent facts as SUBJECT-PREDICATE-OBJECT (SPO) triples to enable PRECISE contradiction detection (same subject AND same predicate AND different object AND overlapping valid-time), vs the current LEXICAL correction-signature in dedup.ts which misses semantic contradictions with low word overlap. SPO structure is the missing piece that makes FR2/FR3 reconcile precise rather than lexical, and epistemic who-knows-what facts are naturally SPO. See docs/Doc_3_NextGen_assessment.md Slice 4.

title: [feature] Better sidecar management — replace the two-console-window launcher+watchdog model
description:
PROBLEM (UX/UI): Launching the Extender opens a console window (start.ps1: the launcher + watchdog), which in turn spawns a SECOND console window for the sidecar itself (start.ps1 ~L131-133, Start-Process powershell.exe running npm). A console window opening another console window is poor from both a UI and UX standpoint — two terminal windows for one background service.

CURRENT ARCHITECTURE:
- start.ps1 = visible launcher window. Runs ready-checks, then a watchdog loop (~L451) that probes port+health and calls Restart-Sidecar (~L182) on death.
- The sidecar runs in its own separate PowerShell window (Start-Process), teeing stdout to logs/sidecar.log.
- Interactive hotkeys in the launcher window: [R]estart [L]og [A]uto-start [Q]uit.

GOAL: one clean way to run and supervise the sidecar — no stacked console windows. Options to weigh (this issue is to DESIGN + pick, not pre-commit):
- A) Single window: run the sidecar as a child process INSIDE the launcher window (no second Start-Process), keep the watchdog + hotkeys, pipe output to the log. Smallest change; removes the second window.
- B) System tray app: hidden background process + a tray icon with Restart/Open setup/View log/Quit. Best everyday UX; needs a tray host (e.g. a tiny C#/WinForms or a packaged Node tray).
- C) Windows service / scheduled task: true background, survives logout, auto-restart via Windows. Most robust supervision; harder install, no obvious window for non-technical users, weaker cross-platform story.
- D) Packaged tray/menubar binary so it's cross-platform from the start.

CONSTRAINTS / NOTES:
- Non-technical users are a target audience (see launcher copy) — whatever replaces it must stay one-click and make 'is it running / how do I restart' obvious.
- A proper supervisor should also capture crash diagnostics better than the current single-file tee (ties into the silent-crash bug filed alongside this).
- Watchdog tuning already learned the hard way (port-bound vs health, ~L501-509) — preserve that logic in any rework.

RELATED: MarinaraExtender-c40 (macOS/Linux start.sh launcher — a cross-platform tray/menubar would subsume part of this), MarinaraExtender-4o2 (remote/LAN access — a service model interacts with binding choices), and the silent-crash bug filed in this same session.
notes: PROMOTED TO P1 2026-07-23 by the inference-proxy migration (epic hq7). The two-console launcher/watchdog model is now user-facing reliability for CHAT ITSELF, not just memory - see 073. Restart behaviour, crash visibility and startup ordering all matter more once Marinara depends on the sidecar to generate at all.

title: [bug] Sidecar process dies repeatedly & silently — watchdog relaunches it (~30 deaths in current log)
description:
SYMPTOM: The Memory Extender sidecar keeps crashing. The start.ps1 watchdog brings it back (working as designed), but it should not be dying this often. User flagged the frequency as the real problem.

EVIDENCE (memory-extender/logs/sidecar.log, single day 2026-06-21): 90 session-starts, 65 'watchdog ... relaunching' lines; of the watchdog deaths, ALL 30 distinct reasons are 'process gone (no listener on port N)' — i.e. the Node process's port listener vanished entirely before the watchdog acted.

KEY DIAGNOSTIC: the crashes are ABRUPT/SILENT. Crash breadcrumbs (index.ts ~L192) only exist as 15x 'signal' + 15x 'process exit' — and those come from the watchdog's own Stop-Sidecar cleanup / deliberate restarts, NOT from the crashes. There are ZERO uncaughtException / unhandledRejection breadcrumbs. So no JS-level exception is being thrown/caught — the process is dying by a path Node's handlers can't catch.

LIKELY CAUSES (unconfirmed): native fault (a native dependency segfaulting — embeddings/onnx/transformers, sentiment, undici, or mammoth), or an OOM kill (V8 FATAL heap exhaustion bypasses uncaughtException). The watchdog's old false-positive 'busy server' restarts are NOT this — that was fixed by the port-bound check (start.ps1 ~L501-509); 'process gone' means genuinely dead.

NEXT DIAGNOSTIC STEPS:
1. Windows Event Viewer → Application log: a node.exe native segfault logs the faulting module/DLL there — that names the culprit dep directly.
2. Separate the npm child's exit code + stderr into a dedicated crash log (current tee mixes everything into one 5.6MB file; the actual fatal line gets buried).
3. Watch heap over time (log process.memoryUsage on an interval; try --max-old-space-size) to rule in/out OOM.
4. Run with node --trace-uncaught and confirm whether ANY catchable error precedes a death.

NOTE: 'Error: unable to determine transport target for pino-pretty' appears once in the log — only fires under ME_HTTP_LOG=1 (pino-pretty transport resolution). Probably unrelated to the crashes but worth ruling out.

RELATED: see the sidecar-management rework issue (filed alongside this) — a proper supervisor would both fix the two-window UX and capture crash diagnostics far better than the current tee.
notes:
INSTRUMENTED 2026-08-04, commit b09d7d2. Purely additive to start.ps1; no behaviour change to launch/restart/kill.

WHY THE EARLIER PLAN WAS WRONG: every previously-proposed capture (separate stderr log, --trace-uncaught, crash breadcrumbs) records from INSIDE the process tree that disappears. Only the watchdog survives a whole-tree termination, so it has to be the recorder.

WHAT WAS ADDED:
- Measure-SidecarProcess, called on every healthy check: records which pid holds the port and its working set. The moment BEFORE a death is now described rather than guessed, which is also the only cheap way to keep testing the memory-pressure candidate.
- Write-SidecarPostMortem, called when the watchdog declares the sidecar dead and — critically — BEFORE Stop-Sidecar, which taskkills the tree and would overwrite the exit code with our own.

It logs: uptime at death; the worker PowerShell's HasExited and ExitCode in decimal AND hex; whether the last-sampled node pid still exists; and any node/powershell Application-log events in the preceding 10 minutes (absence being informative too).

THE DISCRIMINATING VALUE is the worker's exit code. That process sits inside the vanishing tree yet is the only member whose handle the watchdog still holds. 0xC0000005 = access violation, 0xC000013A = close/CTRL event, 1 = ordinary npm failure, kill-shaped = external terminator. It also separates a tree termination from node dying under a surviving shell, which is a different bug with the same symptom, and is reported in those words.

VERIFIED by driving the function against real exiting processes, not by reasoning. That caught a real bug in the first version: in PS 5.1 the literal 0xFFFFFFFF parses as Int32 -1, so the mask was a no-op and the cast overflowed on exactly the negative codes the feature exists to decode. Both fatal shapes now render correctly. Also verified the worker-still-alive branch, the no-handle branch, and the sampler against the live sidecar.

ONE MORE DEATH OBSERVED during the session that wrote this: 2026-08-03 23:16:00, the 13th in the window. CAVEAT worth recording rather than hiding — that one landed while this session was starting and stopping a second sidecar and running a lorebook repair, so it cannot be cleanly attributed to the organic failure. The instrumentation is what settles that question; do not count it as a clean data point.

TO ACTIVATE: start.ps1 must be restarted. The running watchdog is executing the old copy in memory.

description:

Everything [remember:] writes goes to CHARACTER scope (durable, cross-chat) and never appears in the lanes — so it can't be sorted, deleted, or restored from the panel. The lanes show/govern the 426; the 4761 are invisible and unmanageable. The Retired view IS character scope, so the panel already crosses scopes inconsistently.

Being diagnosed; may be a restart/CSRF/handler issue. Track the scope work here; fix the delete bug before closing since this feature depends on delete working per-scope.

All client-side — reload tab, no sidecar restart. VERIFY: toggle to Character → ~4761 entries in collapsed lanes w/ counts → expand → 30 shown + 'Show all' → delete/restore a char entry round-trips → sort orders apply in both scopes. title: Consensus aggregation for multi-pass fact extraction (union is insufficient)
description:
Built the multi-pass toggle (MARINARA_EXTENDER_FACTS_PASSES, a9f559f) per TC. Testing showed pure UNION degrades quality: a 3-pass D&D run produced 74 candidates (judge kept 71 - filter overwhelmed), near-duplicates from reworded repeats, and a one-off mis-attribution survived ('Priya D&D class is Pact of the Tome Warlock' - it is Mari's, but one of three passes said Priya and union kept it). 

FIX - consensus / majority vote across passes instead of OR:
- Group candidates across passes by semantic equivalence (fuzzy match on the fact text + same lane), not exact string - so reworded repeats collapse into one cluster.
- Keep a cluster only if it recurs in >= ceil(N/2) passes (majority). A one-off (the Priya-Warlock error in 1/3) drops out; a real fact (Warlock-as-Mari in 3/3) stays.
- For a cluster with conflicting ATTRIBUTION across passes (Mari vs Priya), take the majority subject; tie -> drop or demote to chat.
- Then judge the consensus set (now small + clean) and ledger it.
This turns 'more passes = more noise' into 'more passes = higher confidence'. Cost is the same N calls TC already accepted via the toggle; the win is the aggregation. Until this lands, passes=1 is the safe default and passes>1 is experimental. Relates to 1dn, egp (Ledger Pattern), the durability judge.
notes: IMPLEMENTED (22cbd03): consensusFilter clusters candidates by embedding similarity (cosine>=0.85; exact-text fallback if the embed model is absent), counts distinct passes per cluster, keeps clusters at floor(N/2)+1 passes with the majority attribution. Wired into ingestSceneFacts (passes=1 short-circuits, default unchanged). D&D 3-pass: 48 candidates -> 22 consensus -> 11 durable; Warlock class captured AND routed to professor_mari; the 1/3 Priya-Warlock mis-attribution dropped. 171 tests. Remaining = the durability judge still leaks ~3 transient facts per scene (low-harm, the ledger is human-editable as the final gate); optional later tuning, not blocking. 1dn is now trustworthy enough to apply via dry-run -> (optional edit) -> apply.
close_reason: Extraction consensus (the titled scope) delivered + verified last session (22cbd03): consensusFilter clusters by embedding similarity, majority-votes across passes, drops the 1/3 Priya-Warlock mis-attribution while keeping Warlock-as-Mari (3/3). The 'remaining' durability-judge leak was investigated this session: tightened JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT with the mask-test discriminator (transient-event-dressed-as-identity) + the two real Hargrove misses as worked DROP examples — a net improvement on the clear cases (drops the targeted transients, keeps concrete durables). But live runs proved the judge is NON-DETERMINISTIC on borderline candidates in BOTH directions (abstract durables and identity-masked transients flip run-to-run); that variance is irreducible at single-pass and prompt-fiddling cannot close it. Robust fix = multi-pass judge consensus, filed as its own piece (8jw) rather than wedged in here. Crucially, the architecture is already resilient to the judge's variance: the dry-run -> edit -> apply ledger gate caught the desk-sex transient leak TODAY even when the judge let it through — the system as a whole doesn't depend on a perfect judge. Calibration harness + fixtures: src/__tests__/judge-calibration.test.ts.

title: Alias-learner pollutes the table: user/persona name + compound 'X and Y' become character aliases (misroutes memory live)
description:
Found while validating 1dn fact routing. The alias table has: canonicalName 'Dr. Mari Zielińska' -> aliases ['Mari','Professor Mari','Mari and TC','Thomas']. 'Thomas' (the player/persona) and 'Mari and TC' (a compound) were wrongly learned as Mari aliases (added 2026-06-12, uses:0). Effect: resolveNameToKey('Thomas') -> professor_mari, and since the LIVE tier-2/tier-3 routing uses the same resolver, facts/beats about the USER (Thomas) have been silently routing into Mari's ledger - corrupting her memory with the player's facts. Not a backfill-only issue.

TWO fixes:
1. DATA CLEANUP (one-off, guarded): remove the bad aliases 'Thomas' and 'Mari and TC' from Mari's entry (uses:0, clearly wrong). Audit other characters for the same pollution (persona name / 'and' compounds learned as aliases). Provide a dry-run script.
2. ROOT CAUSE (code): the alias-learner must NOT learn (a) the user/persona name as a character alias - it should be excluded the way subject-routing already treats 'user'/persona via matchesSessionName; (b) compound strings containing ' and ' / '&' / commas (multi-character mentions) as a single alias. Add these as guards where aliases are added (aliases.ts addAlias / the learning path). 

Severity: affects live routing accuracy for every character whose scenes mention the player by name. Relates to 1dn (surfaced it) and the identity system (cx4/identity.ts). Until fixed, fact backfill --apply would inherit the misroute.
close_reason: Fixed root cause + cleaned existing pollution, verified live. addAlias now refuses compound labels (isCompoundLabel: and/with/plus/&/comma/slash/+, whole-word so Anderson/Sandra are safe) and any label already claimed by the user/persona key; process-turn registers the persona under USER_IDENTITY_KEY so the player-guard has data. scripts/clean-alias-pollution.mjs (dry-run default, --persona, --apply) removes existing pollution via removeAlias. Applied to the live table: dropped 'Mari and TC' (compound) + 'Thomas' (player) from professor_mari. Verified resolveNameToKey('Thomas')=null and ('Mari and TC')=null while Mari/Priya still resolve. 5 new tests, 170 total. Other installs run the script to audit/clean their own tables.

title: Dual-retrieval for guest characters in multi-character scenes (guest-mode voice degradation)
description:
THE FAMILY: 'what does a character know when they are not in their own room.' Sibling to 1dn (fact capture) and to cross-character propagation - all three are about a character's knowledge surface outside their home chat.

DIAGNOSIS (TC named it; confirmed in code): retrieval and injection are single-character. marinara-extender.js getChatCharacterId() resolves ONE host (direct characterId, else first participant); the pre-turn hook (preTurnRefresh) rebuilds and writes exactly ONE lorebook - the host's. participantIds is used only for CAPTURE attribution (routing beats/facts to the right subject), never for RETRIEVAL. So when a character appears as a guest in another character's chat, they run on the scene prompt + visible chat but NOT their own ambient facts, ledger pulls, threads, or recaps at the fidelity their host instance gets. Their voice degrades toward neutral. Observed live: guest-Mari in Priya's chat lacked the June-4 FutureChain canon at host retrieval depth - her 'I have the commit history' line was so good precisely because it was the model pulling the one load-bearing fact and little else around it.

PROPOSED FIX - dual-retrieval mode. On each turn of a multi-character chat, retrieve against EVERY participant's own substrate, not just the host's: loadContext per participant (skipCredit), write each participant's block to THEIR OWN character-linked lorebook. Likely-cheap path: the engine already injects constant entries from every lorebook linked to a character present in the chat, so refreshing all participants' lorebooks (instead of only the host's) may be most of the work - verify the engine surfaces guest lorebooks for scene participants. Each voice then runs on its own canon at home fidelity.

COSTS / OPEN QUESTIONS (opie to scope): N participants = N loadContext calls + N lorebook injections per turn. (a) the 800ms pre-turn budget currently covers ONE sidecar call - N participants need parallelized calls within budget; (b) N injected blocks multiply prompt tokens - per-participant budget scaling on top of the 16384 lorebook bump; (c) confirm the engine injects participant (non-host) character lorebooks into a multi-char chat - if not, the injection vehicle needs rethinking; (d) capture attribution already scopes per-subject, so capture side is fine - this is purely the retrieval side.

ACCEPTANCE: in a multi-character scene, a guest character answers from their OWN ledger/recaps at the same depth as in their home chat (e.g. guest-Mari recalls a June-4 FutureChain detail while in Priya's chat, not just the visible scene). Related: 1dn, dq9, cross-character propagation.
notes: Built (778acdb): preTurnRefresh now resolves every participant (host + participantIds, names resolved) and refreshes EACH one's own lorebook via /api/pre-turn in parallel — not just the host. Self-contained per-participant refresh (fetch block → nuke/recreate its lorebook; writes serialized via _lorebookWriteChain). Budget (PRE_TURN_BUDGET_MS=800) bounds only the blocking await; stragglers finish in background (guest lags ≤1 turn, never generates empty). Single-char chats unchanged. Client-only (no server change; /api/pre-turn already accepts any characterId) → reload tab, no sidecar restart. Always-on per TC. NOTE per-turn cost now scales with N participants (N pre-turn calls, each incl. Stage-2 recap embedding) + N lorebook injections; watch token bite, toggle if needed. PENDING LIVE VERIFY: in a multi-char scene, a GUEST recalls its OWN canon (e.g. guest-Mari recalls a home-chat detail in Priya's chat) — also confirms the open question (engine injects guest character-scoped lorebooks).
close_reason: Verified live by TC 2026-06-20: guest characters answer from their own ledger/recaps at home fidelity in multi-character scenes ('fidelity is GREAT'). Confirms the open question — the engine DOES inject guest (non-host) character-scoped lorebooks, so refreshing every participant's lorebook pre-turn (dual-retrieval, 778acdb) was the correct and sufficient fix. Shipped in v1.2.0.

title: Capture durable FACTS from scenes, not just emotional beats (the capture gradient)
description:
ROOT CAUSE (found tracing Mari's D&D-class / Pact-of-the-Tome-Warlock conversation): the whole capture pipeline is tuned for EMOTIONAL SALIENCE, which is its strength and its blind spot. A scene is captured three ways and a flat identity/lore fact falls through all three: (1) the beat analyzer only fires on chunks that pass a sentiment threshold - a playful 'everyone's D&D class' exchange has near-zero emotion, so no beat; (2) the scene recap is one LLM pass that compresses to the emotional ARC - flavor like 'Mari = Pact of the Tome Warlock' gets dropped from the summary; (3) the tier-3 ambient/identity classifier (which is literally built to extract 'preferences, history, identity') only runs on LIVE process-turn, never on scene import/recap. So a durable fact stated inside a scene is invisible. Result: months later the fact exists nowhere in the ledger and the character confabulates (Mari: 'warlock was wrong, i'd be wizard').

PROPOSED FIX (v1.2, design only - not implementing yet):
PRIMARY - recap-time fact extraction. The scene-recap LLM call already reads the whole scene; extend it to ALSO return a structured list of durable, retrievable facts established there (identity, preferences, backstory, relationships, worldbuilding), distinct from the emotional prose summary. Ingest each as a character_topics/user_topics entry through the existing dedup matrix (identity = trait, never collapsed into an incident). Route each fact to the right subject via the existing roster (Mari's class -> Mari, TC's D&D history -> user_topics, Priya's bard -> Priya) so cross-character facts land in the right stores. Rides an existing call = cheap, bounded to once per scene-conclude, and sees the whole scene rather than per-chunk.
SECONDARY - run the ambient/identity classifier on the import path too, for imports that don't go through scene-recap.
BACKFILL - a script to run fact-extraction over already-concluded scenes (like repair-recap-pairing.mjs) so the existing months of history get their facts.

ACCEPTANCE: import/conclude a scene where a low-emotion identity fact is stated ('my D&D class is X', 'I main a blood elf warlock', 'I've DMed since 2e') -> a faithful, subject-attributed ledger entry exists afterward without manual authoring, and the character answers correctly next session. Related to dq9 (long-form user-message granularity) - same capture-gradient theme, different mechanism. Tonight a manual canon entry (ctopic-mari-warlock-canon) was written by hand as the stopgap.
notes:
SLICE 4 (1f96cbb): persistent ledger - dry-run extracts+judges and writes durable facts to data/fact-ledger/<scene>.json; --apply writes THAT file (no re-extraction). Fixes preview!=apply (apply had been re-extracting nondeterministically and writing a different set than reviewed; a flawed apply was rolled back via removeEntriesBySourceChat). Ledger is human-editable + resumable.

ARCHITECTURE NOW COMPLETE for 1dn: prose extractor (Ledger-Pattern windowing) + scene-scoped roster (whole-word) + name-variant resolution (token containment) + durability judge (verify-before-assemble, strong model) + persistent ledger. All tested, 170.

REMAINING = RECALL VARIANCE (model ceiling, not code): a single extraction pass is high-variance - across runs the Warlock fact appears or not (good runs ~90% precision WITH it; this last run missed it and leaked noise). The ledger makes apply faithful+editable but does not fix whether a run surfaces a given fact. FIX: multi-pass union - run the extractor N times (2-3), union+dedup candidates, THEN judge once, then ledger. The Warlock appears in most passes, so union almost always catches it; bounded extra cost on a one-time backfill; fits the Ledger Pattern (accumulate candidates before assembly). This is the next concrete step; until then the dry-run -> human-edit-ledger -> apply loop is the safe path. The Warlock CAPTURE itself is proven (focused extraction nails it); the work left is making whole-scene recall reliable.
close_reason: Delivered — and grew into the full reconciliation system. The capture-gradient goal (capture durable identity/lore FACTS from scenes, not just salient emotional beats) is met: facts.ts ingestSceneFacts (prose-aware classify -> consensus extraction [967] -> consensus durability judge [8jw] -> route + dedup), backfill script, the Agent SDK curator [5ny], live FR1 queue + shadow drain [b4n], bounded curator view [5f2], ledger hygiene sweep [0kk], embedding semantic clustering [and], two-stage confidence+domain apply gate [mjp]. Verified live on professor_mari: durable facts captured + 37 cruft entries reconciled (22 lexical + 15 semantic), trauma facts preserved separate. Remaining roadmap piece = FR4 audit/rollback (3pl), tracked separately.

title: Scene recaps mispaired by nearest-timestamp heuristic (36 of 56 wrong)
description: The engine's narrator return message never names its scene and scene-chat updatedAt drifts, so syncSceneRecaps attached wrong summaries - Test Drive Transgression carried the couch-morning recap, which is why Priya could not recount the test drive even with pre-turn retrieval working. Fixed in fa03e33: content-word-overlap pairing in the extension + scripts/repair-recap-pairing.mjs offline audit/repair. Applied: 36 repaired, re-audit 56/56 correct. title: v1.2: one-turn recall lag - memory block is built AFTER the response it should have informed
description: OBSERVED LIVE (TC, 2026-06-13): asked Priya about the Porsche test drive; she answered 'no memory of that whatsoever' DESPITE 17 porsche entries + the scene recap in her hot ledger. Log forensics: the block her reply generated against (turn 3) was built from the PREVIOUS exchange's recentText — no porsche; the very next block (turn 5) loaded recap-1ul5k1li + the porsche beats. The architecture assembles the memory block in process-turn (after each AI response) for the NEXT one, so topical recall always arrives one exchange late — the user experiences 'she doesn't remember' on every first ask, which is the single most trust-destroying failure a memory system can present. FIX DIRECTION (pre-turn refresh): the extension intercepts the page's generation request (wrap window.fetch for the engine's generate call — the loader already does blob-script bridging, CSP-compatible), AWAITS a fast sidecar call POST /api/pre-turn {chatId, characterId, userText} that runs loadContext with the OUTGOING user message as recentText and writes the lorebook block, then forwards the generation request. Cost: loadContext is LLM-free — ~100-300ms added per generation; the tier-2/3 capture stays post-turn. Needs care: locate the exact generate endpoint shape; timeout the pre-turn await (e.g. 500ms budget, proceed without refresh on miss — degraded = today's behavior); avoid double-writing the lorebook (process-turn still writes post-turn for capture-derived additions). Acceptance: ask about any old memory cold — the FIRST reply already has it in context.
notes: SHIPPED (pending TC live verification): extension wraps window.fetch, holds POST /api/generate <= 800ms for a pre-turn block rebuild against the outgoing userMessage (sidecar POST /api/pre-turn, LLM-free, skipCredit), writes the lorebook, then generation proceeds; failure/timeout = old behavior. Verified server-side with the exact live failing question - the steakhouse block now contains the steakhouse memories before the reply generates. NEEDS: Marinara tab reload (extension changed), then re-ask the steakhouse question - FIRST reply should know. Engine fetch confirmed interceptable (api-client.ts streamEvents uses plain window.fetch POST BASE+/generate; userMessage rides the body).
close_reason: Verified live end-to-end. The lag fix (pre-turn refresh) was necessary but not sufficient - it unmasked three deeper failures fixed in sequence: recap mispairing (36/56 wrong, fa03e33), the new-chat pre-turn skip (cba43f8), and the engine lorebook tokenBudget default of 2048 silently dropping the grown memory entry (103d571, the actual killer). Final live test 2026-06-11 7:47 PM: Priya recalled the back seat, the windshield, good girl, and Mari driving to the river - all mapped to real entries (ctopic-l0l0r1jb, recap-u943nyuy) delivered by the pre-turn block.

title: v1.2: long-form personal stories must land - granular capture for multi-page user messages (the Army story)
description: USER STORY (TC, 2026-06-13): told Mari a long multi-page traumatic story about his Army time in live chat; she retained essentially nothing and he had to re-import the chat. Telling a character a significant personal memory ONCE should make it durably known — retelling trauma is exactly what a memory system exists to prevent. ROOT CAUSES (compound): (1) the live path chunks one message = one chunk (MarinaraExtender-7h9) — a multi-page story yields at most ONE beat; (2) analyzer genre boilerplate + label-match dedup collapsed what little was captured (fixed this session: same-moment gate + specificity prompts); (3) tier-3 ambient catches isolated facts but not narrative. DESIGN: detect long user messages (e.g. > 1500 chars) in process-turn and route THAT MESSAGE through windowed granular ingestion - the story-import pipeline machinery on a single message (chunk into windows, classify, analyze each, subject-route, thread-tag) - so a told story produces the same beat richness as an imported one. user_topics facts + a story thread minted (the recap layer then gives it an arc). Un-parks 7h9 for the user-message case specifically (assistant-message granularity stays parked/opt-in per TC). Fire-and-forget after the turn; cost is bounded by story length and only triggers on long messages. Acceptance: tell a 3-page story once -> character can answer questions about its specifics next session without re-import.
notes: Implemented (37d42e4): /api/process-turn detects userMessageText > LONG_USER_MSG_CHARS (default 1500, env MARINARA_EXTENDER_LONGMSG_CHARS) and fires runSentimentPipeline(sourceType:chat) on that one message — windowed/per-window/subject-routed/persisted, import-parity. Tier 2 skips its one user chunk when long; Tier 3 facts still run. Design note: skip-the-coarse-chunk means an emotionally-FLAT long message could capture fewer beats (windows may miss sentiment threshold) — acceptable since Tier 3 still grabs facts and dq9 targets significant (charged) stories; revisit if live testing under-captures. PENDING LIVE VERIFY (needs sidecar restart): tell a multi-page story → console logs '[ME:longform] user story (N chars) → M beat(s)' → character's ledger gains multiple beats → next session can answer specifics without re-import.

title: One-click updater: panel Update button + double-click bat - no terminal for upgrades
description: Child of szf (install pipeline epic). TC requirement: users must never need a terminal to upgrade. Three pieces: (1) scripts/update-sidecar.ps1 - stops the sidecar, git pull --ff-only, npm install, npm run build, best-effort ollama pull of the embed model, relaunches via Marinara_Extender_Start.bat, visible console so progress is watchable; (2) Marinara_Extender_Update.bat - the double-click path; (3) in-product: /api/health gains version + updateAvailable (GitHub latest-release check, cached, silent-fail offline; drafts excluded by the API), POST /api/update spawns the updater detached (CSRF-guarded), panel shows an Update button when a newer release exists. v1.0 -> v1.1 remains the last manual hop (v1.0 has no button); v1.1+ upgrades are one click.
notes: LIVE END-TO-END TEST PASSED (v1.1.0 -> v1.1.1): simulated a v1.1.0 install via git reset --hard v1.1.0; health correctly offered the update (version=1.1.0, latest=1.1.1, updateAvailable=true); POST /api/update ran the full loop — stop, pull, install, build, relaunch — server returned at 1.1.1 in ~90s. FOUND+FIXED: version bumps must sync package-lock.json or npm install dirties it and blocks the NEXT pull; lockfile committed and the updater now discards local lockfile drift pre-pull (self-healing across the fleet since updater N+1 cleans what update N left). Also: bodyless POST needs Content-Type application/json (the extension's memFetch always sends it; only raw curl-style calls notice).
close_reason: Shipped in 45ab590, live-verified: /api/health reports version=1.1.0, latest=1.0.0 (published only — the draft correctly excluded), updateAvailable computed by semver compare (3 unit tests). POST /api/update spawns scripts/update-sidecar.ps1 in a visible console (stop server -> git pull --ff-only with loud failure on dirty checkouts -> npm install -> build -> best-effort ollama pull nomic-embed-text -> relaunch; logs to logs/update.log). Panel shows the Update button when a newer release is published; Marinara_Extender_Update.bat is the double-click path. Tag v1.1.0 moved to include it; draft release notes refreshed. Caveat noted in notes: v1.0 -> v1.1 is the last manual hop (v1.0 has no button). Full end-to-end self-update not exercised (would no-op pull on the dev checkout) — first real exercise will be v1.1 -> v1.2.

title: v1.1: narrative threads as first-class objects — thread_id minted at ingest, beats inherit, recall by thread relevance
description:
CORE THESIS (TC, 2026-06-11): v1.1 tracks narrative threads as first-class objects instead of inferring them from message proximity. Each thread = topic/arc identifier + member beats + participating characters. Canonical example: the Porsche test drive — one coherent arc spanning multiple turns and three participants that the system currently sees as 30+ disconnected beats; recalling any beat from it should pull thread context.

DESIGN SKETCH (as agreed):
- thread_id is a stable identifier generated at scene start, or inferred by the tier-2 analyzer when a scene clearly continues an existing thread.
- Ingest tags beats with thread_id at extraction time — rides the SAME LLM call that now returns subject (6qx): roster of ACTIVE threads in the prompt, model picks one or flags new-thread; ambiguous cases use the holding-pool pattern (never guess).
- Beats inherit thread_id; the index gains a THREAD layer parallel to the character layer.
- Recall pulls beats by thread relevance, not just recency + character match.
- Cold storage archives threads as UNITS once closed.

RECONCILIATION with recap-ceiling-data-model.md (which commits to assign-on-promotion): not a conflict — two tiers. Ingest-time thread_id is SCENE-SCOPED (the floor unit; cheap, piggybacked, hot-path mints only scene threads). Cross-scene ARC minting/merging stays at promotion with match-before-mint, and ArcSignature.threadIds (already in the reviewed data model as 'the most reliable signal') consumes exactly these ingest-minted thread ids. Ceiling clustering spike (the open question in the doc) gets its primary input from this feature.

STATUS: not implemented anywhere — no threadId field exists on beats. The ingest-time half of this thesis was never previously written down; the promotion-time half lives in recap-ceiling-data-model.md, bd memory recap-layer-v1.1, and issues ajb/2cu.
notes: INGEST HALF SHIPPED (22a0028), live on sidecar PID 25156. Done: threads.ts registry (data/threads/registry.yaml, nthr-* ids, scene-scoped by chatId, participants + beatCount + lastActiveAt); analyzer returns thread label riding the SAME call as subject (active-thread roster in prompt, verbatim pick or short new label, null for incidental); resolveOrMintThread with intra-chat fuzzy label matching (exact/containment/jw>=0.85) + single serialized mutation (no double-mint under concurrency, 7 tests prove it); beats + beat-index rows carry threadId; closeThread() exported (closed threads leave roster, same label re-mints fresh). 111/111 tests. LIVE VERIFICATION NEEDED (TC): run RP turns, watch for '[ME:tier2] new thread ...' and '| thread=nthr-...' in logs; check data/threads/registry.yaml accumulates sensible labels, not one-thread-per-turn fragmentation or one mega-thread. REMAINING (the payoff half): (1) recall by thread relevance — loader surfaces thread context when a member beat/entry is recalled; design with the recap layer (2cu/ajb), entries may need threadId too; (2) cold-storage archival of CLOSED threads as units; (3) scene-conclude hook — extension calls sidecar to closeThread when Marinara concludes a scene (engine sets sceneStatus=concluded; see marinara-scene-conclude-persists-summary memory); also consider inactivity-based auto-close so rosters do not grow unbounded. NOTE deviation from brief: ambiguous thread labels are left UNTAGGED (null) rather than holding-pooled — the pool is beat/speaker-shaped; untagged = status quo ante and safe.
close_reason: Both halves shipped. INGEST (22a0028): threads.ts registry, nthr-* ids minted at ingest riding the same analyzer call as subject (active-thread roster in prompt, fuzzy label resolution, serialized no-double-mint), beats + beat-index rows carry threadId. RECALL + LIFECYCLE (4c63712): ledger entries inherit threadId from beats; selectEntries ranks by effective relevance = max(own match, thread label match, 0.75 x strongest sibling match) — recalling any beat pulls the thread, returning to an arc by name surfaces members whose summaries never matched; closed threads archive to cold as UNITS (never split, never while active); idle threads (14d) auto-close in the promotion pass. Label quality hardened along the way (one-shot examples, participant-scoped roster, characterName fix). 137/137 tests. Remaining related work tracked separately: rfx (registry health metrics + scene-conclude close hook + scene-title hint), ajb (ceiling arcs consume ArcSignature.threadIds — now unblocked). Live verification: watch for 'thread=nthr-*' on beats and arc-name recall pulling thread context in scenes.
