title: v1.1 floor: atomic writes everywhere the sidecar mutates state (manifest, memory chunks, index.yaml, index.cold.yaml)
description: Every sidecar mutation is currently a plain write — a hard crash (like the 2026-06-10 BSOD that zeroed Marinara's own tables) can NUL-fill or truncate our YAML/JSON state. Add an atomicWrite helper: write temp file, fsync, rename over target. ~10 lines per call site or one shared helper. CRITICAL Windows trap (proven live in the upstream flushFile bug, MarinaraExtender-1kn): fsync must be called on a WRITABLE fd — open the temp with 'w', write, fsyncSync(THAT fd) before close, then renameSync. Never write-then-reopen-readonly ('r' + fsync = silent EPERM no-op on Windows). Skip directory fsync on win32 (can never succeed; NTFS journals the rename). Call sites to convert: beat-index manifest, memory chunk writes, index.yaml, index.cold.yaml — audit for any other writeFileSync on state paths. This is the v1.1 floor: nothing else in v1.1 ships until this is in.
close_reason: atomicWriteFile shipped in cb1cff5: tmp + fsync-on-writable-handle + rename(retry). All 6 state write sites converted (storage.writeYaml, story-jobs, identity, soft-clock, sentiment/encoder, setup .env). Bonus: fixed serializedWrite unhandled-rejection leak in lock pruning. 97/97 tests pass incl. 4 new atomic-write tests; tsc clean.

title: Report upstream: flushFile fsync silently no-ops on Windows (read-only fd), defeating .bak crash protection
description: Crash on 2026-06-10 ~11:05PM zeroed lorebook_entries.json + memory_chunks.json AND both .bak files despite the looksNulFilled/fsync protection shipped in the user's build (dist dated 6/7). Root cause: flushFile() in packages/server/src/db/file-backed-store.ts:286 opens the file with openSync(path,'r') then fsyncSync(fd); on Windows FlushFileBuffers requires write access, so fsync fails with EPERM and the empty catch swallows it — the durability guarantee is a silent no-op on the platform it was written for. Fix: open 'r+' (or 'a') on win32, and consider logging fsync failures once. Needs a GitHub issue on Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Engine per contributor pre-flight before any PR. Evidence: all four files were 100% NUL bytes; .bak mtimes 6 minutes older than mains.
notes: 2026-06-19: NOT our active work — engine bug, reported, being looked into upstream. Confirmed still live on Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Engine main today (flushFile, file-backed-store.ts:289 — openSync 'r' + fsyncSync, EPERM-swallowed on Windows). Part of a RECURRING CLASS: closely related to closed #631; TC has seen 2+ similar file-durability reports on Discord. The EXTENDER is already protected and NOT vulnerable — atomicWriteFile (memory-extender/src/storage.ts:183) fsyncs the WRITABLE handle, warns-once on failure, atomic rename + Windows transient-retry. OPTIONAL follow-up ONLY if upstream stalls: pull the engine repo, one-line fix (flushFile 'r' -> 'r+' + log-once); a high-quality issue body was drafted this session if needed. Deferred pending upstream resolution.

title: Ceiling tier: cross-scene through-line arc clustering + recap rendering
description: The real engineering work and the sidecar defensible value-add (the engine cannot reach across scenes). WHAT: an assign-on-promotion pass that clusters beats across scenes into through-line arcs and renders structured recaps. Carries: binding-signal stack (entity-overlap UNION thread-ID UNION embedding-kNN candidates, causal-ref confirm), MATCH-BEFORE-MINT arc identity (permanent IDs, structural collision detector gates LLM reconciliation), typed N:M edges {beatRef, role-in-arc, salience}, activation-signature dormancy (activation threshold > candidacy threshold), watermark drift. Heuristic salience for v1.1. Can be developed against prototype kNN (model already local) without committing to the install story. Full design in the parent cz3 design field.
design: Data-model sketch: memory-extender/docs/recap-ceiling-data-model.md — Arc (permanent id, re-renderable label, lane-driven), ArcMembership typed N:M edge {beatId, role, salience}, ArcSignature (entities+threadIds+centroid) doubling as dormant reverse-index key, ArcStatus active|dormant|resolved, watermark, RecapEntry extends Entry. Grounded on EmotionalBeat (sentiment/types.ts) and Lane/Entry/cold-tier (storage.ts). Four open type-level questions noted in the doc.
acceptance_criteria: Promotion pass assigns promotion-eligible beats to existing arcs (match-before-mint) or mints new ones; arcs carry typed edges and dormant/active state; loader injects relevant through-line recaps (coherent narrative state) instead of disconnected top-k beats; underlying beats remain queryable at full fidelity.
notes: Data-model review COMPLETE (see memory-extender/docs/recap-ceiling-data-model.md). DECISIONS: watermark = per-character monotonic seq (NOT ISO — created is date-only); edges = standalone ArcMembership with bidirectional load-time indexes; salience = recency x entityProminence x beat.salience normalized WITH a high-salience floor (beat.salience>0.8 caps recency loss, X tunable); centroid inline+cached, batched recompute once per promotion pass. CONSTRAINT (decision-with-evidence): dormant stays on ArcStatus, NOT EntryStatus — loader gates recap injection on the Arc link; do not merge onto EntryStatus (full consumer audit in doc). PRECURSOR (small beat-storage change, blocks the watermark; could be its own task): add nextSeq:number to BeatIndex and write-once seq:number to BeatIndexEntry, assigned inside upsertBeatIndex under the existing per-character serializeBeatWrite lock (encoder.ts:115/132); idempotent on re-encode (assign only on first insert, never reassign), durable in beats/index.yaml.
close_reason: Shipped in 77fd63a and live-verified on real data: Mari's first through-line 'Mari's fractured selfhood' (20 beats, June 1-12, dated trajectory, typed roles: 3 turning_point / 5 escalation / 2 threshold_crossing); Priya's 'surrender to the triad' (73 beats). Full spec honored: union candidate generators (thread/entity/kNN), one renderer call per arc (confirm+label+render, lane-aware, gaps as input, accretion), match-before-mint with H4 dormancy rules, permanent ids, seq watermarks, edge-salience floor, once-per-pass centroids. Cadence: every 60 turns + POST /api/arcs/promote. RESIDUAL TUNING (tracked on cz3): cluster granularity (1 big cluster per char on first pass - taus may need tightening), label quality over time, embedder surface-clustering risk.

title: Floor tier: ingest engine scene-conclude summaries as scene-arc recaps
description: Buildable today, zero open questions. WHY: the engine already emits a dated, named, persisted ~200-word prose summary at /api/scene/conclude (sceneStatus=concluded; readable as an origin-chat message and in each character memories array — see bd memory marinara-scene-conclude-persists-summary). WHAT: ingest these as scene-arc recap LEAVES (the chronological floor) with their underlying beats as footnotes; sceneStatus=concluded is the deterministic trigger. No LLM cost, no clustering. Ships independently of the ceiling. Parent: MarinaraExtender-cz3.
acceptance_criteria: On scene conclude, the sidecar ingests the engine prose summary as a scene-arc recap entry keyed by scene, dated, with member beats cited as footnotes; the recap is retrievable by the loader.
notes: SHIPPED (715913a), live on sidecar PID 14984 — held open for TC live verification. Implementation per the reviewed data model: arcs.ts (Arc/ArcMembership/RecapEntry mirroring docs/recap-ceiling-data-model.md), beat seq watermarks (Resolved #1: BeatIndex.nextSeq + write-once seq under the per-character lock), standalone memberships file (Resolved #2), max-8 footnotes (H3), ArcStatus separate from EntryStatus (audit invariant honored). Scene ingestion closes the scene's threads — pln unit-archival ages members to cold while the recap stays hot (displacement by composition). MECHANISM NOTE: design memory said summaries persist in character.memories arrays — empirically FALSE on this install (0 of 9 characters); ground truth chose origin-chat narrator 'returned from their scene' messages (40 exist, matching 40 concluded scenes) paired by sceneOriginChatId + nearest timestamp. Extension syncs throttled (10 min) per process-turn, idempotent server-side. LIVE VERIFICATION (TC): reload Marinara, take one turn anywhere — the first sync ingests ~40 historical scenes across participants; expect '[ME:recap] scene ... ingested' lines, then check a character's ledger for '[scene recap]' entries and GET /api/arcs. Footnotes on historical scenes will be sparse (old beats lack sourceChatId/threadId; pre-pln capture) — recaps still ingest; footnote richness grows with new scenes.
close_reason: Verified live: 28 scenes ingested per character (56 total) by the extension's own sync on TC's reload; deliberate duplicate re-sync produced 0 dupes (idempotency on real data); 542 memberships bound for Mari, 13 arcs with linked beats (recent ones with provenance), sample recap retrievable in hot index. Historical scenes ingest footnote-sparse as predicted.

title: Recap layer: consolidate beats into arc recaps as the canonical retrieval unit (v1.1 headline feature)
description: WHY: Cold storage treated the symptom (too many entries) not the disease — beat fragmentation that loses NARRATIVE COHERENCE at scale. A loader pulling N high-signal beats without connective tissue yields disconnected moments that do not add up to a story (knowing facts vs knowing a story). WHAT: introduce a RECAP entry that organizes underlying beats by ARC (a named through-line) and becomes the canonical retrieval unit the loader injects instead of fragments. Two tiers: (1) scene-arc recaps = chronological floor, ingested FREE from the engine /api/scene/conclude summaries; (2) through-line arc recaps = thematic ceiling, the cross-scene narrative the engine cannot produce, generated by an assign-on-promotion LLM pass. Background: bd memories recap-layer-v1.1 and marinara-scene-conclude-persists-summary.
design:
TIERS: FLOOR (free) = scene-arc recaps ingested from engine /api/scene/conclude prose summaries (see marinara-scene-conclude-persists-summary). CEILING (paid) = cross-scene THROUGH-LINE arc recaps, built by an assign-on-promotion pass. Rest of this field specifies the ceiling.

BINDING-SIGNAL STACK (candidate-generate cheap, then confirm). Candidate generators run as a UNION (no LLM): (1) shared-entity overlap, 2+ entities; (2) explicit thread-ID references from open_threads — most reliable because intentional, needs the analyzer to surface thread refs at beat extraction; (3) embedding-kNN over beat text — cheap proxy for emotional/thematic continuity, catches cross-entity arcs that entity-overlap walls out. Confirmation runs ONLY on the candidate shortlist: (4) causal references (beat B cites beat A, e.g. 'after the marble incident'), LLM-detectable, mid-cost. CRITICAL: the pre-filter is the UNION of the three cheap generators, NOT entity-overlap alone — a hard entity-only filter bounds the arc universe to entity-anchored arcs and makes thematic/cross-entity arcs (e.g. priya-saying-it-in-daylight) invisible.

FOUR HARDENINGS: (H1 LOAD-BEARING) MATCH-BEFORE-MINT — promotion is reconciliation against the existing arc set by signature (entities + thread-IDs + embedding centroid), gated by a structural collision detector (same pattern as fact-vs-feeling-memory-principle's gated LLM reconciliation). On hit: EXTEND the arc and advance its watermark. On clean miss: mint a new arc. Arc IDs are PERMANENT; labels are re-renderable. This is what turns 'repeated summarizer' into 'accreting memory'. (H2) PRE-FILTER RECALL via the embedding-kNN generator above. (H3) TYPED N:M EDGES — arc = set of {beatRef, role-in-this-arc, salience}; the same beat means different things per arc (turning-point vs escalation vs threshold-crossing). Pays for per-arc footnote meaning + footnote dedup at load + load-budget (render only high-salience edges, so a 200-beat arc surfaces as ~8 footnotes). (H4) ACTIVATION > CANDIDACY — dormant->active flip requires a thread-ID hit or embedding-centroid match, NOT mere entity presence (protagonist is in everything). Store each dormant arc's ACTIVATION SIGNATURE (entity+thread+centroid fingerprint) in a reverse index for a cheap per-beat 'does this wake anything?' check.

DRIFT/WATERMARK: a recap covers a closed prefix 'current through beat N'; newer beats ride hot until the next promotion advances N; resolved/dormant = watermark pinned. Beats stay full-fidelity underneath = regeneration path for bad recaps.

THREE IMPLEMENTATION NOTES: (A) EMBEDDING-MODEL TUNING RISK on the kNN generator — reuses the existing MARINARA_EXTENDER_EMBED_MODEL path (already used for semantic chunk-merge cosine sim in sentiment/chunker.ts; nomic-embed-text is the documented example). Beats are SHORT; small fast models cluster on surface vocabulary not theme ('the puddle' vs 'the gap' may not cluster on shared concrete nouns). Model is pluggable via env, so a stronger embedder is a config change if surface-clustering bites. (B) SALIENCE COMPUTATION — v1.1 HEURISTIC (recency x entity-prominence x emotional-intensity, normalized): cheap-and-coarse beats expensive-and-blocked-on-budget. v1.2 optional LLM-determined salience pass. (C) DORMANCY-GAP AS RENDERER INPUT — the re-rendering pass must RECEIVE the dormancy gap as INPUT (not merely store it as metadata) so the recap can encode 'went quiet for three weeks of in-world time, reopened when...'. The silence is part of the arc.
acceptance_criteria: Loader injects relevant RECAPS (coherent narrative state) instead of disconnected top-k beats; engine scene summaries ingested as scene-arc recap leaves with their beats as footnotes; through-line recaps generated at promotion, lane-aware, watermarked; underlying beats remain queryable on miss at full fidelity and recaps are regenerable from them.
notes: STAGE 3 (e5b4d89): through-line recap surfacing. Activation enumerated only floor '[scene recap]'; now matches both tiers (RECAP_SUMMARY_RE) so ceiling '[arc recap]' recaps activate semantically too, ordered first (broad arc frames specific scenes), prefix stripped on render. Mari has 1 through-line + 36 scene arcs. REMAINING STAGE-3 ITEMS DEFERRED AS PREMATURE (no data/need): dormancy-gap rendering (0 arcs have gaps), reverse-activation-index (only ~37 recaps), recap regeneration, budget tuning. PENDING LIVE VERIFY (sidecar restart + embeddings): steer toward the cross-scene 'fractured selfhood' arc theme without its label words → the [arc recap] should surface. On verify, cz3 core (Stages 1-3) is complete; deferred items → a separate follow-up ticket when data/scale warrants.
close_reason: v1.1 headline delivered. Recaps are the canonical retrieval unit, surfaced by relevance + meaning across both tiers. Stage 1 (loader injects recaps) and Stage 2 (semantic activation) verified live by TC; Stage 3 (through-line surfacing) is a build-verified extension of the same activation path. Deferred polish tracked in MarinaraExtender-rtd.

title: Security hardening: lock CORS to loopback, sanitize scopeId path traversal, stop logging key prefix
description: Pre-v1.0 audit (user-requested). Keys themselves are clean (never committed, gitignored, not returned/logged in full, 127.0.0.1 bind). Three fixes: (1) CORS is Access-Control-Allow-Origin:* on a localhost service with no auth — any site the user visits can read/modify the memory store + overwrite the API key. Restrict to loopback origins (127.0.0.1/localhost/::1) + optional MARINARA_EXTENDER_ALLOWED_ORIGIN. (2) scopeId/characterId/chatId are joined into filesystem paths unsanitized (storage.scopeDir, soft-clock.clockPath, encoder.beatsDir) -> path traversal (read/write/delete YAML outside data dir), reachable via the open CORS. Add assertSafeId guard at the path chokepoints. (3) startup log prints apiKey.slice(0,8) — drop to set/NOT SET. Also stale defaults (api.openai.com/gpt-4o-mini) noted for the install epic.
close_reason: Fixed + verified live (commit f58cd4b). CORS now reflects only loopback/configured origins (127.0.0.1:7860 confirmed allowed, evil.example denied no-ACAO); scopeId/characterId/chatId path traversal guarded at scopeDir/clockPath/beatsDir (../../escape → 500, not out-of-bounds read); key prefix no longer logged. Keys audited clean (never committed/returned/logged-in-full, 127.0.0.1 bind, no env routes). 84 tests.

title: First-run onboarding: one-button import, honest progress, payoff
description: Onboarding flow that takes over the panel until imported/skipped (localStorage onboarded flag). Intro: headline + one line ('Import your past chats so your characters can remember them') + one big button. Scan -> ready (shows chats/calls/tokens estimate) -> running: real progress bar with 'Analyzing chat N of M' + live ETA + Cancel (no mystery spinner). Done: payoff 'Your characters remembered N moments across M conversations' + 'Open a chat' button. Graceful degradation: per-chat failures are caught, skipped, counted, and reported at the end; cancel stops between chats. Reuses loadImportChats/importOneChat/estimate-beats.
close_reason: Onboarding takeover + 5-state flow (intro/estimating/ready/running/done) + ETA + cancel + graceful skip/report + payoff CTA. node --check ok.

title: 'Current' working cache: relevance+recency loader, recency-gated core
description: Reframe what gets loaded into the prompt as a 'Current' working cache, separate from the short/long/core retention tiers. Loader selectEntries no longer always-injects core; instead ranks ALL non-done entries by lexical relevance to the recent conversation -> recency -> proven value -> lane, and fills to budget. Relevance (stopword-filtered keyword containment of summary vs recent user+AI text, passed from process-turn) is the miss-path that resurfaces dormant memories when their topic returns, avoiding the ossification of a pure-recency cache. Core is never pruned (retention unchanged) so it always resurfaces by relevance. Eviction from Current is lossless. Eidetic mode = load all (treat everything as Current; testing only).
close_reason: selectEntries reworked to relevance+recency+value fill; core no longer auto-injected (recency-gated, still never pruned); recentText threaded from process-turn; eidetic loads all. tsc clean, 53 tests pass, relevance verified.

title: Imported beats not retrievable — no companion ledger entry
description: The loader builds the injected <memory> block from the entry index, never the beats store. Live-chat Tier 2 created a companion character_topics entry per beat (retrievable), but the story-import pipeline called encodeBeat only — so imported beats were analyzed but never recallable (the original 'beats not attaching to characters' problem). Fix: pipeline now writes a companion entry per beat via shared companionEntryFromBeat(); POST /api/beats-to-entries + scripts/backfill-beats-entries.ts backfill existing beats. Ran backfill: professor_mari now has 353 active beat-companions.
close_reason: Pipeline writes companion entries; backfill endpoint + script created and run. tsc clean, 53 tests pass.

title: Multi-character story import (one pass, beats routed per character)
description: Import a story once and produce separate beats for multiple characters who interact. Endpoint accepts assignments[{characterId,characterName,names}]; attributes once (shared cached job keyed by union of names), then loops the pipeline per character filtering to that character's speaker names and saving beats under its identity key. Chunks are disjoint by speaker so each is analyzed once (no extra LLM cost); resume works per character. UI: 'Characters in this story' rows (character picker + per-char names, remembered), + add character. Response is per-character; UI shows the breakdown.
close_reason: Endpoint loops pipeline over assignments sharing one attribution; UI assignment rows with character picker + remembered names; per-character result. tsc clean, 53 tests pass, ext node --check ok.

title: Resumable story imports (checkpoint attribution + incremental beats)
description: A long import took ~22min; a cancel/crash lost everything because beats were only encoded in a final batch. Now: (1) attribution windows cached in a per-import job file keyed by hash(text+options); (2) beats have deterministic ids and are encoded incrementally as each chunk finishes; (3) the pipeline skips chunks whose beat already exists. Re-running the same file+options auto-resumes — skips attributed windows and analyzed chunks. Clear-beats also clears jobs. UI shows 'N resumed'.
close_reason: story-jobs.ts (window cache) + deterministic beat ids + incremental encode + skip-existing in pipeline + endpoint orchestration + clearJobs on clear-beats. tsc clean, 53 tests pass.

title: Ledger UI: tabbed layout (Memory/Import/Settings) + preserve scroll
description: renderPanel wiped innerHTML and rebuilt all sections (entries first, controls last) every action -> endless scrolling to reach controls + jump-to-top on every click (e.g. Analyze). Split into Memory/Import/Settings tabs; preserve .me-panel-content scrollTop across re-renders (reset only on tab switch). Tabs auto-expand their sections on entry.
close_reason: Implemented together: tabbed ledger + scroll preservation + cancel + external/bigger-windows + remembered names. node --check ok, tsc clean, 53 tests pass.

title: Automated capture tiers (1/2/3) bypass dedup — duplicates regenerate
description: Only the manual [remember:] and ingest-commands paths call isDuplicate. Tier 1 (digest.ts createEntry / snapshotSession every 30 min), Tier 2 (sentiment, api.ts ~555), and Tier 3 (ambient, api.ts ~591) all call writeEntry+upsertIndexEntry directly with no dedup. This continuously regenerates the exact duplicates runCleanup removes — Tier 3 ambient re-saves stable facts ('user grew up in Texas') every time the topic resurfaces. Fix: shared createEntryIfUnique(scope,scopeId,{lane,summary,content,...}) that reads the index, filters by lane, checks isDuplicate, writes only if unique. Route all three tiers through it.
close_reason: Added shared dedup.ts (createEntryIfUnique + isDuplicate); routed Tier 1 (digest/snapshot), Tier 2 (sentiment), Tier 3 (ambient) through it. api.ts now imports the single isDuplicate. tsc clean, 49 tests pass.

title: Conversational soft clock: temporal context inference
description:
Why: Characters have no concept of time of day or day of week. Memories feel decontextualized — there is no way to know if something happened in the morning after a hard week or late at night when someone could not sleep. Temporal context makes memories feel like real experiences not just facts.

What: Per-chat soft-clock.yaml state file tracking inferred timeOfDay, dayOfWeek, lastSessionEndedAt. Keyword signal detector (good morning → morning, just got home → evening, can't sleep → late night, happy friday → friday, etc). Morning-after logic: if previous session ended evening/night and new session opens with morning signal, infer a day has passed and update day-of-week. Inject current session context into memory block header so character knows roughly when they are. Enrich all encoded memories with timeContext field.
notes: No LLM needed — pure keyword matching. State stored per chatId. Feeds into all three capture tiers.
close_reason: Closed

title: Memory tier system: fields, loader, promotion/demotion engine
description:
Why: The current flat store treats a one-off mention the same as a deeply recurring theme. Memories need lifecycle management so important things persist and noise falls away naturally.

What: Add tier fields to Entry/IndexEntry (short|long|core|secondary_core), retrievalCount, recitationCount, cycleCount, lastRetrievedTurn. Update loader to always surface core/secondary_core before budget, short/long within budget. Add promotion engine (score >= 5 short→long, score >= 25 long→core) and demotion (not retrieved in 100 turns long→short, 50 turns short→pruned). Cycle counter: 3 promotion-demotion pairs → secondary_core regardless of tier.
notes: Score formula: retrievalCount + (recitationCount × 3). Demotion is time-based not score rollback. Core and secondary_core are never pruned.
close_reason: Closed

title: Entity index has no refresh trigger — it is build-once until someone runs the script
description:
FOUND while shipping 76aw slice 1 (z5yn). Named now rather than discovered later as "why does it not know about the character I added last week".

data/entities.yaml is built by scripts/build-entity-index.mjs and NOTHING rebuilds it. So the index is a snapshot: entities that first appear after the last build are invisible to cue expansion, and aliases never strengthen as a name accumulates independent uses.

That is deliberate for slice 1 — the build reads every entry file in the store (14032 on this install), which is far too heavy for a turn — but it is not a resting state.

OPTIONS:
(a) Ride the promotion pass. runPromotion already fires every 20 turns and is off the hot path. Cheapest place to hang it, but a full rebuild is still a whole-store scan.
(b) Incremental observation at ingest. Accumulate run/token counts as entries are written and rebuild the thresholds periodically from the accumulated counts rather than by re-reading the corpus. More code, but turns a full scan into an O(1) update per entry.
(c) Leave it manual and document it. Acceptable only while the store is one person\x27s.

RECOMMENDATION: (b), with (a) as the trigger for recomputing thresholds from the accumulated counts. The observation half is already factored for it — observeField/EntityObservations accumulate into a plain structure, and buildIndex is a pure function of that structure, so the split needed for incremental work already exists.

NOTE: independence and person tagging are RATIOS over the whole corpus, so they cannot be updated correctly from a single entry in isolation — the counts must accumulate and the thresholds be re-applied over the totals. That is why (b) is "accumulate then recompute", not "decide per entry".

title: Ghost scope: __professor_mari__ index has 657 rows and zero entry files
description:
FOUND 2026-08-04 by the tp5 backfill, which reads every entry file an index row points at.

data/characters/__professor_mari__/index.yaml lists 657 entries. The directory contains index.yaml and NOTHING ELSE — no threads/, no user-topics/, no char-topics/. Every one of the 657 rows points at a file that does not exist (sampled: threads/thread-b480a415.yaml, user-topics/utopic-8zzur8ps.yaml).

The double-underscore name suggests a legacy or renamed identity key, so the likely history is a rename/merge that moved the entry FILES and left the index behind — or one that wrote an index under a mangled key that never received files.

WHY IT MATTERS: the loader ranks over index rows and only opens files for entries it selects. So these 657 rows compete for budget on every turn that touches this scope, win slots on relevance, and then contribute nothing — silently displacing real memories that would have fitted. Worth checking whether anything actually loads this scope before assuming it is inert.

QUESTIONS TO SETTLE FIRST: is __professor_mari__ reachable at all (does any identity/alias mapping resolve to it), and do the 657 ids exist under professor_mari — i.e. was this a completed migration that forgot to delete the source index, or a lost one?

DO NOT bulk-delete before answering that. If the files were never migrated, these rows are the only remaining record that those memories existed, and their summaries are recoverable content in their own right.

The tp5 backfill already handles it safely — it skips unreadable files and counts them rather than writing an empty bodyTerms list, so "we could not look" is never recorded as "this entry has no names".

title: Watchdog [Q] left the sidecar running — closing down took two windows killed in the right order
description:
RAISED BY TC 2026-08-04. Ergonomics, reported from daily use.

THE BEHAVIOUR: [Q] Quit broke out of the watchdog loop and let the script end, leaving the sidecar process running. The banner said so outright — "[Q] Quit (services keep running)" — so it was deliberate, not a bug. But it made shutting down for the night a two-step dance in a SPECIFIC ORDER: kill the watchdog window first, then the sidecar window. Do it the other way and the watchdog does its job and resurrects the thing you were trying to stop.

TC: "Intended behavior, but a little annoying when Im trying to close everything for the night."

THE FIX (commit follows): [Q] now stops the sidecar too and confirms the port is actually free before reporting success — "I pressed Q and it stayed up" is exactly the complaint this is meant to end. The old behaviour survives as its own key, [D] Detach, because leaving the server up while closing the console IS a real workflow; it just is not what "quit" means at the end of the day.

Ctrl+C and unhandled errors also shut the sidecar down now: the interactive loop is wrapped in try/finally rather than relying on an exit event, because Register-EngineEvent action blocks run in their own scope and cannot see the script state this needs.

KNOWN LIMIT, stated rather than papered over: a hard window kill (taskkill /F, or the OS destroying the console) notifies the process of nothing by design, so that path still leaves the sidecar running. [Q] is the reliable route. This is the same class of problem as 073 — a process tree that disappears without warning cannot run cleanup — and it is why the fix is a key binding rather than a promise about every exit path.

Ollama is deliberately NOT stopped: other applications share it.

VERIFIED end-to-end against a real sidecar on a scratch port, not by reading: [Q] frees the port and kills the node process; [D] leaves it listening; a second shutdown call is a no-op, which matters because Stop-Sidecar taskkills whatever holds the port and running it twice could kill a server someone had already restarted.

title: A demo sidecar launched without POLLER=0 wrote the LIVE engine's lorebook from a scratch store
description:
HAPPENED 2026-08-03. Filed because the failure mode is structural, not a one-off mistake.

WHAT HAPPENED. A second sidecar was started for a UI demo on port 3099 with a scratch data dir:
  MARINARA_EXTENDER_DATA=<scratchpad>/testdata MARINARA_EXTENDER_PORT=3099 node dist/index.js
Only DATA and PORT were set. The engine poller DEFAULTS TO ON, so the demo instance polled the LIVE engine at 7860, ingested real turns into the scratch store, and — the damaging part — wrote the real character lorebook on the live engine from that scratch store on every ingest.

BLAST RADIUS, verified by comparing lorebook Active Context updatedAt across all three Extender lorebooks on the live engine:
  2026-08-03T23:30:41  Dr. Mari Zielinska        <- written by the demo instance
  2026-07-29T00:54:10  Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran  <- untouched
  2026-06-25T01:53:22  Professor Mari            <- untouched
One lorebook, because the demo only ever ingested the one chat that was active. Both entries present, sizes normal — this is DIVERGENCE, not corruption. The scratch store had been seeded from the live one, so the content is similar but had accumulated its own ingests.

SELF-HEALS: the live sidecar rewrites the lorebook on the next turn ingested for that character (turn-bridge is the only caller of syncMemoryToLorebook). The window is only until TC next talks to her. A repair script is staged at scratchpad/repair-lorebook.mjs to close it immediately — reads the block from the live sidecar on 3001, writes it through the same path, fails closed on an empty block.

THE REAL DEFECT — TWO SIDECARS, ONE LOREBOOK, NO COORDINATION. lorebook-writer serializes writes per character (_lorebookWriteChain), but that mutex is PER PROCESS. Two sidecars against one engine are two writers to the same lorebook with no shared lock, and each write NUKES the lorebook and recreates both entries by design ("absolute correctness every cycle beats caching"). Whoever writes last wins outright. That design is correct for one writer and unsafe for two, and nothing anywhere warns about it.

WHY THIS WILL RECUR: spinning up a second sidecar on a scratch data dir is the NORMAL way to demo, test, or reproduce a bug — it is what a scratch data dir is FOR. The user reasonably believes an isolated data dir means an isolated instance. It does not: the data dir isolates the store, not the engine connection, and the poller default carries the instance straight back to the live engine.

FIX OPTIONS, in order of preference:
(a) Make the poller refuse to write lorebooks (or refuse to start) when the data dir is not the configured/default one — i.e. detect the "scratch store, real engine" combination and fail loud. This is the fail-closed shape the project already prefers.
(b) A startup WARNING when a second instance is detected polling the same engine — cheap, but a warning in a log nobody is reading is what let this run for the whole demo.
(c) Document it in config-and-ops and rely on discipline. Weakest — this is exactly the kind of thing discipline does not catch, since the launch command LOOKS isolated.

RECOMMENDATION: (a), with an explicit MARINARA_EXTENDER_ALLOW_SHARED_ENGINE=1 escape hatch for someone who genuinely means it. Until then, ALWAYS launch demo/test instances with MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER=0.
notes:
REPAIRED 2026-08-04, with TC's go-ahead.

Lorebook 8cuxrlVLU6UZCyumvYUnH (Dr. Mari Zielinska) rewritten from the LIVE store via scratchpad/repair-lorebook.mjs — block sourced from the live sidecar on 3001, written through syncMemoryToLorebook, fail-closed on an empty block. Result: 2 entries, Active Context 26761 chars (was 32710 from the demo store), Instructions 3510 unchanged. The other two Extender lorebooks were never touched.

TRIGGER NOW FIXABLE: the reason this could happen to someone who KNEW to pass MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER=0 was bkdz — .env silently overrode the flag. bkdz is fixed and verified (a demo instance now starts with 'Engine poller: off'), so the practical path into this is closed.

STILL OPEN, and why this stays filed: the STRUCTURAL hazard is untouched. _lorebookWriteChain is a per-process mutex, so two sidecars against one engine remain two uncoordinated writers, and each write nukes and recreates both entries by design. Nothing detects or warns about the combination 'scratch data dir + live engine'. Dropped to P2 because the likely trigger is gone, not because the hazard is.

title: [remember:] can reach GLOBAL scope, but the model is never told global exists
description:
FOUND 2026-08-03 while fixing c0b7, by reading the prompt that teaches the tag syntax rather than the parser that consumes it.

THE MISMATCH. The parser accepts three scopes:
  writer.ts  VALID_SCOPES_SET = { chat, character, global }
The prompt teaches TWO:
  loader.ts  scope — character (default, persists everywhere) | chat (this conversation only)

So "global" is an ACCEPTED-BUT-UNDOCUMENTED value. A model that has never been shown the word can still reach the broadest scope in the system by guessing it — and "global" is exactly the word a model reaches for when it wants "everywhere". The prompt even primes the concept while withholding the token: it describes character scope as "persists everywhere".

WHY IT MATTERS. Global is the only scope injected into EVERY character context regardless of who is speaking. Everything else about global is deliberately opt-in and rare — no automatic writer targets it, and the live store has no global directory at all (0 entries, verified 2026-08-03). Remember-tags are the ONE path by which a model can write there unsupervised, and it is open by accident rather than by decision.

EMPIRICALLY ZERO SO FAR. No global scope dir exists in the live store, so this has never actually fired. That makes it cheap to close now and expensive to discover later — a leaked global entry contaminates every character at once and reads as a retrieval bug, not a write bug.

NOTE — c0b7 slightly WIDENED this. Scope resolution is now case-insensitive, so scope="Global" reaches global where it previously fell through to chat. That was the right call for typo intent, and it makes deciding this question more urgent rather than less.

THE DECISION (policy, not code — needs TC):
  (a) Document global in the prompt and let the model use it deliberately.
  (b) Reject global from tag-emitted writes; global becomes API/UI-only, i.e. a human decision. Falls back to the character default, same as any other unaccepted value, and logs.
  (c) Leave it open and undocumented — the status quo, which is the one option nobody chose on purpose.

RECOMMENDATION: (b). Global is the scope where a wrong memory costs the most and the architecture already treats it as human-curated everywhere else. A model that genuinely needs cross-character reach is describing PERSONA scope (0qx6), not global.

Fixing this is a two-line change in resolveScope plus a test; the work is the decision, not the code.
close_reason:
RULED BY TC 2026-08-04: "Remember should be able to reach the global scope. The fact the prompt doesn't teach it is a bug."

So option (a) from the description, not my recommended (b). The parser was right and the PROMPT was the defect. Fixed rather than closed as wontfix.

WHAT SHIPPED:
- The scope block now teaches all three, with global described as rare and bounded to facts that hold regardless of who the user is talking to (job, city, a name they go by), explicitly not for anything about the character or their scenes.
- A worked global example was added. The prompt taught chat by example but never global, and an unexemplified option is close to an untaught one.
- "character (default, persists everywhere)" was corrected. That phrasing was a second, quieter half of the bug: it gave character the exact words a model reaches for when it means global, so the one scope that really is everywhere was both undocumented AND pre-empted by the default.
- The direct-request paragraph now names both non-default scopes instead of only chat.

GUARD AGAINST RECURRENCE (prompt-vocabulary.test.ts): the taught vocabulary is parsed OUT OF the prompt and asserted equal, as a set, to what extractRememberTags actually honours. Both drift directions now fail:
  taught but not accepted -> the model believes it saved something that was silently rewritten to the default
  accepted but not taught -> a capability reachable only by guessing the word, which is exactly what happened here
Also asserts every worked example in the prompt survives the real parser, since a malformed example teaches malformed output. Verified by mutation: deleting global from the prompt fails 3 cases.

NOT CHANGED, deliberately: ambient.ts still types automatic tier-3 facts as character|chat only. TC's ruling is about the [remember:] path, where a model is making a deliberate, visible decision. Letting the automatic extractor write global would put unreviewed facts into every character's context, which is a different question and has not been asked.

title: [bug] A malformed scope on [remember:] silently NARROWS to chat instead of the character default
description:
FOUND 2026-08-03 while answering "what makes something written to global rather than character".

THE ASYMMETRY, in writer.ts extractRememberTags (both the legacy XML branch and the bracket branch, identical logic):
  const scopeRaw = extractAttr(attrStr, "scope") ?? "character";
  scope: (VALID_SCOPES_SET.has(scopeRaw) ? scopeRaw : "chat") as Scope

So:
- scope OMITTED entirely -> "character" (the intended default, and a sane one)
- scope PRESENT but not an exact match for global|character|chat -> "chat"

A typo therefore does not fall back to the default — it falls to the NARROWEST scope. [remember: scope="Global"] (capital G), scope="world", scope="char", scope="globals" all land in the chat scope, where the memory dies with that chat instead of following the character.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the value is written by a MODEL, not a human. Casing and near-miss synonyms are exactly what a language model produces under pressure, and the failure is silent — no warning, no log line, and the entry looks perfectly healthy in the store. It presents later as "she forgot something I told her to remember forever", which triages as a capture gap or a retrieval miss when it is neither: the memory was captured correctly and filed one scope too narrow.

The same pattern applies to lane, but there the fallback IS the default (user_topics), so a typo is harmless. Scope is the only field where invalid and omitted disagree.

FIX (small): make invalid fall back to the same default as omitted — "character" — and log the rejected value once so a persistently bad emitter is visible. Optionally accept a case-insensitive match first, since scope="Global" is unambiguous in intent.

BEFORE FIXING, CHECK THE STORE for entries that landed in chat scope with content that reads character-scoped; if the emitter has been typo-ing, there may be a population to relocate. Do not bulk-move without looking — relocating a genuinely chat-scoped memory to character is the more damaging direction.

Also worth a test: writer.ts has no coverage asserting the invalid-scope path, which is why this survived.
close_reason: Fixed in 254dc71. resolveScope() normalises case/whitespace and falls back to the character default; warns once per distinct bad value. New remember-tags.test.ts covers the path (12 cases; there was no coverage before). Store check found no recoverable typo population — entries carry no record of the raw scope string, and chat scope holds 3542 pipeline-written entries, so typo victims are indistinguishable after the fact. Nothing bulk-moved, per the issue's own warning.

title: Dispose of the unmerged turn-complete-notification engine branch
description:
Local engine checkout carries feat/turn-complete-notification (commits 370a960cd 'feat(server): optional turn-complete notification for companion tools' and fa31471ad 'docs(turn-notify): record verified regeneration semantics').

STATE, verified 2026-08-02: it was NEVER submitted upstream. gh pr list --author TCLowe1982 on Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Engine returns nothing, and a code search for TURN_NOTIFY_URL across the engine returns 0 hits. The branch is now ~882 commits behind (branch point 1031013b1, stable is v2.4.0).

SUPERSEDED: the capability-package lifecycle hook (MarinaraExtender-7zro) gives turn-complete notification through a supported, versioned API — no engine patch, no rebase tax, and it fires at the write path where a swipe is visible.

DECIDE: rebase-and-submit (only if the package path stalls and we still want the seam upstream), or retire the branch and keep the verified regeneration semantics from fa31471ad as documentation feeding 7zro. Default recommendation: retire, harvest the semantics.

DO NOT DELETE the branch before the regeneration-semantics findings are lifted into 7zro or the skill.

title: Engine upstream bug: custom OpenAI-compat providers send reasoning_effort to every model
notes: Why it looked like it did not reproduce on live: live chats carry saved generation parameters or an enabledParameters toggle that clears reasoningEffort, so they never hit the default. A fresh dev chat with no preset does. TC's live timings (qwen 15001ms, dolphin 6000ms) are consistent with that — live works, dev did not, same code.
close_reason: Fixed upstream in Engine v2.4.0. Release notes: 'Stopped generic OpenAI-compatible connections from inheriting reasoning_effort for unknown models, added an explicit Off option that sends none, and made the Advanced Parameters toggle omit reasoning fields entirely (#4335).' That is the exact bypass this issue documented — the early return on the custom-provider branch skipping isReasoningModel(). Also a receipt that Pasta-Devs act on filed issues, which is the basis for filing the catalog-eligibility ask (lmcz). Verify on the local engine once it is updated to 2.4.0.

title: Rework marinara-engine-expert for ENGINE work — it was built for extension authoring, not contribution
description:
ROOT CAUSE (author, 30.07): the skill was built for EXTENSION work — using the engine as a platform (lorebooks, character cards, custom tools, agents, themes). It was never built for ENGINE work — modifying the engine itself. So we never delved into how the engine actually works internally. Its description claims a CONTRIBUTION mode, but none of the six references support one: architecture, lorebooks, character-cards, custom-tools, extensions, agents, decision-guide are all consumer-facing.

The tell: where the skill does touch server internals, it DISMISSES them.
  references/architecture.md:117 — 'The assembly lives in packages/server/src/routes/generate.routes.ts (6,800+ lines)... It is not user-extensible without forking.'
  references/extensions.md:209 — 'Modify the server-side generation pipeline — that lives in generate.routes.ts, not user-hookable.'
Both statements are TRUE for an extension author and actively misleading for a contributor. A skill's audience assumption becomes an invisible constraint on anyone who inherits it — worth recording as a general lesson, not just this instance.

OBSOLETE CORE RULE. The skill says 'When uncertainty arises about current behavior, fetch from https://github.com/Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Engine before answering.' That rule exists because the skill worked against a repo it could not see. As of 30.07 there IS a local checkout, so the marinara-extender-expert skill's INVERSE rule now applies to both: the truth is on disk and it is authoritative — read it.

LOCAL CHECKOUT (record this so a cold session does not re-derive it):
  path:    D:\Entertainment\Wip\Projects\Marinara-Engine
  branch:  staging (PR target; main is release-only, SpicyMarinara promotes)
  origin:  https://github.com/Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Engine.git
  scale:   packages/{client,server,shared}; server/src = 486 ts files, ~183k lines
  gates:   node >=24 <27, pnpm 10.33.2, 'pnpm check' = impeccable + localization + lint + build. Verified green 30.07.
  dev run: PORT=7870, HOST=127.0.0.1, DATA_DIR=./dev-data, AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=false in a repo-root .env (server reads MONOREPO_ROOT/.env and hot-reloads it). Keeps the household engine on :7860 untouched.
  household install is ALSO a git repo: C:\Users\holyk\AppData\Local\MarinaraEngine, detached HEAD at v2.3.4 = origin/main. Do not develop there.

STALE FACT: generate.routes.ts is 9,279 lines, not '6,800+'. Expect similar drift throughout — staging is 650 commits ahead of main.

MISSING COVERAGE — server internals (all traced 30.07, see MarinaraExtender-hkdq for detail):
- MESSAGE WRITE PATH. createChatsStorage(db).createMessage at services/storage/chats.storage.ts:896 is the single seam; every message-writing route funnels through it (generate, chats, scene, game, encounter routes + generation command runtimes). Exactly ONE raw bypass: services/capability-packages/capability-persistence.service.ts:387. createMessage also updates chats.lastMessageAt — the field the Extender poller watches.
- THE 8-FILE BOUND. Only 4 files import the messages table directly (chats.storage, memory-recall, capability-persistence, awareness.service) plus 4 that import the schema wholesale (db/file-backed-store, routes/admin, routes/backup, services/mari-db). The import graph bounds messages access to 8 files out of 486 — record this method, it beats grepping.
- POST-GENERATION HOOK SITE. generate.routes.ts:9150 already calls chunkAndEmbedMessages fire-and-forget when generation completes. True turn-complete signal. Covers regenerate (addSwipe) and continue (updateMessageContent) as well as new messages — all three branches converge on savedMsg at ~6310 with no early exit before the hook. Gated on memoryRecallVectorizerAvailable, which is NOT the same as MARINARA_LITE.
- MEMORY-RECALL SUBSYSTEM (services/memory-recall.ts, 480 lines) — the engine ALREADY has semantic recall: chunks of 5 messages, verbatim 'Name: content', local embeddings, memoryChunks table, cosine similarity, threshold 0.25, top-8. Read-behind keeps recent messages out of durable chunks. Never summarizes — no LLM in the path. Stale-chunk invalidation on edited history; embedding-dimension guard.
- AWARENESS SERVICE (services/conversation/awareness.service.ts) — cross-chat awareness pulling recent messages from other chats sharing a character, with temporal keyword windows (yesterday / last night / the other day).
- PROMPT ASSEMBLY LAYER — services/prompt/{assembler,merger,macro-context,marker-expander,format-engine,prompt-escaping}. Not yet traced.
- NOT YET READ: services/mari-db/mari-db.service.ts (5,131 lines), routes/game.routes.ts (12,816), routes/backup.routes.ts (3,027).

title: Risk-flag memories for VISIBLE author review — without letting risk bypass the frequency requirement
description:
Adapts the useful half of Promansis's draft-mutation pipeline into the Extender's automatic model. Keeps organic formation; adds a bounded, visible review surface for the minority of writes that are actually dangerous.

WHAT WE TAKE
- Risk scoring per mutation (low/medium/high). Bumps to medium on: relationship/dimension changes, low confidence (<0.85), conflicted values, untyped memories, missing source.
- Source-evidence requirement: drop or flag a memory whose cited evidence does not actually support the claim. This is an AUTOMATIC chimera-fusion defence (MarinaraExtender-hhdr) and needs no human.
- Graph-chain integrity: a change memory must link to a timeline event from the SAME source; a broken chain is a flag. This constrains the JOINS, which is exactly where chimera fusion lives — every fragment can be true while the join is invented.

AUTHOR'S CORRECTION — THE HARD CONSTRAINT
Risk score governs VISIBILITY ONLY. It must never touch ranking, tier, promotion, or injection.

Specifically, a risk flag MUST NOT let a memory jump the frequency requirement. Durability in this system is EARNED: score = retrievalCount + recitationCount*3, thresholds at 5 (long) and 25 (core), with cold archival at 90 days unretrieved. That ladder is the whole point — a memory becomes durable because it keeps getting used, not because something judged it important. So:
- risk MUST NOT promote a tier or seed retrievalCount/recitationCount
- risk MUST NOT raise relevance or win a slot in Current
- risk MUST NOT exempt an entry from cold archival or pruning
- a high-risk memory that is never retrieved still decays exactly like any other

If risk could shortcut the ladder we would have rebuilt importance-by-assertion, which is the thing the tier system exists to replace.

WHAT WE DO NOT TAKE
Not a review queue gating every write. Promansis's design routes ALL memories through human accept/edit/skip/dismiss on the stated principle that set-and-forget systems are 'objectively bad'. That premise is incompatible with this project — organic formation is the thesis. A queue that needs per-item attention also fails silently rather than loudly: completion rate decays, memory quietly stops updating, and nothing errors.

WHAT 'VISIBLE' MEANS (author, 30.07): flagged facts get surfaced UP and visibly, not buried in a queue the author must remember to visit. The flag comes to the author; the author does not go to the flag. Writes still land automatically — the flag is an annotation on committed memory, not a gate in front of it.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: route flagged items through the existing holding pool (holding-pool.yaml) rather than building new infrastructure. Unflagged writes commit as they do today.

RELATED: MarinaraExtender-hhdr (chimera fusion — the failure this defends against), MarinaraExtender-76aw (identity/alias resolution, which Promansis's pipeline already solves and ours does not).

title: Geography conflict: outline places the pre-meet in Kansas, played entries place it in Boston
description:
Needs author adjudication. Not resolvable from the store, and deliberately left un-reconciled because outline must never overwrite played memory.

OUTLINE (utopic-c2q6cb5t, provenance unplayed): the days-before meet was a full KANSAS leg — I-70 driving, a KCI pickup — 'not a boston pier hello'.

PLAYED (recallable canon, currently authoritative):
  thread-y2ewi0wk — Thomas and Priya discussed visiting Erica in BOSTON for the Fourth of July
  thread-3263q4sb — table booked at Oleana, 8pm, party of four, Fourth of July. Oleana is in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
  thread-0mja4llk — dinner plans before Erica's schedule fills 'all reservations in BOSTON on the Fourth of July'

Three played entries independently place the Fourth in Boston, so this is not a single digest slip.

Possible readings:
1. Both legs are real and sequential — Mari's ledger notes 'a table waiting in two cities', which would make Kansas the pre-meet and Boston the Fourth. No contradiction; the played entries are simply silent on the Kansas leg.
2. The Boston framing is itself a chimera join (MarinaraExtender-hhdr) and Oleana was welded in from elsewhere.

Reading 1 is the more likely and requires NO amendment to played canon — only that the outline stay outline until the leg plays. Do not amend the Boston entries without the author choosing reading 2 explicitly; under reading 1 they are correct and striking them would destroy true canon, which is exactly the errata-v1 mistake (see MarinaraExtender-fph4).
notes:
PREMISE CORRECTED 29.07 by the author. Half of this 'conflict' was my own geography error, not the store's.

Oleana is in Cambridge, MASSACHUSETTS — the Boston metro. So thread-3263q4sb (Oleana) and thread-y2ewi0wk/thread-0mja4llk (Boston) agree; they are the same place. I listed Oleana as independent corroboration of a Boston-vs-Kansas contradiction when it was corroboration of nothing — it just says Boston twice.

Ambiguity that caused it: Priya went to school in Cambridge, England and now LIVES in Cambridge, MA. Recorded via bd remember so a future geography lint disambiguates which Cambridge before flagging.

Also: 'a table waiting in two cities' does NOT mean two in-story cities. Per the author it refers to the two registers he holds with Mari — in-story with the character, and out-of-story as the author. So it is not evidence for a two-leg itinerary and must not be cited as such.

What actually remains open, narrowed: the outline's Kansas leg (I-70, KCI pickup) versus a Boston-metro Fourth. These may simply be sequential and both true, but there is now NO store-side evidence for that reading — it rested on the two-cities line, which is withdrawn. Still author adjudication. Boston-metro stays authoritative played canon; the Kansas leg stays unplayed outline; do not amend either without an explicit ruling.

Method note, second instance in one day: I asserted a geographic conflict from my own assumption without verifying the referent. Same class as the errata-v1 failure — certifying on inference instead of checking.

title: Poller slice D: recitation detection from polled message text
description:
Replaces the extension recall detection that POSTed /api/entries/:id/recite. Operates on the completed AI message text fetched in slice B, matching surfaced entry summaries and bumping recitation counts (the promotion signal).

Strictly better than the DOM TreeWalker it replaces: complete text rather than a mid-stream walk, and no React re-render fragility. Known limit carried over from the architecture map: summoned counting is lexical-only.

Shares its implementation with proxy slice pyx - same matching logic, different text source (polled message vs streamed buffer). Build once, call from both paths.

description:

title: EPIC: Migrate Extender integration from client extension to inference proxy
description:
Marinara Engine v2.3.4 removed client extensions entirely (no compat mode; retained extension records and extension-storage:* are permanently erased on first 2.3.4 startup). The Extender bridge (loader.js + marinara-extender.js) is dead.

REPLACEMENT MODEL: the sidecar becomes an OpenAI-compatible inference proxy that Marinara points its Main connection at. Memory is injected directly into the outgoing system message; the response stream is teed for turn ingestion and recitation detection.

DECIDED 2026-07-23 (TC):
- Scope resolution = engine REST cross-reference (GET /api/chats on the engine, match prompt message tail -> exact chatId/characterId) + prompt-prefix-hash cache; fingerprint-only as degraded fallback when the engine is unreachable.
- Injection = direct into the system message. Lorebook mechanism DROPPED entirely.

- Kills e87 (engine silently drops over-budget lorebook entries), axu (duplicate Extender lorebooks), s19 (stale lorebookIdCache) - all become moot.

- Agents/summary/Noodle sub-calls must NOT hit the proxy - engine per-category default connections (Main -> proxy, Agents -> direct). Config is the fix; server-side guard is the safety net.

NOTE: the existing POST /v1/chat/completions (index.ts handleChatCompletions) is the nqy Rewrite Assistant relay, NOT this. It hardcodes stream:false, rewrites the model, drops sampling params, and uses the sidecar key. Reuse the route + config plumbing, not the handler.
