Fix: have the extension send characterName to memory-block and pass it through to resolveIdentity.
close_reason: memory-block accepts characterName; extension sends it. New characters get readable identity slug.

title: Bracket bookmark weight always defaults to 0.5
description: MEMORY_SYSTEM_INSTRUCTIONS tells the model to emit [bookmark: ... weight=0.8 ...] (unquoted), but writer.ts parseBracketParam only matches quoted values (key="..."). So weight is always undefined -> falls back to 0.5 for every bracket bookmark. surfaceBookmarks rolls Math.random()<weight, so all bookmarks surface at 50% regardless of the model's 0.1-0.9 signal. Fix: make parseBracketParam accept unquoted numeric values (key=value up to comma/bracket) OR quote weight in the instructions. Verified with a parse test.
close_reason: parseBracketParam now accepts unquoted values (weight=0.8) and quoted values with commas. Verified weight parses to 0.8.

title: Recitation detection: increment recitationCount when memory is used
description:
Why: Retrieval (memory surfaced in context) is a weak signal. Recitation (AI actually used the memory in its response) is a strong signal for promotion. Without detecting recitation, the scoring system is half-blind.

What: process-turn response includes surfacedIds (list of entry IDs that were selected for context that turn). Extension checks the AI response text against each surfaced entry summary using Jaccard similarity. If similarity > 0.3, calls PATCH /api/entries/:id/recite to increment recitationCount. Server recalculates score and triggers promotion if threshold crossed.
notes: Implemented end-to-end. Server: loadContext now returns self-contained surfaced[] (id+summary+scope+scopeId) instead of bare surfacedIds; process-turn forwards it. recordRecitation rewritten to use new serialized mutateIndex() helper (was doing an unlocked read-modify-write that could clobber retrieval-count stamping = corrupt-YAML race). Extension: detectRecitations no longer depends on panelState (covered only chat scope before) — now works for all scopes from the self-contained payload, and compares each response against the PREVIOUS turn's surfaced set (cached in lastSurfaced[chatId]) to avoid a fresh entry self-matching the response it was extracted from. Metric changed from symmetric Jaccard (mathematically ~0 for short summary vs long response, never fired) to asymmetric stopword-filtered containment; verified: clear use=0.50, unrelated=0.00, partial=0.17, stopword-only=0.00 at threshold 0.30. PENDING: live browser verification after extension reinstall + sidecar restart.
close_reason: Implemented; server type-checks, extension syntax-checks, containment metric unit-verified. Live browser test pending reinstall+restart.

title: Tier 3: ambient detail classifier
description:
Why: Throwaway lines that reveal who someone IS get lost because they carry no emotional weight. 'Priya has a level 400 character', 'I grew up in Texas', 'I cried at the end of MGS3' — these make someone feel known rather than just remembered. This is where the magic lives.

What: After each turn, extract candidate sentences from both user and AI messages. Filter to: sentences under 120 chars, containing first-person markers (I/my/me/we/my), not ending in ?. For each candidate, run a fast binary LLM call: 'does this reveal a stable fact about identity, history, preferences, or relationships?' If yes, extract the fact and save as user_topics (user message) or character_topics (AI message). Fires async — does not block lorebook update.
notes: Small local model (dolphin3:8b) handles this well. Binary output keeps it fast. Candidate filtering is the key — reduces LLM calls dramatically. User messages → user_topics, AI messages → character_topics.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tier 2: sentiment capture on live chat turns
description:
Why: Emotional peaks in conversation (breakthroughs, fights, confessions, crying together) should be captured automatically without the AI needing to self-tag. The sentiment pipeline already works for story ingests — it needs to run on live turns too.

What: process-turn receives recent messages (last 20) from extension. Runs classifyChunks on them (CPU only, no LLM). If any chunk exceeds 0.65 salience threshold, fires analyzeChunk async (does not block lorebook update). Saves EmotionalBeat under character beats directory plus a companion character_topics ledger entry describing the moment. Works in both RP and conversation mode.
notes: Threshold starts at 0.65, tune from there. Classifier is pure keyword/regex so it adds no latency. LLM analyzer fires only when threshold crossed. Game mode excluded for now.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tier 1: time-based session snapshots (30 min)
description:
Why: Long collaborative sessions leave no memory trace when nothing trips an importance signal. A 2.5 hour paper editing session is meaningful context that the current self-tagging model misses entirely.

What: Extension tracks lastSnapshotTime per chatId in localStorage. On each new message, if 30+ minutes have elapsed, sends last 40 messages to new /api/snapshot endpoint. Server runs a single lightweight LLM call: summarize what was discussed, extract user facts and ongoing work, save as character-scope entries. Prompt is distinct from the chat-import digest — framed as ongoing session summary not historical review.
notes: Reuses existing digest infrastructure. 30 min is user-specified. Last 40 messages is a reasonable window — tune if needed.
close_reason: Closed

title: Three-tier ambient memory capture system
description:
Why: The current self-tagging model only captures what the AI explicitly decides to flag — it misses two entire categories of valuable memory. A 2.5-hour paper editing session left no trace because nothing tripped an importance signal. Low-signal throwaway details ('Priya's level 400 character', 'the MGS3 tears') are what make someone feel *known* rather than just remembered, and no current signal catches them.

What needs to be done:

Tier 1 — Temporal snapshots: Periodic memory saves on a cron/timer, independent of emotional weight. Captures long collaborative sessions where content matters but nothing spikes. Simplest to implement — scheduled digest of recent turns into character memory.

Tier 2 — Sentiment-triggered: Emotional peaks flagged and stored automatically. Crying together, breakthroughs, fights, confessions. The sentiment pipeline (analyzer.ts) already scores salience — this tier is about wiring those scores into the memory write path for chat turns, not just story ingests.

Tier 3 — Ambient detail capture: The hard one. Throwaway lines that reveal who someone IS vs what they're doing right now. Needs a lightweight per-turn classifier that asks: 'does this sentence reveal a preference, history fact, or identity marker?' Low-signal, high-value. The difference between a therapist's notes and a best friend's memory. Possible approach: small prompt asking 'does this line reveal something about who this person is?' run against candidate sentences before they're discarded.
notes: User's exact framing: 'that third tier is where the magic lives — the difference between this AI remembers our conversations and this person actually knows me.'
close_reason: Closed

title: Global lorebook bleed: global-scope memories load for all characters
description: The global scope in the sidecar is intended for conventions that apply everywhere, but all global memories are injected for every character regardless of whether they're relevant. This pollutes context for characters that shouldn't see global entries, and there's no mechanism to restrict or opt characters out of specific global entries.
close_reason: Working as designed — global scope is intentionally injected for all characters. No actual bleed occurring.

title: Zombie entries: completed tasks leave empty entry shells in lorebook
description: When memory entries are marked done or deleted in the sidecar, the corresponding lorebook entry content goes empty but the entry shell remains in Marinara's lorebook. These zombie entries clutter the lorebook and waste context budget slots. Completed/deleted entries should be removed from the lorebook or their enabled flag set to false.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lorebook naming: all character lorebooks share identical name
description: Every character gets a lorebook named 'Marinara Extender Memory'. In Marinara's lorebook list this makes them indistinguishable — users can't tell which lorebook belongs to which character. Lorebook name should include the character name or ID so they're identifiable in the UI.
close_reason: Closed

title: Entry naming: no human-parseable scope/descriptor convention
description: Lorebook entries created by the extension have no readable name or consistent naming convention. The comment marker 'marinara-extender-memory-block' is an internal ID, not a label a user would understand. Entries should follow a scope/descriptor pattern so users know what they're looking at if they open the lorebook.
close_reason: Closed

title: loadContext's background exposure-credit writes had no join point (fixed)
description:
FOUND + FIXED 2026-08-03 while running quality gates for c0b7.

SYMPTOM: receipts.test.ts failed at ~50%, intermittently, with
  ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir ...\characters\char-why
and it was always attributed to whichever test happened to run last, never to the code that caused it.

CAUSE: loadContext stamps lastAccessed / retrievalCount as a `void Promise.all([...])` — deliberately not awaited, because stamping must never add latency to a recall. But "the hot path does not await" was implemented as "nothing CAN await": there was no handle at all. A test that deletes its temp data dir immediately after loadContext races an in-flight index write, which recreates the directory mid-rm.

An earlier pass this session diagnosed the same symptom as the fire-and-forget RECEIPT write and fixed that by awaiting it. That fix was correct and necessary but not the whole cause — the credit stamping is a second background writer into a different directory, and it is the one that writes characters/<id>/, which is the path that actually appeared in the error.

EVIDENCE THE OTHERS ALREADY FELT IT: four sibling tests (relevance-ranking, scene-recap, thread-recall, unplayed-provenance) carry `rm(..., { maxRetries: 5, retryDelay: 100 })` with comments naming the fire-and-forget credit stamping. They were treating the symptom with retries. cold-storage.test.ts had neither retries nor skipCredit and was carrying the same latent flake unnoticed.

FIX: loader.ts keeps the promise in a module-level `pendingCredit` and exports `awaitPendingCredit()`. The hot path still never awaits it; teardown does. Added to all six affected test files. Verified 6/6 clean on the previously-flaky file (was ~50%) and 3x clean full-suite runs, 400 passing.

GENERAL LESSON, worth carrying: a background write needs a JOIN POINT even when the hot path never uses it. Fire-and-forget describes who waits, not whether waiting is possible. The retry-with-backoff workaround is the tell — when teardown needs retries, something is still writing and nobody can tell when it stops.

LEFT IN PLACE: the maxRetries options on the four siblings. They now guard only genuine OS-level transients (Windows EBUSY from indexers/AV), which is what retries are actually for.

title: sidecar .env silently overrides process env — a second instance cannot be configured
description:
index.ts loadDotEnv() writes every .env key into process.env unconditionally: 'if (key && val) process.env[key] = val' with the comment '.env always wins — overwrites stale system env vars (e.g. from Python venvs)'.

Consequence: an operator CANNOT override a setting per-invocation. Setting MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER=0 in the environment does nothing if .env says 1 — the banner even prints 'Engine poller: ON'. Hit live 2026-07-30 while trying to start an isolated dev instance with the poller off.

Why it matters beyond convenience: the poller nuke-and-recreates real lorebooks. Someone trying to quickly disable it under time pressure will reach for an env var, see it ignored, and have no obvious reason why. The documented revert path (edit .env) is correct precisely BECAUSE the env var does not work — that is a trap worth removing rather than documenting around.

The original intent is legitimate: a stale MARINARA_EXTENDER_* var inherited from a Python venv should not beat the user's .env. But 'inherited stale var' and 'deliberate override' are indistinguishable the way it is written today.

Suggested fix: keep .env authoritative for values the process did not receive, but let an EXPLICIT override win — e.g. honour process.env when the key is present and non-empty, or add a documented ME_ENV_OVERRIDE=1 escape hatch. Whichever is chosen, print which source won for any key that differs, so it is never silent.
notes: Data dir and engine URL overrides DID hold in that test only because they are absent from .env — so isolation was accidental, not enforced. A dev instance whose .env happens to contain MARINARA_EXTENDER_DATA would have written to the live store.

title: Write install/setup/troubleshooting docs in STE strict mode (non-native readers)
description:
Apply ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English, STRICT mode, to the ACT-DOCS only: install, /setup flow, troubleshooting, env-var reference, and the destructive/maintenance scripts (purgeColdEntry, repair-indexes, backfill).

WHY: the prior extension had roughly 900 users and SEVERAL WERE NON-NATIVE ENGLISH SPEAKERS. STE exists for exactly that reader — controlled vocabulary, one meaning per word, one instruction per sentence, active voice, sentence-length caps. For destructive operations one-instruction-per-sentence is a safety property, not a style preference: a reader at 2am in their second language must not have to parse a compound instruction.

SCOPE LIMIT — DO NOT APPLY REPO-WIDE. Reference docs that carry REASONING stay in ordinary prose: .claude/skills/marinara-extender-expert/references/*, the failure taxonomy, design rationale. Those depend on subordinate clauses and hedging ('plausibly', 'measured in one store, may not generalise'). STE strips voice and nuance on purpose — its own skill file says so.

MEASURED EVIDENCE for that split (30.07), linting our files against the externally LLM-authored research docs in memory-extender/docs/:
  ours    SKILL.md 4.64 | architecture.md 4.66 | data-model.md 5.40 | CLAUDE.md 2.61
  LLM     Comparision_1 3.37 | Comparision_2 3.04 | Doc_3_NextGen 3.25 | Doc_4 4.43
The generic LLM-essay prose scores CLEANER than our reasoning-dense docs, and by the tool's own em-dash 'slop marker' ours look far more machine-written (75 vs 3). So the score does not detect AI slop; it detects register. Optimising reference docs against it would push them toward the exact voice we are avoiding.

TOOLING CAVEAT if the linter gets used at docs time — fix three bugs first or the delta is noise:
1. possessives counted as contractions (regex \b\w+['\u2019](t|re|ve|ll|d|s|m)\b catches 's). "The parser's output is clean" scores 25.00/100w against a claimed 4.36 baseline.
2. predicate adjectives counted as passive voice ("the value is complicated").
3. open(f) has no encoding= and dies on non-ASCII under Windows cp1252.
Also note its headline experiment is circular: all 11 linter checks correspond to explicit instructions in the skill it evaluates, so the reported -74% measures instruction-following on its own rubric.

SOURCE: github.com/woosal1337/blog/tree/main/videos/ep01-the-cure-for-ai-slop — the ste-writing-skill.md file is a usable compact style guide with strict/flavored modes; the surrounding claims are not load-bearing. Official spec is ASD-STE100 Issue 9, free at asd-ste100.org, but COPYRIGHTED — do not paste it in full into the repo or a skill.

title: [done] Backfilled the extension-outage gap tags (2026-07-23) into Mari + Priya memory
description:
One-off recovery: while the extension was dark (~09:40 death -> 14:30 poller start), the characters kept emitting [remember:]/[bookmark:] commands that nothing ingested. The tags survived verbatim in the saved engine messages (the engine did NOT strip them — that was the extension regex script, now gone), so they were recoverable.

TWO chats had activity today: FfpHDWOWtSda7XcMfSen_ (Dr Z / Dr. Mari Zielinska, card Po_H0vIbkPUMbZmt7aUoQ -> identity professor_mari via alias) and PX4ptLqNv_WHOto-JPL04 (Dr. Priya).

TOOL: memory-extender/scripts/backfill-gap-tags.ts (dry-run by default, --apply to commit). Reuses the Extender OWN parsers (extractRememberTags/extractBookmarks) so parsing matches the extension exactly, incl. unspecified-scope -> character default. Remembers go through POST /api/ingest-commands (DEDUPES, so overlap with the poller/pre-death captures is harmless). Bookmarks do NOT dedupe server-side, so only topics confirmed ABSENT from the chat current bookmarks were added.

COMMITTED (verified on disk under data/characters/professor_mari/): 9 remember ledger entries created for Mari (12 sent, 3 deduped — the poller had already caught the newest), 0 for Priya. Bookmarks added: Mari marinara-extensions-killed w=0.7 + w=0.4, Priya thomas-security-fire w=0.5. Re-run is fully idempotent (0 new). 

BONUS CONFIRMATION: the same professor_mari entries also show beat/thread files from the LIVE POLLER processing the same turns via process-turn — the backfill and the poller converged, deduped, no corruption. End-to-end proof the poller path works on real traffic.

Data backup from before any of this: marinara-extender-backups/pre-poller-20260723-142708/.
close_reason: Closed

title: Document the Main-vs-Agents connection split as an install requirement
description:
If the proxy is set as the engine default connection it will also receive tracker agents, chat summaries, Noodle refreshes and scene analysis. Injecting memory into a tracker prompt, or ingesting a summary call as a chat turn, poisons the memory store.

Engine supports per-category default connections (Main / Agents / Images / Videos, v2.2) and per-agent dedicated connections. Main -> proxy, everything else -> direct.

This is a CONFIG fix and must be prominent in /setup and the README, not buried. The server-side guard in slice 3 (skip injection when the request does not resolve to a known chat) is the safety net, not the primary defence.
notes: DEMOTED P1 -> P3 2026-07-23: this only matters on the OPT-IN proxy path. The poller does not sit in the generation path at all, so agent/summary/Noodle calls never reach it and there is nothing to misroute. Still required documentation IF someone enables the proxy.

title: Proxy slice 5: server-side recitation detection over the response buffer
description:
Replaces the extension recall detection that POSTed /api/entries/:id/recite.

The proxy already buffers the full assistant text for slice 4, so recitation detection moves server-side: match surfaced entry summaries against the completed response and bump recitation counts (the promotion signal).

Strictly better than the DOM approach it replaces - operates on the complete text rather than a mid-stream TreeWalker, and no React re-render fragility. Note the known limit recorded in the architecture map: summoned counting is lexical-only.
notes: DEMOTED P2 -> P3 2026-07-23: superseded on the default path by poller slice ay7. Same matching logic, different text source - build it once in ay7 and have the proxy path call it.

title: Proxy slice 4: tee the response stream for turn ingestion
description:
Replaces the extension POST /api/process-turn call after each AI response.

- Buffer the assistant text while streaming it through to the engine (tee, never block or delay the stream).
- On stream completion, fire process-turn with the user text (last user message from the request) + the assembled AI text, for the resolved scope. Stays fire-and-forget as today.
- Handle aborted/cancelled streams: partial or user-cancelled generations must NOT be ingested as a completed turn.
- Handle regenerations: a re-rolled turn should supersede, not duplicate, the prior ingestion for that position.
- Group scenes: each participant ingests under its own scope, as the extension did per-lorebook.
notes: DEMOTED P1 -> P3 2026-07-23: proxy is the OPT-IN path now. Turn ingestion on the default path is poller slice 23i, which gets identity for free from the engine.

title: Proxy slice 3: inject the memory block into the outgoing system message
description:
Replaces the two constant lorebook entries as the injection mechanism.

- Load the memory block for the resolved scope (existing GET /api/memory-block logic), split it as splitMemoryBlock does today (instructions before the \n\n<memory> marker, live context after).
- Insert into the outgoing request: append to the existing system message, or insert a system message if none. Preserve preset section ordering intent as closely as the wire format allows.
- Respect the existing per-scope token budgets (BUDGET_CHAT 4000 / _CHARACTER 2000 / _GLOBAL 1000) and EIDETIC.
- Skip injection entirely when the request does not resolve to a known chat (agent/summary/Noodle sub-call safety net).

KILLS: the forced ME_LOREBOOK_TOKEN_BUDGET 16384 workaround, the _lorebookWriteChain mutex, ensureLorebook, writeMemoryToLorebook, and bugs e87/axu/s19.
notes: DEMOTED P1 -> P3 2026-07-23: proxy is the OPT-IN path now; the poller writes memory via the lorebook API instead (slice lxp). Keep the design note recorded on 53f: on the Anthropic route, inject into the TOP-LEVEL system parameter, not a role:system message.

title: Proxy slice 2: resolve chat/character scope from an OpenAI-compatible request
description:
An OpenAI-compatible request carries no chat or character ID. Resolve it.

DECIDED: engine REST cross-reference + fingerprint cache.
- Primary: call the engine API on its base URL (GET /api/chats + messages), match the incoming prompt message tail to resolve exact chatId + characterId. Engine is single-user local-first; GETs should not need CSRF (VERIFY - mutations do).
- Cache by prompt-prefix hash so resolution is one lookup per conversation, not per turn.
- Degraded fallback: fingerprint the stable prefix (character name + first message) when the engine is unreachable. Known limit - cannot distinguish two chats with the same character and same greeting, so it degrades to character scope.

EDGE CASES: chat forks/branches sharing a prefix, regenerated turns (same tail resolves twice), edited first messages invalidating the fingerprint, group scenes with multiple participants.

Feeds the existing identity/alias stable-key system rather than inventing a second one.
Same read channel later unlocks bos (lorebook import) and chat digest/import.
notes: DEMOTED P1 -> P3 2026-07-23: proxy is now the OPT-IN path (epic hq7), and scope resolution is only needed there. On the poller path the engine hands us chatId and characterId directly, so this whole matching problem does not exist. Only build it if someone actually runs the proxy path.

title: Opt-in multi-pass consensus for the import pipeline (high-accuracy historical ingestion)
description: From the Doc_4 review (Slice 1). The batch import (runSentimentPipeline behind /api/analyze-beats and /api/ingest-story) is currently SINGLE-pass: each windowed chunk is analyzed once. The Ledger Patterns consensus branch would run the extraction N times and keep a fact only at consensus_count >= floor(N/2)+1, with span-overlap dedup-first and normalize-to-canonical, eliminating single-pass misattribution. Genuine accuracy upgrade for importing thousands of multi-year messages, at N times the LLM cost -> make it OPT-IN / cost-gated (a high-accuracy import mode), not the default. The windowing + on-disk ledger + async parts are ALREADY present in the import pipeline; this adds only the multi-pass consensus assembly. Source: docs/Doc_4_LedgerIntegration_review.md Slice 1.

title: Sensitive-domain (YMYL) protected memory category: importance floor + decay exemption
description: From the Doc_3_NextGen assessment (YMYL, Slice 7). Extend the existing apply-gate domain-sensitivity (currently a trauma lexicon that always-holds) into a broader protected-domain classifier for Your-Money-or-Your-Life sensitive info (health, finance, legal, safety). Two-stage: fast regex keyword detect, then local-LLM semantic check. A memory tagged protected gets a higher importance floor, exemption from decay/pruning (like the never-pruned core tier), and mandatory reconcile-gate validation before storage. Builds directly on apply-gate (domainFlags) + the core tier. Source: docs/Doc_3_NextGen_assessment.md Slice 7.

title: Importance-weighted adaptive decay (vary decay rate by extraction-time importance)
description: From the Doc_3_NextGen assessment (FadeMem, Slice 7). Today decay is uniform: bookmark weight x 0.97 per turn and tier demotion by fixed staleness days. Proposal: make the decay rate adaptive to an IMPORTANCE score assigned at extraction time, so trivia fades quickly and pivotal facts persist. An importance score (from the sentiment/ambient analysis) modulates either the bookmark decayRate or the tier-demotion staleness window. Note: hysteresis (separate promote/demote thresholds) and consolidation (re-access strengthens) are already covered by tier thresholds + secondary_core + recordRecitation; the genuinely-new part is the importance-adaptive decay rate. Complements fr0 (story-time decay) and the tier engine. Source: docs/Doc_3_NextGen_assessment.md Slice 7.

title: Per-model prompt adapters / structured output for the analysis pipeline
description: From the Comparision_2 review (shortcoming 2.4 supplement). The analysis system prompts (analyzer/ambient/digest) assume a dolphin3:8b-class model; format adherence (JSON/YAML) varies across model templates (ChatML, Llama-3-Instruct, etc.), so a weak or alignment-tuned model degrades capture quality. NOTE: model-swapping is already supported (MARINARA_EXTENDER_LOCAL_URL/LOCAL_MODEL + external fallback) and the tiers are fire-and-forget with defensive parsing, so this is HARDENING, not a crash fix (the source docs crash framing is overstated). Proposal: a lightweight per-model adapter layer that adjusts prompt formatting and/or requests structured output (e.g. Ollama JSON-schema mode) based on the configured model. Modest scope; existing defensive parsing already covers some of this. Source: docs/Comparision_2_review.md Slice 6.

title: Party Scope: shared scene memory for group chats (dedupe recaps across co-stars)
description: From the Comparision_2 review (shortcoming 2.3 supplement). In a group scene with N AI characters, each participant currently gets its OWN lorebook (the extension refreshes each participants memory into its own lorebook), so a shared scene event (e.g. a scene recap) can be stored/injected N times across N characters. Proposal: a dedicated Party Scope (chat-level, shared read-only across the scenes participants) for shared scene events, so co-stars read one copy instead of each duplicating. NOTE: the GLOBAL scope already provides cross-character shared memory and partially covers this; Party scope is the per-scene refinement. The 60-percent token-savings figure from the source doc is unverified/fabricated; savings TBD. NOT a gap: Tier-2 already routes beats to the correct co-stars ledger LIVE via participantIds + buildSubjectRoster + resolveNameToKey. Source: docs/Comparision_2_review.md Slice 5.

title: Story-time bookmark decay: modulate decay by narrative time-leaps (activate + extend soft-clock)
description: From the Comparision_1 review (proposal 4, partially-built). soft-clock.ts already exists (narrative time-of-day + presence from prose) but is OFF by default (TIMESENSE=0, v1.0). NEW work: (a) detect time-LEAP phrases in prose (next morning, months passed, 3 years later) via the local beat-analysis model; (b) modulate the bookmark weight decay rate by elapsed STORY time, so a large narrative jump ages/expires old bookmarks instead of preserving turn-count weight. Current soft-clock does context tagging, not decay modulation, so story-time decay is genuinely new on the existing foundation. Addresses the Lack-of-Time-Sense limitation the review confirmed accurate (Slice 10). Source: docs/Comparision_1_review.md Slice 11 proposal 4.
notes: Design enrichment (Doc_3_NextGen Slice 3): consider the BI-TEMPORAL model as the advanced version of simple story-time decay. Tag facts with Valid Time (when true in-story) + System Time (when recorded); query asof(tv,ts) for world-state at a plot moment. On a narrative time-leap, CLOSE old facts validity windows rather than only decaying bookmarks. Bonus: doubles as a cleaner contradiction model than FR2 supersession (time-bound facts become 'no longer valid' instead of 'wrong'). Weigh bitemporal (more work, more correct) vs simple decay-rate. See docs/Doc_3_NextGen_assessment.md Slice 3.

title: Decision: promote FR3 reconcile curator from opt-in/offline to default/live
description: From the Comparision_1 review (proposal 2). The conflict-resolution gatekeeper Gemini proposed ALREADY EXISTS: FR1 dedup -> FR2 supersede (auto, default) -> FR3 agentic curator (reconcile.ts + apply-gate.ts). FR3 is currently opt-in/offline (MARINARA_EXTENDER_RECONCILE, shadow-by-default, runs via scripts/reconcile-facts.mjs). NOT new code to build; it is a config/UX/cost DECISION: should the semantic curator run live on the turn path by default? Cost: it is Anthropic-coupled (Agent SDK / Claude CLI auth) and adds latency. Weigh default-on semantic conflict resolution vs the current opt-in. The review found the belief-contradiction limitation overstated precisely because FR2/FR3 exist. Source: docs/Comparision_1_review.md Slice 11 proposal 2 + Overall Verdict.

title: entities.yaml multi-hop entity index (relationship topology for retrieval expansion)
description: Genuinely-new proposal surfaced by the Comparision_1 (Gemini) analysis review. The Extender does entity RESOLUTION (identity/aliases) but has NO relationship topology for multi-hop retrieval (user -> brother -> brothers friend). Build a lightweight flat entities.yaml relationship map (no graph DB): per entity, a relationship map (e.g. character_B: older_brother) plus topics_of_interest. On a memory query mentioning one entity, expand to pull related entities memories into the injected block. Addresses the real No-Multi-hop-Reasoning gap the review confirmed accurate (Slice 10). DISTINCT from w4l: w4l is a flat subject->target EMOTION ledger (explicitly not a graph); this is a relationship TOPOLOGY for retrieval expansion. Complementary, not duplicate. Fits the flat-YAML philosophy. Source: docs/Comparision_1_review.md Slice 11 proposal 3.

title: recall_memory tool: model-initiated targeted retrieval via Marinara function calling
description:
Add a Marinara custom tool (function call) that lets the CHARACTER actively query its own memory mid-turn, complementing the passive always-on injected block. New capability the current loadContext injection can't do: model-initiated, arbitrary-query, targeted retrieval.

SCOPE — READS ONLY. Do NOT route memory WRITES through function calling. Investigation of Marinara staging (generate.routes.ts:6332 tool loop) confirmed every tool call forces a SECOND full LLM generation — no fire-and-forget. For a write (save_memory), that doubles chat-model generation per save for a side-effect the model needs no result from; the existing [remember:]/[bookmark:] bracket convention is fire-and-forget (one generation, parsed post-hoc) and stays the write path. For a READ, the second generation is the whole point (the model needs the retrieved facts to write its reply), so the cost is justified.

DESIGN (grounded in Marinara staging source):
- Tool: recall_memory(query: string). Engine POSTs {tool, arguments:{query}, context:{...}} to a sidecar webhook; sidecar runs a scoped loadContext-style query and returns top-N matching entries as JSON (any shape; parsed straight back to the model).
- Use includeHiddenContext:true so the engine adds the "context" key to the webhook payload (tool-executor.ts:308) — pass characterId/chatId through it; the model supplies only the query, never identity. Sidecar resolves scope itself.
- Webhook reachability: needs WEBHOOK_LOCAL_URLS_ENABLED=true in Marinara's .env (then http://127.0.0.1:3001 is allowed, no HTTPS/restart; security.ts:319/267). One-time setup step, acceptable. Timeout is 60s (DEFAULT_CUSTOM_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS), generous.
- Works on local models: for local endpoints the engine injects tools as a <tool_call>{...}</tool_call> text convention rather than requiring native function calling (generate.routes.ts:5211).
- Auto-attach: extension creates the tool via loopback-privileged POST /custom-tools, and enables it per chat by PATCHing /chats/:id/metadata with {enableTools:true, activeToolIds:[...]} (unguarded). Same per-chat shape as the existing ensureLorebook flow.

OPEN BEHAVIORAL SPEC (pin before building): WHEN should the model call recall_memory vs rely on the passive injected block? Naive prompting risks the model calling it every turn, doubling latency. Need a trigger heuristic (e.g. only when referencing something not present in the injected block) + a guard. Validate-before-scaling: one tool, one scope, confirm in a running engine before generalizing.

Source: Marinara Engine function-calling investigation this session (engine on 2.0.x; staging traced). Progressive enhancement — bracket convention remains the universal default + write path.

title: Import from Smart-Memory: migrate SillyTavern Smart-Memory data into the Extender
description:
One-shot migration for users coming from SillyTavern + Smart-Memory (senjinthedragon). Smart-Memory stores its memory in two places we can export from: (1) per-character in ST settings.json under extension_settings.smart_memory.characters[name].{memories, persistent_arcs, relationship_history, canon, entityRegistry}; (2) chat-scoped in chatMetadata.smartMemory (short-term summary, session memories, scene history, chat-level arcs, state_ledger, profiles). Importer ingests that JSON and maps it into our data model.

Mapping sketch: memories (fact/relationship/preference/event) -> facts/entries with lane+scope (character vs chat); persistent_arcs -> arcs.ts/recap; canon -> recap/canon entry; session memories + scene history -> chat-scoped entries; profiles -> fold into arcs/canon. Route writes through dedup + apply-gate. Reuse story-import infra (story-parser.ts/story-jobs.ts; add POST /api/import/smart-memory with a progress job).

FIDELITY DEPENDENCIES: two Smart-Memory categories have no home in our model yet — relationship_history needs MarinaraExtender-w4l, and epistemic knowledge (knows/suspects/believes-false/unaware/hiding) needs MarinaraExtender-1m9. Without those, this importer must DROP or flatten those categories (log what was dropped). Full-fidelity import is gated on 1m9 + w4l landing first.

Lower priority than lorebook import (MarinaraExtender-bos): narrower audience (ST+Smart-Memory migrants only) though high-intent. See skill comparison review.

title: Inference proxy + /api/config endpoints have no automated tests
description:
GAP: The inference-proxy branch added server endpoints with zero automated coverage — the vitest suite (240 passing) doesn't touch them. Verified manually (live smoke test 2026-06-21: 400 guard, local-success completion, CSRF block/allow, /api/config GET+POST, /rewrite-assistant.js 404 fallback all observed working), but a future refactor could break them silently with no test failing.

ENDPOINTS TO COVER:
- POST /v1/chat/completions (memory-extender/src/index.ts handleChatCompletions): empty/missing messages[] -> 400; local-model success path (mock fetch -> 200 passthrough); local-disabled + no key -> 502 with helpful message; external-fallback path.
- GET /api/config (setup.ts): returns localUrl/localModel/localEnabled/externalUpstream/externalModel/apiKeySet.
- POST /api/config (setup.ts): writes only present fields to .env; empty body -> 400 'no recognized fields'; CSRF guard (browser origin + no token -> 403, no origin -> passes).

SUGGESTED: memory-extender/src/__tests__/proxy.integration.test.ts, pattern after the existing *.integration.test.ts files.

RELATED: MarinaraExtender-ap3 (client extension has zero tests — different surface), MarinaraExtender-nqy (the configure-endpoint feature these endpoints implement).

title: [bug] Duplicate Extender lorebooks created when starting a new chat for a character
description:
SYMPTOM: Creating a new chat for a character resulted in two (duplicate) 'Marinara Extender — <name>' lorebooks for that character. Reported as non-critical (memory still functions, but clutters the lorebook list and may split/confuse writes).

REPRO (to confirm): create a new chat for an existing character that already has an Extender lorebook; observe whether a second 'Marinara Extender — <name>' lorebook appears.

HYPOTHESIS (UNCONFIRMED — needs repro with devtools/network tab): race in ensureLorebook() with no mutex. ensureLorebook (marinara-extender.js ~L4057) matches existing lorebooks by characterId, so duplicates should not happen by design. But on a brand-new chat the lorebookIdCache (marinara-extender.js ~L3703, characterId -> lorebookId) is empty. If two events fire near-simultaneously (e.g. pre-turn injection + first memory write), both call ensureLorebook, both do a fresh GET /lorebooks, both find nothing, and both POST /lorebooks -> two lorebooks. The cache is only populated AFTER ensureLorebook returns (L3760-3763), and _lorebookWriteChain serializes WRITES but not ensureLorebook LOOKUPS.

POSSIBLE FIX DIRECTION: serialize/dedupe ensureLorebook per characterId (in-flight promise map), or re-check for an existing lorebook immediately before POST.

RELATED: MarinaraExtender-s19 (lorebookIdCache staleness on manual delete) — same cache/lookup surface, different trigger.

NEXT STEP: reproduce live, watch the network tab for two concurrent POST /lorebooks, confirm the race before patching.

title: [feature] macOS/Linux launcher (start.sh) — bring the Windows onboarding niceties cross-platform
description: User-surfaced on Discord 2026-06-20: the GH install reads Windows-first; Mac/Linux users currently start the sidecar manually via npm (now signposted in the README install section). The sidecar + extension are fully cross-platform (Node + browser JS); only the LAUNCHER is Windows-only (Marinara_Extender_Start.bat / start.ps1). WHAT: a start.sh that mirrors the start.ps1 conveniences on macOS/Linux — Node preflight, first-run npm install + build, Ollama detect/start + chat/embed model pull (with the same BYO-backend tolerance: skip Ollama when MARINARA_EXTENDER_LOCAL_URL is non-Ollama), sidecar start with port guard + crash watchdog + log tee, the extension-install bridge (open /setup first run), and first-run-only onboarding. Mirror start.ps1's behavior/UX (see szf Phases 1-3). P3: works fine manually today; this is the convenience parity, demand-driven (bump if Mac/Linux uptake is high). Relates to szf (closed install epic).

title: [feature] Recap layer — deferred Stage-3 polish (gaps render, activation perf index, regeneration, budget)
description:
Deferred from cz3 (recap layer; Stages 1-3 shipped). These were intentionally NOT built — premature against current data/scale. Each has a clear trigger for when it becomes worth doing; do not build speculatively before then.

1) DORMANCY-GAP RENDERING — render an arc's quiet period in the recap ('went silent ~3 weeks in-world, reopened when...'); the re-render pass must RECEIVE the gap as input (cz3 design note C). TRIGGER: arc promotion actually populates Arc.gaps — currently 0 arcs carry gaps, so there is nothing to render. Needs the promotion side to compute/store gaps first.

2) REVERSE-ACTIVATION-INDEX (cz3 H4 perf) — replace the loader's per-turn cosine-over-ALL-recaps with a reverse index (entity/thread/centroid fingerprint -> candidate arcs) for a cheap 'does this wake anything?' check. TRIGGER: per-character recap count grows large enough that cosine-all in the hot path costs (currently ~37 for professor_mari — trivial). Revisit at hundreds+.

3) RECAP REGENERATION PATH — regenerate a bad/stale recap from its underlying beats (beats are kept full-fidelity underneath precisely for this). TRIGGER: a bad recap observed in practice, or a watermark re-render needed.

4) RECAP BUDGET TUNING — explicit token budget for the recap section. Today recaps ride the character budget and footnotes add tokens on top (loader). TRIGGER: recap+footnote tokens observably crowd the character budget in real transcripts.

Parent: cz3 (closed). Activation (Stage 2) tunable via MARINARA_EXTENDER_RECAP_TAU.

title: Embedding-based similarity for the curator (clustering + ledger-view ranking)
description: Both the sweep's clustering (0kk, clusterFacts) and the live curator's ledger view (5f2, selectLedgerView) use lexical jaccard. Concrete live miss: professor_mari's two Warlock entries (ctopic-auq9mre9 + ctopic-bbupy8fl) are SEMANTICALLY identical but LEXICALLY divergent, so they don't cluster at 0.5 and the sweep won't catch them — exactly the case TC flagged. Upgrade: use embedding cosine (fetchEmbeddings/cosineSim already exist, used by consensusFilter) for clustering + ranking, with the embed model pulled. Cache per-entry embeddings (4685 entries — embed once, reuse) so it's not a per-run cost. Gated/opt-in (embed model may be absent -> fall back to lexical, which already works for lexical dups like the 'sold solution/fix' cluster). This is the recall upgrade; lexical is the cheap floor. Relates to 0kk, 5f2, egp.
close_reason: Embedding-based semantic clustering built + verified. The stated motivator (Warlock pair) was DISPROVED by measurement — the 6 fact-scoped warlock entries don't cluster even at cosine 0.80 (they're distinct facets; my original 'two warlock dups' was a false alarm, never verified same-fact). But the full-ledger measurement found the REAL justification: embedding catches 10 (@0.90) to 28 (@0.87) real semantic-dup clusters that lexical jaccard completely misses — watersports/piss-kink restatements x6, 'full name Thomas Charles Lowe' x3, 'veteran in a 26yo body' x2, 'berserker mode during anal' x2, etc. (same fact, different words). Built clusterFactsEmbedding (embed once -> normalized cosine union-find; embed injectable; returns null -> caller falls back to lexical). Wired buildSweepLedger to prefer embedding (auto mode, SWEEP_EMBED_THRESHOLD 0.87 = measured sweet spot; curator stays the precision gate for borderline) with lexical fallback + --lexical override. Live: script reports 'clustering: embedding'. 5 offline tests (clusterFactsEmbedding + buildSweepLedger mode/fallback); 211 total pass. NOTE: this upgrades the SWEEP clustering. selectLedgerView (5f2 live-curator view ranking) still uses lexical — embedding ranking there is deferred as low-value since the live curator already pins the structurally-flagged collision, so view-ranking barely matters; revisit only if a live miss surfaces.

title: Confidence-gated apply + audit-log maturation (b4n apply phase)
description: Build on the confidence field now in the curator verdict + audit line. (1) APPLY GATE: when --apply is trusted, auto-apply only HIGH-confidence verdicts; route medium/low to a review lane (a separate file to eyeball) instead of mutating memory. The curator does the obvious 80%; the human only adjudicates the genuinely ambiguous. (2) AUDIT MATURATION: date-partition/rotate audit.jsonl so grep stays fast; a --summary reader that tallies verdicts/confidence ('this week: 12 EXPAND, 3 UPDATE, 1 NEGATE, 4 low-conf flagged'). (3) CALIBRATION LOOP: treat human overrides of curator verdicts as a signal — high-confidence-but-overridden = overconfidence to fix in the prompt; low-confidence clusters = the hard cases worth a prompt/consensus pass. The log becomes the dataset that tells us where to improve. Relates to b4n, 3pl (FR4 rollback/audit UI).
notes: First real apply-phase calibration data (embedding sweep on Mari, 14 merges): 11 high + 3 medium + 0 low. All 11 high = clean semantic dedup (auto-apply-safe signal). The 3 medium: M1 (watersports x4, varied framing — correct merge), M9 (Mari+Priya both-vague — harmless), M13 (PTSD specific-vs-vague — DROPPED by human review). DESIGN: mjp's gate must be TWO-STAGE — (1) domain-sensitive flags (trauma first) -> ALWAYS human, never auto-apply regardless of numeric confidence (see bd memory + the M13 rationale); (2) numeric high/low threshold for everything else. Data so far: high=clean across 11+19=30 reviewed merges; medium=mixed (2 correct, 1 correctly-dropped). No low-confidence merges emitted on clear-enough-to-propose clusters — the curator self-selects out before proposing. Tune high-auto-apply / low-route thresholds against accumulating apply-phase audit (data/reconcile-queue/sweep-audit.jsonl + audit.jsonl).
close_reason: Two-stage confidence+domain apply gate, built + tested + verified. STAGE 1 (apply-gate.ts domainFlags): domain-sensitive verdicts (tight trauma lexicon — ptsd/trauma/abuse/assault/rape/suicide/self-harm/flashback/grief, deliberately NOT war/combat/veteran/death to avoid flooding) ALWAYS hold regardless of confidence — the M13 rule, systematized. STAGE 2 (applyGate): high auto-applies, medium/low/unknown hold. Wired into BOTH apply paths gated-by-default: applySweepLedger + drainReconcileQueue (the live path has no human review, so gating-by-default is the safe posture); --ungated overrides (trust prior review). Held items -> held.jsonl review lane with reasons (never dropped). AUDIT MATURATION: scripts/reconcile-audit.mjs tallies live/sweep/held by mode/verdict/confidence ('answer your own question in 30s'). Verified: 222 tests (7 pure gate + sweep gated-hold + 3 drain gated/ungated); live summary on real logs shows the apply-phase distribution (sweep high=71 medium=20 low=2, 32 applied). Had the gate existed for the embedding sweep it would have auto-held M13 (trauma) + the 2 mediums and auto-applied the 11 high — exactly the wished-for behavior. DEFERRED (low value): audit log rotation/date-partitioning; full calibration-loop automation (the data IS captured — summary reader + held lane + audit are the inputs; human overrides are the signal).

title: FR3-live: gate the reconciliation curator into the turn path
description: Live integration of the offline curator (MarinaraExtender-5ny) into the running sidecar. Distinct shape from the offline path, hence its own scope: (1) COST GATING — run the curator only on FR1-flagged same-subject collisions (the structural detector), never on every save or a blind sweep; the create-correction path in dedup.ts is the partial FR1 seed to build the trigger on. (2) LATENCY BUDGET — the curator is an agentic loop (multiple model round-trips); it cannot block a live turn synchronously. Needs an async/deferred lane (post-turn queue or background pass) so the player never waits on it. (3) LIVE DATA, not a ledger — no dry-run/reconcile-ledger preview gate; decisions apply directly, so it needs its own audit trail (pairs with FR4/3pl) and a kill switch. (4) AUTH POSTURE — still CLI-session Agent SDK; decide whether the live sidecar may assume a logged-in CLI session, or whether live mode requires an explicit key. Reuses runCurator/applyDecision from reconcile.ts unchanged; this ticket is the trigger + scheduling + safety envelope around them.
notes: Refinements surfaced by the first live curator runs (5ny verification on Mari scenes): (1) CANDIDATE-vs-CANDIDATE pre-dedup — the curator reconciles each candidate against STORED memory only, not against sibling candidates in the same batch; two near-dup candidates from one scene each got a write-verdict (and force-create bypasses the Jaccard gate), so both would be written. Collapse candidates among themselves (consensus/dedup) BEFORE the curator, or make it batch-aware. (2) UPSTREAM durability gate, NOT curator tuning — on Hargrove the judge leaked ~14/19 candidates incl. restatements and a CONTRADICTORY scenario-frame identity; a conservative curator EXPANDs that noise rather than collapsing it -> slow ledger bloat. Fix upstream: strengthen the durability judge or add an 'is this worth storing at all' pre-check before reconciliation. DESIGN RULE (TC): do NOT make the curator more aggressive to compensate. EXPAND-conservative default is CORRECT — overwriting real canon is catastrophic+irreversible; bloat is reversible. Tuning the curator down while the upstream gate is leaky MASKS the upstream problem. Keep curator conservative; fix input quality.
close_reason: Live shadow integration shipped + verified end-to-end (commit 0fc7eb4). FR1 trigger (decide()->skip on fact lanes) enqueues collisions during play, gated by MARINARA_EXTENDER_RECONCILE (default off = unchanged); persistent queue + JSONL audit; drainReconcileQueue runs the curator OUT-OF-BAND (no Agent SDK / spend / latency in the sidecar), SHADOW by default with --apply wired. Verdict now carries confidence; audit is one structured decision per line (taskId, againstId, verdict, confidence, rationale, ts). Proven live: enqueue -> shadow drain -> real curator -> audit line with confidence:high + correct EXPAND. All four ticket concerns met (cost-gating, latency, live-data+audit+killswitch, CLI-session auth). Two follow-ups filed: bound search_entries for mature ledgers (needed before running on Mari's real ledger), and confidence-gated apply + audit maturation (the apply phase).

title: Extension (marinara-extender.js) has zero automated tests - extract pure logic
description: Audit finding #5 (structural gap, not a bug). The extension is the highest-churn, least-covered surface: pre-turn refresh, scene-recap content-pairing, CSRF/memFetch retry, version stamping, import filtering - all browser JS with no unit tests, so regressions only surface live (which is exactly how the recap-mispairing and pre-turn-skip bugs reached the user). Plan: extract the pure, side-effect-free logic into testable functions and cover them with vitest. Best first target - the scene-recap content-overlap pairing (greedy best-first assignment): pull it out of syncSceneRecaps into a pure function (scenes, returns) -> Map, and test the pairing decisions directly (correct match, sub-threshold no-match, multi-scene contention, timestamp fallback). memFetch's 403-retry and the budget-vs-lorebook-ceiling math are also good unit candidates. Pairs naturally with the 1dn/38x work since those touch the same code.

title: lorebookIdCache can go stale if the ME lorebook is manually deleted
description: Audit finding #3 (low severity). marinara-extender.js preTurnRefresh caches characterId -> lorebookId in lorebookIdCache (added for speed). Normal operation only nukes/recreates ENTRIES, keeping the lorebook container, so the cached id stays valid. But if a user deletes the entire 'Marinara Extender - <char>' lorebook in the engine UI, the cached id points at a dead lorebook and writeMemoryToLorebook writes into nothing until the tab reloads (which clears the in-memory cache) - memory silently stops injecting. Fix: invalidate lorebookIdCache[characterId] on a write/lookup failure (404 from the entries endpoint) and re-run ensureLorebook, which already does a fresh uncached lookup. Note the original ensureLorebook comment explicitly says 'no caching so deletions are handled correctly' - the pre-turn cache was layered on top, creating this inconsistency.

title: Engine drops over-budget lorebook entries silently - consider upstream report
description: The engine's per-lorebook tokenBudget (default 2048) silently drops constant entries that exceed it - no console warning, no UI hint. Cost us a 5-hour bug hunt: memory blocks grew past the budget and recall died invisibly while every link upstream was green. We guard our own lorebooks now (16384 + heal on lookup, 103d571), but any extension writing large constant entries will hit this. Candidate for a Discord report like 1kn: suggest the engine log or badge dropped entries. Low urgency for us post-fix.

title: ME_HTTP_LOG=1 crashes startup — pino-pretty transport configured but not installed
description: index.ts logger config uses transport pino-pretty when ME_HTTP_LOG=1, but pino-pretty is not in devDependencies — fastify's logger factory throws at boot and the sidecar never binds. Found 2026-06-12 while trying to enable HTTP request logging for the post-CSRF loader diagnosis. Fix: npm i -D pino-pretty, or drop the transport and use plain JSON logging for this flag. Until fixed, ME_HTTP_LOG=1 in .env makes the launcher window show a logger-factory stack and exit.
close_reason: pino-pretty installed as devDependency; verified ME_HTTP_LOG=1 boots a working server on a scratch port (health ok). Flag is OFF by default; enable in .env when raw HTTP tracing is needed.

title: Tiered cold storage for the entry index (not summarization)
description: Bound the hot index (loader scans ALL rows every turn; professor_mari ~2780 and growing) WITHOUT lossy summarization. Approach (user design): hot/cold physical index split per scope — index.yaml hot, index.cold.yaml archive; entry files stay full-fidelity, only index rows move. runPromotion demotes stale non-core entries hot->cold instead of pruning/deleting (also stops the current lossy prune + de-risks #4 backup). Loader consults cold ONLY on a recall miss; a recited cold entry rehydrates to hot (recordRecitation inverted). Note: targets the ledger ENTRY index the loader reads (companion entries), not the separate beats store. See bd memory cold-storage-not-summarization. Open knob: cold-miss trigger (see issue notes).
close_reason: Done + tested. Tiered cold storage: stale non-core entries archive hot->cold (index.cold.yaml) instead of being pruned/deleted; loader does a cold scan only on a relevance miss and rehydrates the best match; recitation also rehydrates. Bounds the hot scan without summarization loss, and stops the lossy prune (de-risks backup). 90 tests, tsc clean.

title: Auto-start sidecar on boot (optional)
description: Now that the loader depends on the sidecar, if the console isn't running the extension silently vanishes. Offer an opt-in Windows startup registration (Task Scheduler or Startup shortcut) so 'always works' doesn't require remembering to launch a console.
close_reason: Done. [A] toggle in start.ps1 console writes/removes a Startup-folder launcher (Marinara Extender.cmd) that relaunches start.ps1 minimized at login; banner shows ON/off; opt-in + user-removable. Launcher string verified well-formed; ps parses clean.

title: .env.example committed template
description: A fresh clone has no .env and no template (real .env is gitignored). Add memory-extender/.env.example with all vars commented (pure defaults when copied), API key line empty, no secrets. Confirm not caught by *.env ignore. README points to it.
close_reason: Shipped + verified. start.ps1 builds + runs prod (dev fallback) and preflights Node 20+; loader shows an on-page offline banner; .env.example committed. Prod build runs (health 200), loader valid JS, tsc clean, 84 tests, ps parses.

title: v1.1: support any OpenAI-compatible local provider (not just Ollama)
description: The chat/analysis path already talks the OpenAI protocol (MARINARA_EXTENDER_LOCAL_URL points at an OpenAI-compatible /v1 base). v1.1: make 'any local provider via OpenAI protocol' a first-class, documented story — LM Studio, llama.cpp server, vLLM, text-generation-webui, KoboldCpp, etc. Work: (1) generalize the Ollama-specific bits — the /api/health check pings the Ollama root, and chunker embeddings use Ollama's native /api/embeddings; make these provider-agnostic or clearly optional. (2) document per-provider base URLs + a 'bring your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint' section. (3) test the sentiment JSON path across a couple of providers. Defer until v1.0 install pipeline is done.
notes: Bumped P4→P3: real community request (a KoboldCpp user asked 'does Ollama being a prereq mean I can't use this?'). FINDING: the CORE already supports any OpenAI-compatible local provider — all analysis calls hit /chat/completions and embeddings hit /v1/embeddings against MARINARA_EXTENDER_LOCAL_URL (llm-config.ts DEFAULT_LOCAL_URL is just Ollama's OpenAI endpoint). So Kobold/LM Studio/llama.cpp work TODAY via .env. Remaining is ONBOARDING, not capability: (1) launcher (start.ps1) is Ollama-only (detect/start/pull/install); (2) messaging + .env said 'Ollama' — .env.example now reworded (this commit) to spell out KoboldCpp/LM Studio/llama.cpp + ports; (3) embed status check uses Ollama /api/tags. Folded into szf Phase 2 (docs + 'bring-your-own-backend' launcher tolerance) and overlaps nqy (easy endpoint config UI).

title: True group-chat per-speaker routing (plumb Marinara per-message speaker)
description: Chat-import per-speaker routing (P4) works for speakers the chunker detects: inline 'Name:' prefixes + narration. It does NOT yet handle TRUE group chats where each message is a separate row from a distinct character and the speaker lives only in Marinara's message metadata (fetchChatMessages currently keeps only {role, content}). To finish: (1) verify Marinara's per-message speaker field for group chats (characterId/name/author/etc.), (2) extension fetchChatMessages prefixes assistant content with 'Name: ' when discoverable (chunker already parses that), or pass a speaker field, (3) verify routing splits a real group chat per character. Needs the real Marinara group-chat message schema — do not guess-ship field names into the import path. Also: clean re-import (removeEntriesBySourceChat) only clears the primary character's entries; orphan-routed companions on OTHER characters aren't cleared on re-import (dedup + deterministic beat ids cover re-runs, but note it).
close_reason: Implemented same turn it was filed: Marinara stores per-message characterId (confirmed from chats.storage.ts); DigestMessage.speaker + parseTurns honor it; extension maps characterId->name and sets speaker. Unit-tested (parseTurns honors speaker, robust to periods/accents). End-to-end vs a real Marinara group chat is in-browser-only to confirm.

title: Re-evaluate RP time-sense post-v1.0 (multi-model behavior)
description: Time-sense (soft-clock narrative time + presence + no-nag guidance) is gated OFF via MARINARA_EXTENDER_TIMESENSE for v1.0 — worked under Claude 4.6, unreliable under 4.7. Re-evaluate after v1.0: (1) characterize 4.7's raw default time/break-nagging behavior with the feature OFF; (2) test the feature ON across models (4.6, 4.7, others) to see where it helps vs. goes wacky; (3) gather user feedback; (4) decide whether to re-enable by default, keep opt-in, or rework the prompt steering. All logic is intact behind the flag — no rebuild needed to test, just flip the env var. See commit gating it.

title: FR4: supersedes audit trail + rollback UI
description: Tooling on top of the FR2 supersedes link: surface a fact's supersession history in the ledger UI and allow rollback when the LLM (FR3) or structural rule (FR1) got it wrong — restore a superseded fact to active, re-superseding its replacement. The link/data model already exists from FR2; this is the human-in-the-loop affordance. Depends on FR2 (and pairs with FR3).
notes: CODE COMPLETE, awaiting manual UI verification (not closing — the rule: UI is verified only by the user clicking in a running browser). Backend done + verified on real data: restoreSupersededEntry (storage), factHistory/listRetired/rollback (rollback.ts, undo+flip), GET /api/retired + POST /api/rollback (characterId->identityKey, character scope), 7 offline tests; listRetired(professor_mari) returns 44 real retired facts. UI: collapsible 'Retired (character memory)' section in the panel memory tab (renderRetiredSection in marinara-extender.js) with Restore=undo / Restore-as-canonical=flip, lazy-load, reused CSS. TO VERIFY + CLOSE: (1) restart the sidecar so the new endpoints go live; (2) open the panel -> memory tab -> expand 'Retired'; (3) confirm the 44 facts list with their replacements; (4) Restore one (undo -> both active) and one with --flip (replacement retired); confirm via re-expand. Committed; pushed.

title: FR3: LLM reconciliation pass — adjudicate fact collisions
description: The expensive correct layer for subtle cases. GATED: runs ONLY on FR1-flagged same-subject candidates (not every save, not a blind periodic sweep) so cost stays rare. Prompt: given an incoming fact and the existing same-subject fact(s), decide UPDATE (supersede), EXPAND (both true, keep both), DISTINCT (false collision, keep both), or NEGATE (incoming disproves existing -> mark existing superseded as a negative fact). Routes Ollama-local -> external fallback like the rest. Depends on FR2.
close_reason: Fulfilled by MarinaraExtender-5ny for the OFFLINE path: the curator adjudicates UPDATE/EXPAND/DISTINCT/NEGATE/CREATE/DUPLICATE against same-subject ledger entries and applies via the FR2 supersede primitive. Implemented as a Claude Agent SDK tool loop (not the single Ollama->external prompt originally scoped) on CLI-session auth, ledger-gated (preview==apply). The LIVE FR1-gated turn-path integration is split out to its own ticket (different shape: cost gating, latency budget, live data vs ledger).

title: P4: collision detection, auto-suggest aliases, group-chat verify
description: Polish/edge cases. Collision: same label maps to multiple characters -> detect at alias-add, user picks owner or marks ambiguous (per-beat manual). Auto-suggest: new chat introduces 'Dr. Chandrasekaran' when 'Chandrasekaran' already maps to a char but the longer form doesn't -> prompt to add alias. title: Decide: should mere exposure (retrievalCount on load) still drive promotion?
description: computeScore = retrievalCount + recitationCount*3. retrievalCount still increments on every LOAD, so an entry that merely surfaces a lot can promote to core without ever being demonstrably used. lastRetrievedAt is now use-only (honest), but score still rewards exposure. Decision needed: de-weight or drop retrievalCount from computeScore (promotion = proven use), weighed against recitation detection's blind spot (it misses paraphrased use, so pure-recitation promotion could under-credit genuinely-useful-but-not-echoed entries). Deferred for a deliberate call.
close_reason: Resolved: exposure credit is now relevance-gated in loader.ts selectEntries — retrievalCount increments only when an entry is SUMMONED (relevanceScore > 0.1), not when it merely rides in on the recency fallback. So mere exposure no longer drives promotion; relevance-driven exposure does, which becomes a more honest proxy for use as the Current cache improves. computeScore (retrievalCount + recitationCount*3) kept as-is. See commit.

title: In-memory index read-cache (read-only; preserve atomic write-through)
description: From the Comparision_2 review (shortcoming 2.1 supplement, partial). At large entry counts the hot index.yaml grows and is re-read+parsed from disk every turn (loader has no persistent cross-turn cache). Proposal: an in-memory READ cache of the per-scope hot index, invalidated on write. IMPORTANT: READ half ONLY. Do NOT adopt the source docs async-write-queue-every-30s idea: it conflicts with the existing atomic-write durability (storage.ts temp+fsync+rename, per-path serialized, for crash/power-loss safety) and risks losing up to 30s of memory on a crash. Writes stay write-through. Also: the source doc overstates the I/O problem (claimed thousands-of-files per turn; actually the hot/cold + index/entry split already bound per-turn I/O to one index + a handful of selected entries). Low priority unless a real large-dataset benchmark shows index-parse latency. Source: docs/Comparision_2_review.md Slice 3.

title: [task] Measure pre-turn budget headroom — how much of PRE_TURN_BUDGET_MS we actually use
description:
We block generation up to PRE_TURN_BUDGET_MS (800ms, marinara-extender.js) for preTurnRefresh, but we have no measurement of how much of that lead time we actually consume — so we can't tell if we're comfortable or at the edge. This matters more now: 38x (dual-retrieval) turned pre-turn from ONE sidecar call into N (one per participant, each including the Stage-2 recap embedding) + N lorebook writes. We told the user 'always-on, add a toggle if the bite is too big' — this is the instrument that tells us whether/when that's needed, instead of guessing.

WHAT: instrument preTurnRefresh to report lead-time usage:
- total elapsed from start to when the awaited refreshes settle (or the budget timeout fires);
- whether the budget timeout fired and how many participants were still pending (stragglers that lagged to next turn);
- ideally per-participant timing (which character's refresh is slow — pre-turn call vs lorebook write) and participant count.
Console log at minimum (e.g. '[ME] pre-turn: 540/800ms, 3/3 participants, 0 stragglers'); optionally surface a rolling stat in the panel Settings or /api/health so it's visible without console-diving.

WHY P4: no pain observed yet; this is pre-emptive observability. ESCALATE earlier if multi-character scenes feel laggy, prompts balloon, or we're deciding on the dual-retrieval toggle (38x) and want data first. Relates to 38x.

title: serializedWrite keyed by raw path string - case-insensitive FS edge
description: Audit finding #4 (theoretical/very low severity). storage.ts serializedWrite serializes per filePath using a Map keyed by the raw string. On case-insensitive filesystems (Windows, default macOS), two different-cased path strings for the same physical file ('Foo.yaml' vs 'foo.yaml') would hash to different keys and NOT serialize, allowing a concurrent read-modify-write race that could corrupt YAML. Mitigated in practice because all paths come from the same path-building helpers (entryPath/indexPath/etc.) which emit consistent strings, so divergent casing should never occur. Fix if we ever want belt-and-suspenders: normalize the lock key (e.g. path.resolve + toLowerCase on win32) before Map lookup. Filing for awareness; not currently reachable.
